items.description: Coding and decoding tables for use of a late-18th-century "cabinet noir" or "Black Chamber," the secret cipher departments of the European courts of the early modern age. Content and provenance link this specimen with the Bavarian Electoran court.

items.title: Agustin V. Zamorano letter : Santa Barbara, Calif., to the alcaldes of Santa Barbara, Monterrey, and San José Guadalupe, 1832 May 9
items.description: Zamorano's letter to the alcaldes of Santa Barbara, Monterey, and San José Guadalupe, requesting that they publish the attached manifesto informing the public of Zamorano's journey to Santa Barbara and his efforts to preserve peace in California.

items.title: Jose Maria Estudillo manuscript document
items.description: Manuscript document dated Monterey, California, August 9, 1824 (per T. S.) (Thomas Streeter?). Signed by Jose Maria Estudillo. Jose was the founder of the Estudillo family in upper California.

items.title: Letter and administrative file concerning storm-related damage to the Presidio of San Francisco and proposals for its repair : ALS and ADS, 1805-1807
items.description: Leatherbound folio containing a letter from Josef de Iturrigaray, Viceroy of New Spain, to His Excellency Don José Antonio Cavallero, explaining an enclosed document containing testimony compiled by José de Arrillaga, governor of the Californias, describing damage to the Presidio caused by a storm in Dec. 1798-Jan.…

items.title: Letter, 1832 Aug. 14, to the Alcade of San J'ose de Guadelupe
items.description: Statesman, soldier, craftsman, and California's first printer.

items.description: Handwritten letter addressed to H. French, Esq. introducing Mr. Charles Bernhardt as the agent for Santa Clara Co. regarding the sale of Roi du Savons soap and signed by Withington Williams. Verso of letterhead includes advertising inserts for Sacramento businesses.

items.title: Eloesser-Heynemann Co. records, 1860-1972
items.description: The origins of Eloesser-Heymann Co. dates back to 1851 when Leonard D. Heynemann, an immigrant from Hamburg, realized there was a future in providing supplies to the miners who flocked to San Francisco and Sacramento as part of the California Gold Rush.

items.title: Visite de Msr le Duc d'Aumale a la Croix-Rousse, dans l'atelier de M. Carquillat : le 24 Août 1841
items.description: Picture shows the Duc d'Aumale full length and facing right, accompanied by four members of his entourage; to his right, Carquillat, also full length but facing slightly left, holds his well-known portrait of Joseph Marie Jacquard.

items.title: Chinese Railroad Workers
items.description: The Chinese Railroad Workers Digital Materials Repository offers open access to materials that are selected for their qualities that they are difficult to retrieve, and rich for historical study. All individual items are curated with descriptions that highlight revelatory details.

items.title: Journal of the clipper ship Red Gauntlet, 1855-1856
items.description: Journal kept by ship's carpenter William F. Harden documenting the second voyage of the clipper ship Red Gauntlet under Captain Andrews, departing New York for San Francisco, Hawaii, and Canton on August 18, 1855.

items.title: Alfred Robinson papers, 1837-1859
items.description: Originally from Mass., Robinson first went to Calif. in 1829 as the representative for the hide-trading and shipping firm Bryant, Sturgis & Co. He married an heiress of Santa Barbara's de la Guerra family Primarily business correspondence to and from Robinson, in his role as a San Francisco merchant and as agent for…

items.title: Jacob P. Leese papers
items.description: Early California merchant Jacob Primer Leese was born in St. Clairsville, Ohio, in 1809, and came to California in 1833 and again in 1834, engaging in trade in Los Angeles and later in Monterey.

items.title: Letter from C. Curry Guns and Fancy Goods to Hardy & Kennedy regarding pistol order and firearms inventory, 1860 September 27.
items.description: Letter from Charles and Nathaniel Curry of C. Curry Guns and Fancy Goods, San Francisco, to William S. Hardy and Samuel S. Kennedy of Hardy & Kennedy Co., Forest Hill mining district, regarding an order of three pairs of large pistols with Damascus barrels and holsters.

items.title: William A. Leidesdorff collection, 1834-1857, 1928
items.description: William Alexander Leidesdorff was born in 1810 in the Danish West Indies. His father, Alexander Leidesdorff, was a Dane, and his mother, Anna Maria Spark, was a creole of mixed-race ancestry. Leidesdorff's correspondence (1845-1847) as vice-consul.

items.title: William D.M. Howard papers, 1823-1878
items.description: Howard was a merchant and financier in San Francisco, California. Correspondence, invoices, and receipts from pioneer Calif. residents, merchants, and companies, reflecting Howard's extensive commercial activities through his firm, Mellus & Howard Company, including letters to and from business partner Henry…

items.title: Leland Stanford letter to Butler Ives
items.description: At the time of the letter, Butler Ives was an assistant engineer with the Central Pacific Railroad.

items.title: Lewis Tasheira's history : typescript copy, 1920 Dec. 13.
items.description: Mention of various railroad men and companies. Worked with Henry Root in Oakland, later C.P. Huntington and Leland Stanford in California and elsewhere. Covers the period 1864-1903.

items.title: Notes about Henry Root and the California Central Railway, nd
items.description: Notes from Root's book, "Personal History and Reminiscences, 1845 to 1921." Also notes from the DAILY ALTA CALIFORNIA, 1860-1863.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 4, Accounting Department records, 1862-1988
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. It was the first railroad to connect Los Angeles to the rest of California and its lines extended as far as New Orleans.

items.title: William C. Ralston Correspondence, ca. 1870-1890
items.description: William Chapman Ralston, born 12 June 1826 in Ohio, was a banker and steamship owner. In 1864 he helped organize the Bank of California and served as its first president. He died 27 August 1875.

items.title: Incoming correspondence, 1863-1864
items.description: Bulk of the letters are requests for purchasing the Fowler adding machine and the circulars advertising the product. Several letters are responses to the company's advertisement seeking agents throughout the United States to sell the machines.

items.title: Parke & Lacy business records, circa 1870-1901
items.description: 1 business ledger (labeled "day book," 7 original photographs, and related business documents).

items.title: Towne and Bacon Printers records, 1854-1875
items.description: Two major archival repositories, plus ten unpublished manuscripts were used in researching this dissertation. Very often the publications produced by James Towne were themselves sources of historical information. These are included in the following section devoted to Secondary Sources.

items.title: New Almaden Mine records, 1845-1973
items.description: In 1845, Captain Andres Castillero of the Mexican Army was sent on a routine scouting patrol through what is now northern California, then part of Mexican territory. As an amateur geologist, Castillero recognized the possibility that the rolling hills held vast mineral deposits.

items.title: Reports on California mines : ms, 1860-1865
items.description: Reports and letters giving overviews of mines either purchased by or of interest to the firm of Adelberg & Raymond. Includes gold, silver, iron, quicksilver, and tin mines.

items.title: Stock certificate, 1869 August 21.
items.description: Stock certificate issued to C.G. Myrick for ten shares in the capital stock of the mining company. Issued at Mayfield, Santa Clara County, by Wm. Paul, president. The mine location is White Pine District, Nevada.

items.title: Telegraphic mining code, c. 1860
items.description: Birdseye Creek was one of California's earliest hydraulic mining companies to use thir private telegraphic codes. Mines owned by this company include among others Star of the West, Red Dog, and Uncle Sam.

items.description: Two documents (1864 and 1867) concern ownership of the Sanchez de Pacheco land grant, Rancho San Miguel. The earlier is a transfer from Francisco Soto to his brother-in-law, Lasario Galindo, of land deeded by Soto's grandmother, Juana Pacheco.

items.title: Map of the Santa Clara City Homestead Association
items.description: Shows owners, Quito Ranch line, proposed railroad from Alviso to Saratoga, Lawrence and Santa Clara depots, etc. Oriented with north toward lower left.. In: Map, prospectus, articles of association and certificate of incorporation of the Santa Clara City Homestead Association ... 1869.

items.title: Mesa land case papers, 1853-1930
items.description: Copies of transcript of proceedings in case No. 238, Maria Antonia Mesa, claimant vs. The United States, defendent for the place named "Rinconada del Arroyo de San Francisquito," 1853 and 1861; and notes on Ranchos of Santa Clara, Santa Cruz and San Benito Counties from Capt.

items.title: Records of Stanford properties, 1861-1927
items.description: Deeds and other legal documents relating to properties owned by Leland and Jane Stanford and, later, by Stanford University in Butte, Tehama, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Yolo, Monterey, Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Los Angeles, Marin, Napa, Sacramento, San Francisco and San Luis Obispo counties, California.

items.title: Santa Clara County (Calif.) land grant plats, 1851, 1856, and 1863
items.description: San Jose, California. The corner of Market Street and San Fernando Street in San Jose, with the division of the Mesa family land into six parcels, surrounded by Antonio Sunol and Brown & Co. land. Also shown is an "acequia" which runs along one side of the properties.

items.title: City of San Jose / copied from the original map drawn by Pherman [i.e. Sherman] Day, civil engineer, 1850 : facsimile map.
Pulgas base : map, 1854
items.description: Shows coastal outline, hills, roads, vegetation, and settlement locations of Jones, Steinbergen, and Carr in the vicinity of Palo Alto. Includes a profile of the base line (length 6.53 miles) and a sketch showing the location of the base line in relation to the southern half of San Francisco Bay.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: Alfred A. Hart photographs, 1862-1869
items.description: Alfred A. Hart, born in Norwich, Connecticut on March 16, 1816, was the principal photographer for the Central Pacific Railroad during the construction of the Overland Route. He photographed the construction from 1865 to 1869 when the last spike was driven by Leland Stanford at Promontory, Utah on May 10, 1869.

items.title: E. G. Greenfield account book for wharfages collected from steamers, vessels, etc., and diary : Stockton, Calif., 1855-1861
items.description: Account book (1855 May 16-1856 May 12) and diary (1858 Jan. 1-1859 Nov. 12) kept by harbor master Elijah G. Greenfield recording wharfages collected from ships and daily events in Stockton, Calif.

items.title: Keepsakes issued to members of the Book Club of California in commemoration of the centennial of the transcontinental railroad, 1969
items.description: Includes 1. "The Hewes Receipt," by Ralph W. Hansen; and 2. "The 'Goat Island Grab'," by Ted Wurm (2 copies).

items.title: Railroad timetables and other printed ephemera, 1838-1946
items.description: Includes timetables for the New England states (The Pathfinder Railway Guide, (1849-1854 & 1896), the west coast.

items.title: The Southern Pacific Railroad Company, plaintiff, vs. Calvin Martin et als, defendants : petition for the condemnation of lands to public use, 1868
items.description: Defendants include ca. 140 names, many of which are from early Santa Clara County families.

items.title: To the Honorable the Legislature of the State of California : the citizens of the City of San Francisco, in view of the great commercial interests so necessarily... Pilotage
items.description: A petition to the California state legislature from San Francisco citizens, calling on the government to reform the official pilotage system.

items.title: Manuscript letter copy book from Department of the Interior, General Land Office regarding claims of Central Pacific Railroad land, mineral title issues, conflicts, etc. for the Placer County, California region from the estate of W & P Nicholls, bankers, at Dutch Flat, 1862-1869
items.description: Based on the contents, the letters are primarily concerned with conflicting claims to land between the Central Pacific Railroad and American settlers in California. Many of the letters involve Joseph S. Wilson in his role as the General Land Commissioner.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Journal of a schoolteacher
items.description: The journal begins with Wells' journey on foot, probably from somewhere near Murphy's Camp, to Jackson, then by stage to Sacramento where he takes up a post as assistant teacher at the Sacramento Seminary, a Methodist school run by trustees and supported by the parish and tuition fees.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: George T. Clark papers, 1862-1935
items.description: Clark was Stanford University Librarian, 1907-1928 (emeritus 1928 until his death in 1940) and co-founder and first president of the California Library Association.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Carleton E. Watkins photograph collection
items.description: Carleton E. Watkins was a 19th century photographer based in San Francisco who made his name documenting the rapid growth of the American West. His photographs of the Yosemite Valley, in Mariposa County, California, are said to have influenced Abraham Lincoln's 1864 Yosemite Land Grant, the first act of Congress to…

items.title: Isaiah West Taber photograph collection
items.description: Isaiah West Taber (1830-1912) was an American daguerreotypist, ambrotypist, and photographer. He worked for photographers Bradley and Rulofson in San Franciso from 1864 before opening his own studio, the "Taber Gallery," at No. 12 Montgomery Street in 1871. He became well-known for portraiture and views of California.

items.title: William Hubert Burgess letters and miscellany, 1851-1899
items.description: Burgess was an artist, silversmith, miner, and teacher. He and his family were originally from England, then settled in Boston and New York. He arrived in Calif. in 1850, sailing via Cape Horn, aboard the ship Byron. Consists of 13 letters and some incomplete letters to Burgess's mother in England.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Samuel Charles Bugbee papers, 1861-1876
items.description: Architect Samuel Charles Bugbee helped plan the Stanford family home in Palo Alto, and perhaps also contributed to the San Francisco Conservatory of Flowers in the late 19th century. This collection consists of three sketchbooks and loose drawings on onion skin paper.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: a Roy Page Ballard papers 1894
items.description: Graduate of Stanford University in history (A.B. May 1897). Notes and outlines for a history of the Stanford campus area originally prepared for a class assignment.

items.title: A Woodside reminiscence: as told by Grizzly Ryder
items.description: "A Woodside Reminiscence: as told by Grizzly Ryder," by Cutler L. Bonestell, is a recounting of a 1914 conversation between Cutler L. Bonestell and Grizzly Ryder on how he survived an attack by a grizzly bear near what is now called Bear Creek, near Woodside, CA.

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. The individuals and families represented include: pioneers and settlers; professionals, including teachers, doctors, scientists, lawyers and judges; bankers and merchants.

items.title: California history : scrapbook and miscellaneous pamphlets, 1857-1955
items.description: The scrapbook consists primarily of clippings about Santa Clara County history, as well as Monterey, Stanford, and Yosemite. There are also two poems by John E. Richards (pp. 123 & 146).

items.title: California. Legal documents, 1858-1892
items.description: Colusa County. Check for $25. to J.B. Stanton for services to school, 1858. Commissary General of Subsistence. Letter to Lieutenant J.C. Morrill of Fort Ruby, Nevada City, Calif., 1863. Shasta County. Election roll list for American Ranch, 1869. (Gives name, age, occupation, state or country of origin) Alameda County.

items.title: Californian and Western manuscripts collection, ca. 1760-1963
items.description: Small collections and miscellaneous single items pertaining to various periods, persons, and phases of California history (1760-1963). Includes letters, journals, diaries, reports, financial and legal documents, pictures and maps, some typescripts and photostats.

items.title: Carleton Watkins stereoview and cabinet photographs
items.description: Photographs by or published by Carleton Watkins. All but one are views of California. Photographs by or published by Carleton E. Watkins in the form of cabinet cards or stereographs.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photographs, ca. 1870-1890
items.description: 1. Vertical steam pumps, stereo, nd. (JL006) 2. 15 stereos from "Pacific Coast Series," including Pigeon Point, New Years Island, Pescadero's Pebble Beach, and Pescadero (M237). 3. 1 stereo San Francisco City Hall cornerstone laying, 1872. Also includes a stereo by Thomas Houseworth of White Sulphur Springs, nd. 4.

items.title: Juana Briones collection, circa 1960-2009
items.description: Juana Briones (1802-1899) was a businesswoman and landowner in the San Francisco Bay Area.

items.title: Northern California newspaper clippings : mounted in one large album, 1854
items.description: Handwritten notes annotate the text on many pages.

items.title: Pacific Slope scrapbooks, 1819-1906
items.description: The first series of scrapbooks was created by mayor (and later governor) Washington Bartlett, containing articles pertaining to political and civic issues in San Francisco and California from 1855 to 1886, as well as some notes and memoranda chronicling his duties as mayor.

items.title: Paul Percy Parker collection of historical documents pertaining to Monterey County, California, 1782-1936
items.description: Paul Percy Parker was a newspaperman in California'a Salinas Valley. Correspondence, manuscripts of narratives and memoirs, official documents, and clippings dealing predominantly with the Monterey and Salinas Valley areas before 1900.

items.title: Reid W. Dennis collection of California lithographs, 1850-1908
items.description: This collection of prints, mostly lithographs (including chromolithographs and colored lithographs), as well as one engraving, primarily portray San Francisco city views, public buildings, and landscapes.

items.title: William Wesley Boak pocket letter book to his wife Samantha
items.description: Thirty-seven page autograph signed filled-in Gregory's Express Pocket Letter Book, written by an Iowan gold seeker in California to his wife with an interesting detailed description of the mild climate and successful farming in the Santa Clara Valley, preceding its development as the world's leading fruit growing…

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Andrew Smith Hallidie diary : ms, 1852 Jan.-May.
items.description: Diary of Hallidie's voyage with his father from Liverpool to San Francisco via New York and Panama aboard the ships Pacific, Brother Jonathan, and Brutus. Discusses everyday life aboard as well as engineering aspects of the ships, including propulsion equipment and functional problems during a storm.

items.title: California letters, 1852-1858
items.description: Collection consists of letters from A. S. Gibbons and his wife, Sarah Cloud Gibbons, to her family in Virginia (1852-1857). A. S. Gibbons was an itinerant Methodist preacher who spent one year teaching at Santa Clara College. The letters describe domestic problems and the temperance movement.

items.title: Chester Smith Lyman journals, 1845-1854
items.description: Consists of 14 journals kept by Chester Smith Lyman documenting his voyages from New York to Hawaii (1845-1846), from Hawaii to San Francisco (1847), and from San Francisco to Connecticut (1850), as well as his observations and experiences in Hawaii and California between the years 1846 and 1850.

items.title: Culver family papers, 1858-1915
items.description: John Oscar Culver, born May 2, 1830, was one of ten children born to tailor James Culver and Kezia [Lee] Culver of Sandy Hill, New York (now Hudson's Falls). James Culver's grandfather, resident in New York and Connecticut, had fought for the Colonies in the Revolutionary War.

items.title: Daingerfield family letters, 1850-1853
items.description: Leroy Daingerfield and his brother William Daingerfield were early residents of northern California. Leroy was a miner and rancher and William was a lawyer and businessman.

items.title: Daniel Jagger diary : ms, 1846-1860
items.description: Leatherbound diary, primarily documenting Jagger's overland journey with other members of his gold mining company from Warren, Ohio to Georgetown, El Dorado, County, Calif., Apr. 1849-Jan. 1850.

items.title: Diario borrador : Notebook of accounts and special events, 1860-1890
items.description: Cover page states "Tepic, Cal.," but inside on the first and second pages, and on several other pages states "Hacienda de Nueva Almaden;" there are also numerous references to San Jose and Santa Clara.

items.title: Diary, March-April 1851
items.description: Littlefield writes about his experiences in California, giving details of selling lumber, traveling from Benicia to San Francisco by steamer, staying at the Temperance House, and telling of the many ships and their cargoes that he observes on San Francisco Bay.

items.title: Frank Shay, "A lifetime in California, 1860-1939" typescript
items.description: California reporter and attorney. Growing up in California, Shay served in a wide variety of positions throughout his life, including special reporter for Sacramento and Virginia City newspapers, accountant and telegrapher for the Sutro Tunnel Company, and, after completing his law degree at Hastings Law College…

items.title: H.S. Bradley ship's log : ms copy, 1849 Nov. 13-1850 May 7
items.description: Handwritten copy of a ship's log kept by Bradley, a passenger on the bark Orion, on a voyage from Boston to San Francisco via Rio de Janeiro and the island of Juan Fernandez. Entries record the weather, the ship's course and location, ships spoken, and significant shipboard events.

items.title: Harwood family papers, 1722-1962
items.description: Over his lifetime, Andrew Allen Harwood (1802-1884), great grandson of Benjamin Franklin, kept letters and notes of interest and autographs in a collection known as ODDS & ENDS. He willed it to his grandson, Thomas Triplett Hunter Harwood.

items.title: Hosmer correspondence, 1849-1853
items.description: Charles and Edward Hosmer left their parents, brothers and sisters in Avon, New York in March 1849 for California, arriving in September 1849. Edward travelled around Cape Horn by boat while Charles went overland by wagon train.

items.title: Joseph G. Eastland diary and letters : ms and ALS, 1846-1853
items.description: The entries in Joseph Eastman's diary, dated May 1846 to May 1849, begin when Eastland was a 14-year-old from his home in Nashville, Tenn. and New Orleans, La. The diary continues through the Mexican War, in which Joseph Eastland apparently served as a young man.

items.title: Leland Stanford papers, 1840-1909
items.description: Leland Stanford was born March 9, 1824 in Watervliet Township, New York. He was admitted to the practice of law in 1848 and married Jane Lathrop in 1850. In 1852, Stanford moved to California where he first worked as a storekeeper in Mother Lode mining camps and later became a successful Sacramento businessman.

items.title: Leland Stanford photograph album, 1868-1882
items.description: Images in the album are largely of Leland Stanford Jr., from the age of 3 months to 14 years; others include one image of Leland Jr. with Jane Stanford, which has been hand colored, and several images of Leland Stanford Sr. In addition there is one image of Wilsie [Wilson] Taylor, a friend of Leland Jr.

items.title: Letters (photocopies) to family, 1866
items.description: 3 letters were mailed from Green Oaks and describe episodes of her life on the Steele brothers' dairy; one was mailed from Aspinwall, the Atlantic port of Panama, before crossing by train to the Pacific.

items.title: Log of the extreme clipper ship Spitfire, 1854-1855
items.description: Manuscript logbook documenting the second voyage of the extreme clipper ship Spitfire under Captain John W. Arey, comprising approximately 9,000 words of daily entries. The voyage departed Boston in November 1854, arriving at San Francisco on March 21, 1855, after a passage of 118 days.

items.title: Logbook for the steamship Panama : ms, 1849 Feb. 18-May 6
items.description: Daily record of the ship's voyage from New York to Panama via the Straits of Magellan, under the command of Lt. David D. Porter, U.S. Navy. Includes information on the course, wind, hours, temperature, and other technical measurements, and occasional repairs to the engine.

items.title: Moses Schallenberger papers, 1847-1898
items.description: Moses Schallenberger was an early California pioneer. Correspondence and photographs (1847-1898) covering the period after the arrival of Schallenberger in California. Also included is an account, recorded by Mary Sheldon Barnes, of Schallenberger's overland journey to California from Missouri in 1844.

items.title: Richard J. Bush journal of the Collins Overland Telegraph expedition
items.description: An original unpublished manuscript journal of Collin's telegraph expedition departing San Francisco, CA on July 3, 1865 to Nikolayefsk-on-Amur, Russia.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Mission Santa Clara marriage records, 1846-1847
items.description: Undated manuscript translation of a portion of the Mission Santa Clara marriage register, beginning with record number 2873 (1846 Jan. 3) and ending with record number 3003 (1847 Dec. 11).

items.title: Record-Book. Rules, By-Laws & Proceedings of the Santa Cruz Cornet Band
items.description: A 43 page hand-written record book in a contemporary notebook. Includes minutes of the meetings from 1869 up to 1871. The organization reorganized June 7th, 1869.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: Calvin Brown letter to James T. Ames on Mare Island Navy Yard, 1861 May 30
items.description: Letter from U.S. Navy civil engineer Calvin Brown to arms manufacturer James T. Ames describing Brown's first impressions of the Mare Island Navy Yard, then under construction. Brown discusses the yard's buildings, equipment, machinery, and labor force.

items.title: Edward Otho Cresap Ord letters, 1854-1885
items.description: Letters written by Ord to his wife during the period when Ord was on a survey of the Pacific Coast, including descriptions of the region, details of incidents and problems relating to the survey, Indian campaigns, and other matters relating to the West Coast.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: San Francisco town journal : ms, 1847-1848
items.description: First financial record of San Francisco, kept by the elected treasurer, William A. Leidesdorff. The journal contains eleven pages of entries, recording cash received and expended, and expenditures for goods and services, including payments made for the salary of Alcalde George Hyde, the first survey of San Francisco…

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Advertising and marketing

items.title: Crate, can, and bottle label collection, circa 1920s-1940s
items.description: Comprises crate, can, and bottle labels, the bulk of which were designed and created between the 1920s and 1940s by San Francisco and Los Angeles lithography companies.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Electronics industry (national and international)

items.title: Billy Malone, "The Early History of the Magnavox Company"
items.description: One of the founders of the Magnavox Company was Edwin S. Pridham, who graduated from Stanford University in May 1909 with an a.b. in physics. Prior to the founding of Magnavox in March 1911, Pridham worked with Cyril Elwell, a 1907 Stanford graduate, on his wireless radio transmitter in Palo Alto.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Capital Soap Company, manufacturers of chemical, olive, family, toilet and bleaching soaps : also the famous Le Roi du Savons Soap, which washes without rubbing. : letter, 1863 October 5.
items.description: Handwritten letter addressed to H. French, Esq. introducing Mr. Charles Bernhardt as the agent for Santa Clara Co. regarding the sale of Roi du Savons soap and signed by Withington Williams. Verso of letterhead includes advertising inserts for Sacramento businesses.

items.title: Cours de theorie pour le tissage professée par P. Audibert [two students' course books]
items.description: Two students' manuscript notebooks documenting the use of Jacquard's punched card silk weaving method in 1884 and 1885. The volumes contain a total of eight (8) punched cards tipped in at end as well as numerous drawings of punched cards throughout the text.

items.title: Eloesser-Heynemann Co. records, 1860-1972
items.description: The origins of Eloesser-Heymann Co. dates back to 1851 when Leonard D. Heynemann, an immigrant from Hamburg, realized there was a future in providing supplies to the miners who flocked to San Francisco and Sacramento as part of the California Gold Rush.

items.title: Framed portraits of Christian De Guigne (color photograph by Mushet Photography, Los Angeles, n.d.) and John Stauffer (oil painting by unknown artist, n.d.)
items.description: These portraits hung in the Stauffer Chemical Company San Francisco offices until their closure in 1987.

items.title: French Jacquard loom programming manual with textile samples, circa late 19th century
items.description: French manuscript documenting Jacquard loom programming methods and textile production, containing 94 textile samples with corresponding loom programming instructions and machine patterns.

items.title: Gladding, McBean and Company account book
items.description: Gladding, McBean and Company is a California firm that manufactures clay roofing tiles. Photocopy of contract book with brief entries on building, location, owner, architect, material, and amount; included are entries pertaining to buildings on the Stanford University campus.

items.title: Joshua Hendy Machine Works Articles of Incorporation and minutes of the proceedings of the board of directors : ledger, 1882-1909
Les laboureurs: poème tiré de Jocelyn. Reproduit en caractères tissés avec license des propriétaires éditeurs
items.description: This is the first book woven entirely in silk using programmable punch cards (Jacquard loom method). This book was created by an automated programmable machine, with hundreds of thousands of programmed operations generated by highly complex algorithms through the use of punched cards.

items.title: Remillard Brick Company records, 1879-1921
items.description: Title papers, together with various bound ledgers of the Remillard Brick Company (San Francisco and Oakland, California) covering the period 1879 to 1921.

items.title: White's Patent Rotary furnace : patent agreement, San Francisco, 1879
items.description: Concerns the various interests of parties involved with the ore-processing furnace, who are from either San Francisco or San Jose. John Howell is to be paid $1000. for the exclusive right of Rankin Brayton & Co. to manufacture the "Howell improved White furnace.".

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: [Wong Quon Sue ("Wah Chung") businessman and Chinese labor contractor for the Southern Pacific Railroad] [graphic]
items.description: With the Royal Gallery hand stamp verso and credit recto.

items.title: Herbert Gregory Prichard diary recording labor strife and the shipbuilding industry in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1918-1919
items.description: The diary records first-hand observation and eyewitness accounts of the coal strikes and ensuing violence that occurred in the San Francisco Bay Area in the early 1900's.

items.title: Oral history interview with Gallagher on the I.W.W. and Tom Mooney by Willa Klug Baum

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: Laying the first Pacific cable : diaries of cable engineer Henry Clifford on the ships Colonia and Anglia, 1902-1903
items.description: The diaries begin with joining the Anglia at Greenwich on January 7, 1902, and from there on there is a daily record of the voyage to Brisbane where the first leg - from Southport to Norfolk Island - begins. Here they had to build the station while the New Zealand and Fiji branches of the cable were laid.

items.title: Letter to Ebon C. Ingersoll, Chairman Sub-Committee on Commerce on Cuba Telegraph, 1870 July 12.
items.description: Requests repeal of the monopoly claimed by Act of 1866.

items.title: Oakland Home Telephone Company records, 1893-1909
items.description: Business and legal documents and correspondence which deals with the creation and organization of the Oakland Home Telephone Company. Correspondence includes letters from an injured employee, letters dealing with stockholders of Telepost, and letters discussing bills and agreements concerning construction and…

items.title: Telephone advertising card / Portsmouth Telephone Exchange

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: DeForest Radio Telephone Companies, 1907-1920 : typescript, 1977
items.description: Mayes has an interest in the history of radio tube development.

items.title: Federal telegraph company : photographs
items.description: Early 20th century photographs depict the first Poulsen arc from Denmark; a wireless telephone station; generators and cabinets; interior and exterior views of various telegraph stations in the United States, Ireland and England; and construction sites for new stations.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Trade, merchandising and retail

items.title: Faxon Dean Atherton Papers
items.description: A native of Dedham, Massachusetts, Atherton first came to the Pacific coast around 1834 to work for a ship chandlery firm in Valparaiso, Chile. He settled in Valparaiso in 1840 and became a successful merchant dealing in hides and tallow, foodstuffs, and other commodities.

items.title: Menlo Park (Calif.) grocery store : day book, 1882
items.description: List of customers, their purchases and the prices paid for their supplies.

items.title: W.H. Taylor collection, 1837-1938
items.description: W.H. Taylor, for whom this collection is named, was a San Mateo, California, resident at the time of his gift, and was with W. H. Taylor & Co., Ltd., Investment Securities, in San Francisco.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: American and Australian Line via New Zealand around the world : schedule, 18--.
items.description: Schedule, with fold out maps of the world, United States, New Zealand, and the British Isles. Also included are two pasteboard invitations: civic dinner in honor of James Rolph, 21 Feb 1934, at Benjamin Franklin Hotel, San Mateo, and to meet Hon. Herbert Hoover, 8 Apr 1938, at War Memorial Opera House, San Francisco.

items.title: California Street Railroad Co. records, 1877-1904
items.description: Legal papers, accounting reports and other papers pertaining to the company.

items.title: James Otey Bradford papers, 1869-1919
items.description: James Otey Bradford (d 1919?] was born in Virginia and served as a lieutenant in the Confederate Navy. After the war he worked for various English shipping lines. He began his employ with Wells, Fargo in New York City. In this position he was in charge of freight and travel requests for tourists.).

items.title: Letcher railroad collection, 1860-1889
items.description: Dr. Howard T. Letcher worked for the Shasta Division of the Southern Pacific Railroad in 1940 and 1941; he was a noted railroad historian and in 1971 was asked by then California Governor Ronald Reagan to serve on the board of directors of the Transportation museum in Sacramento, California.

items.title: Letcher railroad collection, 1887-1889
items.description: Dr. Howard T. Letcher worked for the Shasta Division of the Southern Pacific Railroad in 1940 and 1941; he was a noted railroad historian and in 1971 was asked by then California Governor Ronald Reagan to serve on the board of directors of the Transportation museum in Sacramento, California.

items.title: Lewis Tasheira's history : typescript copy, 1920 Dec. 13.
items.description: Mention of various railroad men and companies. Worked with Henry Root in Oakland, later C.P. Huntington and Leland Stanford in California and elsewhere. Covers the period 1864-1903.

items.title: Manzanita Water Company records, 1883-1908
items.description: Since the early 1860s, The Manzanita Water Company distributed water for domestic, manufacturing, and irrigation purposes. Their primary clients included Stanford University and nearby organizations such as St. Patrick's Seminary in Menlo Park.

items.title: Mr. C.P. Huntington's reception : Palace Hotel, San Francisco : albumen print, 1888 May 1.
items.description: Fifty-three male portrait busts with Collis Potter Huntington in the center. Each attendee to the reception is identified by name.

items.title: Photographs of an early street car and Henry Casebolt, president, ca. 1872 and 1875 Feb.
items.description: The street car photo includes the driver, John McCord, and Henry Casebolt, president. Photographed by John D. Codeus, People's Art Gallery. The portrait of Henry Casebolt, president of the Sutter Street Railroad Company in 1872, was made by I.W. Taber.

items.title: Relations between the Central Pacific Railroad Company and the U.S. government : published pamphlet
items.description: I. The legal obligations and the manner in which they have been observed. II. The benefits promised and how they have been realized.

items.title: Reports, 1880-1881
items.description: Includes: 1. Extracts from the land agent's report, 1880; 2. The stock of the Central Pacific Railroad Company by Fisk & Hatch, 1880; and 3. Central Pacifc report to stock holders by Fisk & Hatch, 1881.

items.title: Southern Pacific Company public relations collection, 1900, 1959-1972
items.description: Typescripts generated by the Southern Pacific public relations office concerning historical material, the Southern Pacific Pipe Lines, Inc., and the Southern Pacific Transportation Company. Also included is a bibliography, a photocopy of a speech by C.P. Huntington, May 1900, and two publications.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1867-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. It was the first railroad to connect Los Angeles to the rest of California and its lines extended as far as New Orleans.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 2, Operating and Maintenance Department records, 1889-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. It was the first railroad to connect Los Angeles to the rest of California and its lines extended as far as New Orleans.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 3, Mechanical Department records, 1909-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. It was the first railroad to connect Los Angeles to the rest of California and its lines extended as far as New Orleans.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 4, Accounting Department records, 1862-1988
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. It was the first railroad to connect Los Angeles to the rest of California and its lines extended as far as New Orleans.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Venture capital and finance

items.title: Anthony Egl et als., plaintiffs, vs. The Central Pacific Railroad Company, defendants. Complaint. In the District Court of the Fourth Judicial District of the State of California, in and for the City and County of San Francisco : published pamphlet, 1876
items.description: Legal brief presented in the Fourth judicial district court of the State of California by plaintiffs Anthony Egl, Anthony Coolot and John R. Robinson vs. The Central Pacific Railroad Company. Defendants are Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins and Collis Potter Huntington.

items.title: Donohoe Kelly & Co. records, 1863-1917
items.description: The Donohoe, Kelly Banking Company was a large private banking company formed in the second half of the nineteenth century, and flourishing until 1929 when it transferred its business to the Bank of America of California, later the Bank of America, National Trust and Savings Association.

items.title: Stock and bond certificates : miscellaneous collection, 1875-1911
items.description: Several of the stock certificates were signed by Charles F. Crocker.

items.title: Stock report and California Street Journal, 1872 May 21.
items.description: Lists latest mining news, removals, morning sales, previous day's afternoon sales, stock brokers' cards, and lost or stolen shares.

items.title: William C. Ralston Correspondence, ca. 1870-1890
items.description: William Chapman Ralston, born 12 June 1826 in Ohio, was a banker and steamship owner. In 1864 he helped organize the Bank of California and served as its first president. He died 27 August 1875.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: Classification and Arrangement of the Stock of A.L. Bancroft & Company, No. 721 Market Street, San Francisco
items.description: Single-sided printed broadside, with one small woodcut, arranged as if an uncut eight-page pamphlet. Describes the arrangement of the books as well as "The Scope of the Business: Books, Stationery, Music & Musical Instruments, Printing, Lithography & Engravings, Binding and Blank Book Manufacturing, Publishing."…

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company payroll book, 1883
items.description: Pacific Improvement Company payroll ledger, 1883. This is a single item collection constituted by the Pacific Improvement Co. payroll book for 1883. The book does not duplicate any information in the related Pacific Improvement Co. Collections (JL001 and JL017).

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1863-1967
items.description: Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed by C. P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. The Company played a role in the development of land and railroads in various parts of the United States, but particularly in California and Texas.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1869-1931 (bulk 1883-1927)
items.description: The Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed during the days of C.P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. Contains business records of the Pacific Improvement Company and its subsidiaries.

items.title: Parke & Lacy business records, circa 1870-1901
items.description: 1 business ledger (labeled "day book," 7 original photographs, and related business documents).

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Environment and conservation

items.title: Are the lands in the Big Basin worth one hundred dollars per acre? The result of a personal visit to a most marvelous forest of redwood, that pointed gigantic fingers to heaven before Moses crossed the Red Sea : newsclipping, 1902 July 30.
items.description: Testimony is presented as to the land's value as a park and the value of the timber alone. Letters are printed from several readers.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Farming, canning and food processing

items.title: Betty Chase collection related to the Wilcox Fruit Company, 1870s-1960s.
items.description: I. A. Wilcox was the founder of the Wilcox Fruit Company. He bought property in Santa Clara and left his wife and children in the East Bay. His son, Dr. Walter I. Wilcox, took over management of the Wilcox Fruit Company in the early 1900's. Another son, Harry Wilcox, had a printing company in San Jose.

items.title: Cliff Pierce, "The Webb Ranch: Pioneers to Pumpkins"
items.description: Leased from Stanford University and subleased by James Rolph in 1922, George Webb started Webb Ranch as a strawberry farm. It is now the oldest operating farm that has leased land from Stanford University.

items.title: Henry Kingwell photo album of life as a California Agricultural Commissioner, 1921-1953
items.description: Henry Kingwell, a resident of Colusa, California, served for decades as Glenn County's Agricultural Commissioner until his retirement in 1951. Photograph album with a total of 566 original photographs, of various dimensions (including some 8x10 in.), each neatly captioned, in white ink, by Kingwell on the album…

items.title: Palo Alto Stock Farm photographs, 1880-1885
items.description: Charles Conklin Wooster, born in Albany, NY, in 1845, was a horse trainer and coachman for Leland Stanford from about 1870 until Stanford's death in 1893. He continued to work for Jane Stanford, and after her death in 1905, for the University.

items.title: Palo Alto Stock Farm Records, 1875-1913
items.description: The Palo Alto Stock Farm comprised the major farming properties of Senator Leland Stanford. The first property of the Palo Alto Stock Farm was purchased in 1876 from George Gordon; later additions increased its size to approximately 8000 acres. The Stock Farm later became the site of Stanford University.

items.title: Steele Ranch records, 1855-1973
items.description: Compilation of ranch records from the Steele Ranches of San Mateo County, California. Includes financial papers, legal papers, photographs, maps, and miscellaneous background notes written by Mrs. Catherine Steele. The collection is a compilation of ranch papers from the Steele Ranches of San Mateo County, California.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Mining and quarrying

items.title: Adolph Sutro papers, 1869-1899
items.description: Adolph Heinrich Sutro was born in Prussia in 1830. He came to the United States in 1850, to California in 1851, and to Nevada in 1860. Sutro was the mining engineer who planned the Sutro Tunnel, which was constructed through Mount Davidson to reach the Comstock lode.

items.title: Asbury Harpending papers
items.description: Asbury Harpending was a native of Princeton, Kentucky. At the age of fifteen, he ran away from home, joining William Walker on his filibuster expedition to Nicaragua. In 1857, he traveled to California, making a fortune in gold mining in Camptonville, California, and, later, in Mexico.

items.title: Greystone Quarry papers
items.description: Greystone Quarry, formerly known as Goodrich Quarry, was the source for the sandstone used to build Stanford University in the 1880s and 1890s. Map, instructions, and photographs (with negatives) from a tour of Greystone Quarry led by Robert Butler and Rixford Snyder in April 1994; a clipping on the quarry, 1984.

items.title: James Macdonald Hyde papers
items.description: James MacDonald Hyde, a mining engineer, earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford University in May 1901. These papers consist of three patents for mining apparatus, 1912-1919; three maps of the Sullivan Mine (Congress Junction, Arizona); photographs of Hyde's machinery, 1912-1916 and undated.

items.title: New Almaden Mine records, 1845-1973
items.description: In 1845, Captain Andres Castillero of the Mexican Army was sent on a routine scouting patrol through what is now northern California, then part of Mexican territory. As an amateur geologist, Castillero recognized the possibility that the rolling hills held vast mineral deposits.

items.title: Western mining documents, maps, and photographs, circa 1900-1941
items.description: Materials include a variety of documents related to mining operations (primarily in California and Nevada, though with some documents related to Colorado and British Columbia), including plans, printed matter, reports on properties, agreements, financials, maps, several reports on tungsten, blueprints, photographs…

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: Buildings of Fair Heirs in San Francisco [graphic]
items.description: This album documents approximately forty downtown San Francisco real estate holdings of the heirs of real estate, silver, and railroad magnate James Graham Fair.

items.title: Deed to Mary E. Daves for land in the Rancho Rinconada de los Gatos, Santa Clara County, Calif., 1877
Keep your eye on Palo Alto : real estate promotion, 1892
items.description: The brochure includes a Palo Alto map by H.W. Simkins, city clerk and editor of the Palo Alto Times, from which a large segment on Stanford University, its founders, and the environs of Palo Alto is reprinted.

items.title: Land sale document to Samuel Manning, 1870 Aug. 16.
items.description: Nine and one-half acres in Santa Clara County, Calif.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company map collection
items.description: Maps of Pacific Improvement Company holdings in California and Nevada, as well as a few Utah and Oregon properties. Over 300 blueprint maps mounted on 144 canvas-backed, bound sheets showing various towns and localities in the Western United States and depicting the real estate holdings of the Pacific Improvement…

items.title: R.O. Holtzman letter to Herbert C. Nash
items.description: Herbert C. Nash (1860-1902) was private secretary to Leland Stanford, tutor to Leland Stanford Jr., and librarian at Stanford University. Letter from Holtzman, Washington, D.C., real estate agent, to Herbert C. Nash pertaining to the disposition of Leland Stanford's house and property in Washington.

items.title: Records of Stanford properties, 1861-1927
items.description: Deeds and other legal documents relating to properties owned by Leland and Jane Stanford and, later, by Stanford University in Butte, Tehama, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Yolo, Monterey, Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Los Angeles, Marin, Napa, Sacramento, San Francisco and San Luis Obispo counties, California.

items.title: Santa Clara County abstracts of title, 1889-1919
items.description: 8 abstracts of title, city of San Jose, 1889-1919; 1 abstract of title, city of Santa Clara, 1914; and 1 abstract of title, Solano County, 1910 (lacking title page).

items.title: Stanford ranches and lands records, 1838-1896
items.description: In 1876, Leland Stanford acquired 650 acres of the former Rancho San Francisquito with the intention of establishing a rural residence. Subsequently, he initiated the establishment of the Palo Alto Stock Farm, dedicated to breeding trotting horses.

items.title: Stanford University map collection, 1853-1998
items.description: The maps in this collection pertain to the University campus, to other lands owned by Jane and Leland Stanford or the University, and to adjacent communities.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: A few of the first steamship pioneers living in 1874, surrounding the old ship, and William H. Webb : photographs, ca. 1875
items.description: Included in the photo of pioneers is a photo of the "California.".

items.title: George E. Tillitson collection on railroads, 1880-1940
items.description: Collection contains outlines of corporate histories of railroads in the United States and Canada including some streetcar lines and electric interurban lines. Includes dates of incorporation, lists of points served, lists of mileage, time schedules, maps of lines, and lists or reports of accidents.

items.title: I.W. Taber photographs
items.description: Taber was a noted commercial photographer whose studio was based in San Francisco beginning in 1871. Along with his own photographs he sold work by Carleton Watkins (whose negatives he purchased following Watkins' bankruptcy) and Alfred Hart among others.

items.title: Keepsakes issued to members of the Book Club of California in commemoration of the centennial of the transcontinental railroad, 1969
items.description: Includes 1. "The Hewes Receipt," by Ralph W. Hansen; and 2. "The 'Goat Island Grab'," by Ted Wurm (2 copies).

items.title: Life of Cable Ropes : notebook containing data on the San Francisco cable railroads, 1884-1888
Mayfield Road proposed changes papers
items.description: Consists of two documents: notice to Santa Clara Supervisors relative to planting trees along Mayfield Road (undated but initiated by Leland Stanford) and "field notes of proposed change of road from Mayfield to Searsville" by J. G. McMillan, November 1887.

items.title: Newsclipping collection, 1890-1952
items.description: The collection was probably assembled by the Transportation Librarian; the newspapers are primarily local (Palo Alto times, San Francisco Chronicle, and San Francisco Examiner), but the Tacoma News Tribune is also represented so it is assumed other people were sending in material to the library.

items.title: Railroad passes issued by and to C.H. Redington, 1873-1924
items.description: Redington received passes from many railroad companies, both before and after his retirement as Assistant Treasurer for the Southern Pacific Company.

items.title: Railroad timetables and other printed ephemera, 1838-1946
items.description: Includes timetables for the New England states (The Pathfinder Railway Guide, (1849-1854 & 1896), the west coast.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley Interurbans, An Oral History by One who Remembers it Well
items.description: Rixford Snyder was a professor of history at Stanford University. Photocopies of photographs, illustrations, and articles with additional text by Snyder, concerning the Peninsular Railway, the electric trolley that ran between San Jose and Palo Alto, California, passing through Stanford University.

items.title: Timothy Hopkins transportation collection, 1816-1942
items.description: Correspondence, records, logs, clipping books, timetables, tickets and legal documents pertaining to early railroading in England, India, and the United States. Topics include the construction of the Central Pacific railroad, shipping and aviation.

items.title: William Birelie Hyde papers, 1861-1896
items.description: William Birelie Hyde was born February 14, 1842, in or near Baltimore, Md., the second child of Oliver Hyde, Jr. and Harriet Kean Hyde. He and his family traveled overland to California either in 1851 or in 1853, and settled in Benicia, where he later attended the Benicia Collegiate Institute.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: John G. McMillan papers, 1887
items.description: Map, estimates of water flow, and letter to Leland Stanford relating to proposed pipeline extending from a proposed dam on Corte Madera Creek to a proposed dam on San Francisquito Creek, 1887.

items.title: Joseph W. Gross research collection pertaining to water supply/control and flooding in California, 1890-1940
items.description: Joseph Watson Gross was a graduate from the University of California in 1907 and majored in Sanitary and Irrigation Engineering. He had a long career specializing as a "municipal and reclamation" engineer.

items.title: Niles Dam collection
items.description: Niles Dam on Alameda Creek was built in 1887 by the Spring Valley Water Company, at the same site where Jose de Jesus Vallejo had build a dam for his grist mill in 1841. Water from the SVWC dam was diverted to the San Francisco water system. The dam was removed in 2006 as part of the Alameda Creek Restoration Project.

items.title: Spring Valley Water Company records, 1905-1920
items.description: Legal papers documenting the agreements between the Spring Valley Water Company and Stanford University regarding Searsville Dam and Resevoir, 1919.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Angelo F. Semino papers, 1856-1986
items.description: Angelo F. Semino received his a.b. in mechanical engineering from Stanford in 1922. Land deeds for property in Mountain View, California (the Mayfield Mall), together with a 79 page typescript about its history. Original typed reports, copies, reprints, and manuscript notes on heat exchanges in the petroleum industry.

items.title: View of the widening of Kearny Street and construction of the Mechanics' Hotel in San Francisco : photographic print
items.description: Large crowd of men and one woman is gathered in front of the three-story brick Mechanics' Hotel on Kearny Street near Broadway. The hotel has been elevated on wooden supports to widen the street. Supporting lumber and machinery are visible. Photo appears to be dated in the late 1890s.

sectors.name: Education and research — Campus and student life

items.title: Geological Club of Stanford University minute book
items.description: The Geological Club at Stanford University was founded in 1892, and was later reorganized into a geological society in 1899 and included both students and alumni. The club continued to operate with the support of the Department of Geology and Mining into the mid-20th century.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: J.C.L. Fish notes for the drafting room
items.description: J. C. L. (John Charles Lounsbury) Fish (1870-1962) was a Professor of Civil Engineering, Emeritus, at the School of Engineering, Stanford University. The senior drafting room in the engineering building was the meeting place for the Civil Engineer's Club, later Civil Engineering Society.

items.title: John Richards, "Works administration: lectures before the student of the Leland Stanford Junior University"
items.description: John Richards was a lecturer in mechanical engineering at Stanford University, 1895-96. Contains ten lectures on shop management; topics include expense, plant implements and processes, plant design, employees, measurements, machine tools, invention, cooperation, and selling the product.

items.title: L.M. Hoskins, the theory of hydraulic motors lecture notes
items.description: Hoskins was professor of applied mathematics at Stanford University from 1892 until his retirement in 1925. Notebook of Hoskins' mimeographed lectures kept by Thomas Henry Pomeroy, with some problem solutions done by Pomeroy, a member of the Stanford class of 1895.

items.title: Max C. Yost report on Stanford engineering curricula
items.description: Max C. Yost earned his BS in mechanical engineering at Stanford in 1952. Collection consists of tables compiled by Yost comparing engineering requirements for his years at Stanford (1944-1952), the Pioneer Class (entered 1891, graduated 1895), and the academic year 1996/97.

items.title: Stephen Timoshenko papers, 1907-1996 (inclusive), 1921-1970 (bulk)
items.description: Stephen Prokofievitch Timoshenko, a world-renowned authority on theoretical and applied mechanics, was educated at the Munich Polytechnic Institute and at the University of Gottingen. Correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, galleys, notes, reprints, photographs, passports, awards, and other items.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Castilleja School, 1907-1940
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1907 by Mary Ishbel Lockey (a Stanford alumna) to offer girls a comprehensive, college preparatory education, taking its name from the first girl's school in Palo Alto known as Castilleja Hall.

items.title: College of Notre Dame (later: Notre Dame de Namur University), 1890-1976
items.description: Located in San Jose, then Belmont, California. Founded in 1851 as the Academy of Notre Dame. Chartered in 1868 as the College of Notre Dame. Moved to Belmont in 1923. In 2001 name changed to Notre Dame de Namur University.

items.title: George A. Merrill letters, 1885-1908
items.description: Letters from Horace Davis, A.S. Hallidie, David Starr Jordan, and L.A. Buchanan, largely pertaining to the Lick School of Mechanical Arts, of which Merrill was principal. Buchanan, largely pertaining to the Lick School of Mechanical Arts, of which Merrill was principal.

items.title: Margarita Espinosa notes on Adelante Villa, 1987-1993
items.description: Photocopy of undated notes by Espinosa on Adelante Villa, a preparatory school for girls founded by Lucy Fletcher and Eleanor Brooks Pearson and first located at Stanford. Also includes short article and letter on the history of Castilleja School, 1987, and the letter that accompanied these materials, 1993.

items.title: Palo Alto Military Academy (formerly: Manzanita Hall), 1893-1932
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1893 as Manzanita Hall. Became Palo Alto Military Academy in 1919. Closed in 1972.

items.title: San Jose State University (formerly: California State University, San Jose; formerly: San Jose State College; formerly: California State Teachers College at San Jose; formerly: California State Normal School), 1875-1982
items.description: Originally located in San Francisco, but moved to San Jose in 1871. Established in 1857 as the Minns' Evening Normal School. Became California State Normal School in 1862 and the California State Teachers College at San Jose in 1921.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Education, records
items.description: In October 1892, the Department of Education at Stanford University established a kindergarten on campus to serve in part as a laboratory for advanced students of the education department. It was under the direction of Professor Earl Barnes and instructor Margaret Schallenberger.

items.title: University of the Pacific (formerly: College of the Pacific, formerly: University of the Pacific), 1873-1978
items.description: First located in Santa Clara, California. Chartered in 1851 as California Wesleyan College, soon changed to University of the Pacific. In 1911 became College of the Pacific. Moved to San Jose in 1871 and from San Jose to Stockton, California in 1924. In 1961 became University of the Pacific.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: Cecil H. Green oral history interview transcript, 1995
items.description: Green was a British-born American geophysicist who trained at the University of British Columbia and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He was a founder of Texas Instruments.

items.title: Geological map; San Juan Bautist Hills, 3 miles south of San Jose, California : hand-drawn and colored map, 1901, Jan..
items.description: Scale 1 : 7680, contours 25 ft. (1 inch = 640 ft.) Data of topography enlarged from San Jose sheet (U.S.G.S.).

items.title: John Casper Branner papers, 1882-1921
items.description: John Casper Branner, second president of Stanford University, was born in New Market, Tennessee in 1850. He entered Cornell University in 1870, but left in 1874 for Brazil first as assistant geologist on the Geological Survey of Brazil then as assistant engineer for the Sao Cyriaco Gold Mining Company.

items.title: The Berkeley Hills : a detail of coast range geology / original typewritten copy, 1902
items.description: Originally a gift of the author to Stephen B. Fiske.

items.title: William Russel Dudley papers, 1838-1937 (inclusive), 1864-1912 (bulk)
items.description: William Russel Dudley earned his bachelor's (1874) and master's (1876) degrees in botany at Cornell University; after graduation he pursued botanical study in Strassburg and Berlin. He taught at Cornell and Indiana University before joining the Stanford faculty in 1892.

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Doris Helen Linder (1925-2008) was born in Columbia, South Dakota to Swedish immigrants Hilda and Arvid Justus Linder. Linder studied history at Stanford University, where she received a BA in 1946 and an MA in 1949. She received a Ph.D. in History from the University of Minnesota in 1961.

items.title: Eric Hutchinson papers, 1891-1982 (inclusive), 1954-1982 (bulk)
items.description: Eric Hutchinson, born in England in 1920, was educated at the University of Cambridge (1938-1945), earning all three of his degrees in chemistry. He taught at Sheffield University and Fordham University, before joining the Stanford faculty in 1949.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: "Becoming Stanford: The Making of an American University" [videorecording]
items.description: Part 1, "The Founding," covers the origins and building of the university through World War I; highlights include Stanford family history, the first Big Game between Stanford and UC Berkeley, early student life, the rise of tenure, and the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Andrew Putnam Hill photograph album, 1887-circa 1895
items.description: Formerly a student of art, Andrew Putnam Hill became a professional photographer in 1889, opening a studio in San Jose, California with his partner, Sydney J. Yard. The images in this album primarily document the Palo Alto residence of Jane and Leland Stanford, the Palo Alto Stock Farm horses, and Stanford University.

items.title: Andrew Putnam Hill Photograph collection, 1890-1895
items.description: Mounted albumen prints, commercially produced by Hill and his two studios, Hill & Yard and Hill & Watkins, of the newly established Stanford University and of the activity of the Palo Alto Stock Farm, upon which the University had been built. Subjects include campus views.

items.title: Andrew Putnam Hill photographs
items.description: Andrew Putnam Hill (1853-1922) was born in Porter County, Indiana. In 1867 at the age of 14, he moved to California with an uncle, coming to Santa Clara County in 1868. He attended high school at Santa Clara College, and then studied art in San Francisco.

items.title: Archibald J. Treat papers, 1883-1961 (inclusive), 1883-1941 (bulk)
items.description: Archibald J. Treat was employed by the Central Pacific Rail Road in 1879 as an office boy and telegraph operator. He worked his way up to become secretary to Stephen T. Gage, who was assistant to Leland Stanford when Stanford was president of the CPRR.

items.title: Charles Anderson Gauld papers
items.description: Gauld, who earned his A.B. in history at Stanford in 1932, was a lecturer at Stanford and assistant editor of HISPANIC AMERICAN REPORT. These papers pertain largely to Stanford anecdotes and history and include his typescript articles on George E. Crothers and Jane Stanford.

items.title: David Starr Jordan Papers
items.description: The Jordan Papers span 1861-1951, although the bulk of the collection dates between 1891 and 1929. Very few items pre-date Jordan's connection with Stanford University and there is very little material after the severe stroke he suffered in the summer of 1929.

items.title: David Starr Jordan papers, 1861-1981
items.description: David Starr Jordan was born at Gainesville, New York, on January 19, 1851. In March, 1869, Jordan entered Cornell University to join the first freshman class (which had begun work in the fall of 1868).

items.title: Francis Albert Smith papers
items.description: Francis Albert Smith earned three degrees in chemistry at Stanford University: AB 1922, AM 1923, and Ph.D 1926. Collection includes two appointment letters from Ray Lyman Wilbur, 1922-23; 3 letters from Edward C. Franklin, 1923-32; fundraising letter from Herbert Hoover re the Stanford Re-investment Fund ca. 1940.

items.title: George Mann Richardson letter to Firstall
items.description: Professor of Organic Chemistry at Stanford University (1891-1902). Letter recounting the first year at Stanford University, in particular difficulties from the lack of equipment, the success of the football team in its first game against Berkeley, and a hiking trip Richardson and his wife took from Stanford to…

items.title: George T. Clark papers, 1862-1935
items.description: Clark was Stanford University Librarian, 1907-1928 (emeritus 1928 until his death in 1940) and co-founder and first president of the California Library Association.

items.title: Grant founding and endowing the Leland Stanford Junior University
items.description: The Leland Stanford Junior University was established in 1885 in memory of Leland Stanford Jr., the only child of Senator and Mrs. Leland Stanford. Founding of the University was accomplished by a Grant of Endowment by Jane and Leland Stanford, dated November 1885.

items.title: Halsey L. Royden, "The History of the Stanford Mathematics Department"
items.description: Halsey L. Royden earned his B.S. in 1948 and his M.S. in 1949 at Stanford University and his Ph.D. at Harvard in 1951, after which he returned to Stanford to join the faculty in the department of mathematics.

items.title: Henry Z. Osborne papers
items.description: Henry Zenas Osborne (1848-1923) was owner/editor of the Los Angeles Evening Express (1884-1897), gold miner, and California state representative from 1917 until his death in 1923. He was married to Helen Annas (formerly of Cazenovia, New York). All five of their children attended Stanford University.

items.title: Nancy Mason, "A Part of his Childhood Belongs to Peter Coutts; A Reminiscence of Wendell Fletcher" typescript
items.description: Account of Wendell Fletcher's childhood, as written by Nancy Mason. Fletcher lived on campus in the Tower House with his family from 1910 to 1918. His father was a civil engineer with Stanford University during this time.

items.title: Palo Alto Times, Special Memorial Edition, March 24, 1905
items.description: Jane Eliza Lathrop was born August 25, 1828, the daughter of Dyer Lathrop of Albany, New York. In 1850 she married Leland Stanford, returning with him to California in 1855 where they settled in Sacramento. Leland Stanford later became President of the Southern Pacific Railroad and Governor of California.

items.title: President Benjamin Harrison's tour to the Pacific Coast : photographs and ephemera, 1891-1987
items.description: Collections largely consists of photographs taken during the tour, some of which are arranged in an album; subjects include the visit to Stanford University, San Francisco, Monterey, Sacramento, Salem (Oregon), the Presidential train and its crew, the Presidential party, and crowd scenes at various depots.

items.title: Stanford Alumni Association, alumni reminiscences
items.description: Correspondence between Jack W. Shoup, secretary of the Alumni Association, and alumni concerning memories of Senator and Mrs. Stanford (1955-1956), which included attending parties at the Stanford home, Mr. Stanford observing work on Encina Hall, Mrs. Stanford observing work on Memorial Church, Mrs. Stanford visiting…

items.title: Stanford Historical Photograph collection, 1887-circa 1996
items.description: Series 1, General Photographs, documents the campus and campus life; subjects include athletics, original construction of the campus, individual buildings, students and student life activities, commencement activities, academic departments, and damage from the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University. The files were maintained by University Archives staff from around the time of the Archives' establishment in 1965 through mid-2011 Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford…

items.title: Stanford University glass plate negatives, circa 1890-1900
items.description: Eighty glass plate negatives of Stanford images, circa 1890-1900. Subjects include construction, students, faculty, the museum, and the campus.

items.title: Stanford University Photographs, circa 1880s-1906
items.description: Loose and mounted photographs of Greystone Quarry and quarry workers, Stanford campus buildings, Stanford students. Included is a copy of "Glimpses of Leland Stanford, Jr., University, Palo Alto, California," by J. Collier Loose and mounted photographs of Greystone Quarry and quarry workers, Stanford campus buildings…

items.title: Stanford: a sentimental journey : video recordings, 1987
items.description: This film in celebration of Stanford University's centennial includes interviews with faculty and alumni; scenes of academic and student activities; views of the campus; and still photographs transferred to video, primarily concerning the history of Stanford.

items.title: The search for Jane's cold cream jar [electronic resource]; an archaeological adventure at the Stanfords' Palo Alto home
items.description: The Search for Jane's cold Cream Jar is an interactive CD containing images and information about the history, artifacts, and archaeology of the Stanfords' Palo Alto home.

items.title: The Stanford years, being an excerpt from "memoranda," the unpublished autobiography of Theodore J. Hoover:
items.description: Head, Department of Mining and Metallurgy (1919- ) and founding dean of the School of Engineering (1925-1936). Stanford class of 1901. Manuscript (typescript) excerpt from "Memoranda," the unpublished autobiography of Theodore J. Hoover.

items.title: Thomas Welton Stanford Library time capsule collection, 1886-1898
items.description: Thomas Welton Stanford, Leland Stanford's younger brother, reassigned half of his bequest from Leland Stanford's will to Jane Stanford, who used the funds to build a new library. It was one of the first buildings to be completed in the construction of the outer Quadrangle.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: Jane Lathrop Stanford papers, 1860-1983
items.description: Jane Eliza Lathrop was born August 25, 1828, the daughter of Dyer Lathrop of Albany, New York. In 1850 she married Leland Stanford, returning with him to California in 1855 where they settled in Sacramento. Leland Stanford later became President of the Southern Pacific Railroad and Governor of California.

items.title: Samuel Franklin Leib papers, 1881-1920
items.description: The collection consists of four major components: Stanford correspondence pertaining to Judge Leib's association with the Stanford family and his responsibilities as a member of the first Board of Trustees of Stanford University (1891-1923); personal correspondence (1885-1910).

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The Business Affairs organization at Stanford provides integrated financial, technological, business and human resource services for the benefit of the university community.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Angle of repose collection, 1875-1934
items.description: Born in Milton-on-Hudson into loose-knit, Free-Soil Republican, Quaker family, which was keenly interested in literacy, temperance, women's rights and anti-slavery issues of the day. Family friends: Horace Greely, Henry Ward Beecher, Susan B. Anthony.

items.title: Animal locomotion : an electro-photographic investigation of consecutive phases of animal movements. 1872-1885
items.description: The plates are numbered consecutively and supplied only with two title-pages (v. [1] and [16]) A prospectus and catalogue of plates was issued the same year and has been catalogued separately.

items.title: Bruce Bliven papers, 1906-1985
items.description: Born July 27, 1889 in Emmetsburg, Iowa, Bruce Ormsby Bliven was the son of Charles and Lilla Ormsby Bliven. Having won prizes for his writing ability as early as age fourteen, Bruce went on to work his way through Stanford University as a cub reporter for the S.F. Bulletin. He received a B.A. in English in 1911.

items.title: Canciones : collection of Mexican folksongs, 1883-1885
items.description: Probably collected by a Californian, possibly Mary Sheldon Barnes or someone in her history class, because the clippings come from San Francisco and San Jose newspapers.

items.title: Carleton E. Watkins photograph collection
items.description: Carleton E. Watkins was a 19th century photographer based in San Francisco who made his name documenting the rapid growth of the American West. His photographs of the Yosemite Valley, in Mariposa County, California, are said to have influenced Abraham Lincoln's 1864 Yosemite Land Grant, the first act of Congress to…

items.title: Chester W. Barker sheet music collection, 1891-1973
items.description: This collection contains approximately 70 items dating from 1891-1973, the majority of which are from musicals. Almost all are inscribed by Barker with notes, pasted-in lyrics, and a few programs.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photograph collection
items.description: This collection by Eadweard Muybridge encompasses stereographic cards, gelatin silver prints, mammoth plates, an 1877 panorama of San Francisco, and Muybridge's motion studies plates. Also includes a photograph album of early views of Grizzly Giant, Yosemite, Mills College, and San Francisco, and other locations.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photograph collection
items.description: Eadweard Muybridge was born in Kingston-upon-Thames, England, in April 1830 as Edward James Muggeridge. He came to the United States in 1851 and worked for two publishing companies on the east coast until 1855, when he moved to California and established a book store in San Francisco.

items.title: Isaiah West Taber photograph collection
items.description: Isaiah West Taber (1830-1912) was an American daguerreotypist, ambrotypist, and photographer. He worked for photographers Bradley and Rulofson in San Franciso from 1864 before opening his own studio, the "Taber Gallery," at No. 12 Montgomery Street in 1871.
