He became well-known for portraiture and views of California.

items.title: John W. Metcalf papers, c. 1880-1940
items.description: John W. Metcalf (1856-1926) was a composer, musician and music instructor. Metcalf considered himself the first music teacher at Stanford University, but it is more likely that he taught several students privately at Roble Hall. Unpublished listing of music titles available on request. Please contact the department.

items.title: Leland Stanford : lithograph, 1875
items.description: Portrait print mounted in a folder. Handwritten note by Anthony L. Auradou, written January 24, 1941, presents the image to Mr. Leland Cutler. Auradou mentions that Henry Steinegger engraved the image about 1875, and that it is rare that a protrait of this size should be engraved on stone.

items.title: Mary Hallock Foote papers, 1863-1924 (inclusive), 1868-1916 (bulk)
items.description: Mary Hallock Foote was born Mary Haviland Hallock on November 19, 1847, at Milton-on-Hudson, N.Y., the youngest of four children. Her close-knit farming family were Quakers, Free-Soil Republicans of English stock, sympathetic to anti-slavery, temperance, and women's rights.

items.title: Pauline Lane papers, 1878-1897
items.description: Pauline Lane (d. 1902) was the wife of Levi Cooper Lane, president of Cooper Medical College in San Francisco. After her death, she bequeathed a third of her estate to college. It was the largest gift allowed at that time under California law. With that gift, the Lane Medical Library was established in 1906.

items.title: Sheet music : miscellaneous collection, ca 1890-1950
items.description: Includes some early San Francisco and San Jose imprints. Also includes professional copies specifically for broadcast only.

items.title: William Hubert Burgess letters and miscellany, 1851-1899
items.description: Burgess was an artist, silversmith, miner, and teacher. He and his family were originally from England, then settled in Boston and New York. He arrived in Calif. in 1850, sailing via Cape Horn, aboard the ship Byron. Consists of 13 letters and some incomplete letters to Burgess's mother in England.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: An architect grows up in Palo Alto; memoirs of Birge M. Clark, F.A.I.A. : typescript, 1982
items.description: Birge M. Clark earned his A.B. in graphic art at Stanford in 1914 and his degree in architecture at Columbia in 1917. After his service as a balloon observer during World War I, he returned to Palo Alto and began his practice as an architect.

items.title: Archibald J. Treat photograph collection
items.description: Working his way up from office boy for the Central Pacific Railroad office to secretary to Stephen T. Gage, assistant to Railroad president Leland Stanford, Treat was admitted to the California bar in 1897.

items.title: Charles Edward Hodges papers, 1891-1929
items.description: Charles E. Hodges was appointed Resident Architect by Leland and Jane Stanford in 1891, a position he held until his resignation in June of 1906. Prior to this appointment, he was draftsman to Shepley, Rutan and Coolidge, the architectural firm responsible for many of the University's original buildings.

items.title: Charles Edward Hodges photograph albums, circa 1898-1905
items.description: Collection contains two photograph albums belonging to Charles E. Hodges, resident draftsman and later architect at Stanford University. Volume 28.1 (ca. 1898-1905) contains images of Memorial Arch and its frieze; the Stanford University Inn.

items.title: Lee Emerson Bassett house records
items.description: Lee Emerson Bassett, professor of Speech and Drama at Stanford University from 1900 to 1938, built his home on campus at 740 Santa Ynez Street. Included in this collection are specifications by the architect, A. W. Smith; bills and one letter from Leon S. Bean, general contractor, 1909.

items.title: Palo Alto ranch employee time records
items.description: Time record notebook for employees on Palo Alto Ranch, maintained by J. C. Conway. Includes records for named employees and the hours spent on specific Quad construction jobs during March 1892. C. Conway.

items.title: Samuel Charles Bugbee papers, 1861-1876
items.description: Architect Samuel Charles Bugbee helped plan the Stanford family home in Palo Alto, and perhaps also contributed to the San Francisco Conservatory of Flowers in the late 19th century. This collection consists of three sketchbooks and loose drawings on onion skin paper.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society, Historic Houses III : research and production materials, 1972-2004 (inclusive), 1999-2004 (bulk)
items.description: Research and production materials for the book, HISTORIC HOUSES III: SAN JUAN NEIGHBORHOOD, STANFORD UNIVERSITY, published by the Stanford Historical Society in 2005. Includes Byron Feig's original watercolor painting used on the cover and his original pencil drawings of each house.

items.title: Stanford University, Museum, Committee for Art, Stanford portfolio records, 1970-1980
items.description: Research files of Hametia Fielder King relating to the design and construction of the Stanford Museum of Art, used by the Museum docent program for their "Stanford Portfolio." A number of the files pertain to George Washington Percy and Ernest Ransome and there are some files pertaining to other campus buildings.

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. Architects active during the early years of the University include Bakewell and Brown; Shepley, Rutan, and Coolidge.

items.title: The autobiography of an architect
items.description: Includes a one-page letter from Mrs. Dorothy Feltham, Secretary to Mr. J.H. Clark, explaining the memoir.

items.title: Views of Thurlow Lodge by Carleton Watkins: photograph album, circa 1874
items.description: The album contains original albumen prints of the mansion and grounds of Milton S. Latham in Menlo Park, California. This album, with images approximately 14 x 17 inches, was originally presented to David Farquharson, architect of Thurlow Lodge.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: [California Winery Exhibition 1894] [graphic]
items.description: Pair of large original photographs (27 x 33 cm) by Taber of the California Winery’s exhibition at the Midwinter Fair (1894). The photos show the building’s ornate entrance (with the entrance designed to appear as a wine barrel) as well as the decorative Tasting Room, with many tables (and bottles) but sans visiteurs.

items.title: A Century of Western Living, 1898-1998 : centennial keepsakes, 1998
items.description: Exhibit catalog, copy of the original May, 1898 issue, pin, and ephemera.

items.title: A Century of Western Living, 1898-1998 : poster for centennial exhibit, 1998
Stanford family library, 1795-1902 (inclusive), 1834-1897 (bulk)
items.description: A sampling of the books contained in the libraries of Jane Lathrop Stanford, Leland Stanford, and their son, Leland Stanford, Jr. Included are books inscribed by Mrs. Stanford to Leland, Jr., books annotated by Leland, Jr., and books of Thomas Welton Stanford (brother of Leland Stanford).

items.title: Sunset Magazine : video, 18 Oct. 1998
items.description: Includes interviews of Mel and Bill Lane. Discusses the role of Sunset Magazine over the last one hundred years.

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: Alice Park collection of papers relating to the American League to Abolish Capital Punishment, 1914-1940
items.description: Alice Locke Park was born in Boston in 1861 but lived most of her life in Palo Alto, Calif. She was active in many socially progressive organizations.

items.title: Big Basin : article and clippings removed from A.P. Hill's photograph album, 1901-1954

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: "The Sky Lark"
items.description: Volume 1, issue 1, of a one-page advertiser issued in Mayfield, CA, Oct. 21, 1876. Includes short notice that Peter Coutts was building a brick tower near his home. 21, 1876.

items.title: a Roy Page Ballard papers 1894
items.description: Graduate of Stanford University in history (A.B. May 1897). Notes and outlines for a history of the Stanford campus area originally prepared for a class assignment.

items.title: A Woodside reminiscence: as told by Grizzly Ryder
items.description: "A Woodside Reminiscence: as told by Grizzly Ryder," by Cutler L. Bonestell, is a recounting of a 1914 conversation between Cutler L. Bonestell and Grizzly Ryder on how he survived an attack by a grizzly bear near what is now called Bear Creek, near Woodside, CA.

items.title: Britton and Rey, Lithographers. Artotypes : Artistic homes of California, published in San Francisco Newsletter and Advertiser
items.description: The collection includes artotypes of business blocks, street views, churches, schools, hotels, "bird's eye" views, and other public buildings such as an old people's home, a bath, a store, and athletic club in San Francisco.

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. The individuals and families represented include: pioneers and settlers; professionals, including teachers, doctors, scientists, lawyers and judges; bankers and merchants.

items.title: California history : scrapbook and miscellaneous pamphlets, 1857-1955
items.description: The scrapbook consists primarily of clippings about Santa Clara County history, as well as Monterey, Stanford, and Yosemite. There are also two poems by John E. Richards (pp. 123 & 146).

items.title: California photographs : album, 1885-1899
items.description: Annotated photograph album of California landscape and topographical views. The prints include 19th century views of Palo Alto, Stanford University, San Francisco, Monterey; and in Southern California, Pasadena, Los Angeles, Riverside and Redlands.

items.title: California photographs, circa 1882-1940
items.description: Of unknown origin. 49 photographs. Includes Sierras, boats, Golden Gate Bridge under construction, one unidentified portrait, Pacific Coast Amateur photography association meeting 1889 photographing a solar eclipse, Higuera House in Warm Springs (Fremont) in 1882, interior views.

items.title: California photographs, circa 1900-1950
items.description: Artificial collection created by Stanford. Three boxes of photo prints and lithographs depicting various locations in California.

items.title: California. Legal documents, 1858-1892
items.description: Colusa County. Check for $25. to J.B. Stanton for services to school, 1858. Commissary General of Subsistence. Letter to Lieutenant J.C. Morrill of Fort Ruby, Nevada City, Calif., 1863. Shasta County. Election roll list for American Ranch, 1869. (Gives name, age, occupation, state or country of origin) Alameda County.

items.title: Carleton Watkins stereoview and cabinet photographs
items.description: Photographs by or published by Carleton Watkins. All but one are views of California. Photographs by or published by Carleton E. Watkins in the form of cabinet cards or stereographs.

items.title: Carnegie (Calif.) : typescripts about the Corral Hollow site, 1961
items.description: Includes several pieces: 1. Carnegie; historical landmark in Corral Hollow (11 p.). 2. Tesla, Pottery and Carnegie in Corral Hollow, 1892-1912 (17 pp.), by Mrs. Josephine Leary, of Stockton, Calif. 3. Notes about California registered historical landmarks No. 740 and 755 (including the home of Edward B. Carrell).

items.title: Carnegie : typescripts about the Corral Hollow (California) site, 1961
items.description: Includes several pieces: 1. Carnegie; historical landmark in Corral Hollow (11 pp.), by Earle E. Williams. 2. Tesla, Pottery and Carnegie in Corral Hollow, 1892-1912 (17 pp.), by Mrs. Josephine Leary, of Stockton, Calif. 3.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photographs, ca. 1870-1890
items.description: 1. Vertical steam pumps, stereo, nd. (JL006) 2. 15 stereos from "Pacific Coast Series," including Pigeon Point, New Years Island, Pescadero's Pebble Beach, and Pescadero (M237). 3. 1 stereo San Francisco City Hall cornerstone laying, 1872. Also includes a stereo by Thomas Houseworth of White Sulphur Springs, nd. 4.

items.title: Harry C. Peterson lantern slides, 1892-1917
items.description: Harry Claude Peterson was born in Algona, Iowa, in 1876, son of Julius E. Peterson, a Norwegian mechanician. Leland Stanford had learned of the elder Peterson in Europe and brought him to Stanford University to teach machine shop. Young Harry was educated in public schools in Algona and Palo Alto.

items.title: Illustrated newspapers reporting news from Santa Clara County, 1897-1900
items.description: Articles describe leading business establishments and institutions in Santa Clara County and its cities. Includes many illustrations and several pages of advertisements. The 1900 edition states that this is the oldest illustrated paper in California, established in 1870.

items.title: Joseph Collier, My holiday in California : photograph album, 1901-1941 (inclusive), 1901 (bulk)
items.description: Joseph Collier (1836-1910) was a Scotland-born photographer. Much of his photography was of early Colorado, where he resided from 1871 until his death. Leather bound album of 151 original photographs, including approximately 60 images of Stanford University.

items.title: Juana Briones collection, circa 1960-2009
items.description: Juana Briones (1802-1899) was a businesswoman and landowner in the San Francisco Bay Area.

items.title: Katherine E. Doyle collection of photographs
items.description: Collection contains one print and 22 glass plate negatives, the latter depicting the grounds and interior of a large estate, probably the Doyle residence known as Ringwood in Menlo Park. The negatives are uncredited and may not all be taken by the same photographer.

items.title: Main street, Palo Alto (Calif.) : photograph, ca.1898
items.description: View of University Avenue. Printed on wall of building on the left is "Mail pouch tobacco.".

items.title: Mary Sheldon Barnes collection of Pacific Slope materials, 1769-1898
items.description: Letters, reminiscences, interviews, and term papers written for and collected by Mary Sheldon Barnes and her students in Stanford's Pacific Slope history class. Includes manuscripts of William B. Ide and others on the Bear Flag Revolt; a letter by Jessie Fremont.

items.title: Newspaper devoted to the interests of the California pioneers, 1897, vol. XII, no.6.
items.description: Articles of interest to settlers and pioneers of California including mining news, obituaries, local observances, biographies and illustrations.

items.title: Pacific Slope scrapbooks, 1819-1906
items.description: The first series of scrapbooks was created by mayor (and later governor) Washington Bartlett, containing articles pertaining to political and civic issues in San Francisco and California from 1855 to 1886, as well as some notes and memoranda chronicling his duties as mayor.

items.title: Peter Coutts' Story papers
items.description: Jean-Baptiste Paulin Caperon (better known in California as Peter Coutts), was a successful French businessman, book collector and editor of the republican, anti-royalist paper, LA LIBERTE. Political disputes and health problems caused him to leave France and take up residence in California.

items.title: Reid W. Dennis collection of California lithographs, 1850-1908
items.description: This collection of prints, mostly lithographs (including chromolithographs and colored lithographs), as well as one engraving, primarily portray San Francisco city views, public buildings, and landscapes.

items.title: The eastern editors visit to Vacaville : photographs, 1892 May 21st.
items.description: The photographs depict two scenes along Main Street with a railroad, parade of horse-drawn carts and several buildings, one displaying the American flag. Vacaville was hosting eastern newspaper editors in order to promote their town and orchard industry.

sectors.name: Society and community — Medicine and public health

items.title: [Collection of drug prescriptions], 1880-1937
items.description: Collection of hand-written drug prescriptions from various physicians to various pharmacies. A sampling of physicians and druggists included as entries in this record. Prescriptions have been pasted on blank pages of volumes in roughly prescription number order/chronological order.

items.title: Agnews State Asylum photograph album, 1890-1906
items.description: Consists of photo albumn with 62 photos and an additional 18 loose photos. Depicts Agnews State Asylum in Santa Clara, California. The images depict residents, staff, grounds, and the interior of the asylum including: offices, kitchen, dining room, workshops, the pharmacy, and other areas.

items.title: Maison de Santé de la Société Française de Bienfaisance Mutuelle logbook, 1903-1908
items.description: Logbook for the French Hospital in San Francisco, with entries spanning the years 1903 to 1908. Each entry contains information about a patient, such as name, nationality, date of entry, doctor, and diagnosis. Includes entries on and around April 18, 1906, when San Francisco suffered a major earthquake and fire.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: A camping party in California, 1887
items.description: A transcript of "A Camping Trip to California" undertaken by four friends: Charles Wheeler and his soon-to-be-bride Lily Marsh, and James de Fremery (driver and photographer of the expedition) and his wife Wilhelmina Suermondt de Fremery over two weeks in the summer of 1887.

items.title: Alice G. Lathrop photograph album, circa 1870-circa 1880
items.description: Photographs, mostly cabinet cards, and one tintype of unidentified friends and family members, taken by San Francisco photographers.

items.title: Amy White photograph album of the American West
items.description: Photo album from the early 1870s commemorating a trip to California with prints by Carleton Watkins, Alfred Hart, Eadweard Muybridge, and others. While there is little known documentation about its creation or provenance beyond the inscription "Amy White, from her brother Howard.

items.title: Anderson family papers, 1848-1963
items.description: The Anderson Family Papers cover the history of a distinguished family that, up to a point, followed a somewhat typical pattern in America. Of Scottish-English origins, with a short history in the Maritime Provinces, Canada, the family came to the United States in the middle of the nineteenth century.

items.title: Brasch family papers, 1891-1920
items.description: Otto and Caroline Brasch had immigrated from Germany sometime during the 1870's and gave encouragement to their children to improve themselves by the writing of letters. Collection consists primarily of letters written by the children of Otto and Caroline Brasch to their brother Frederick E. Brasch.

items.title: Charles A. Gunnison journals, 1881-1887
items.description: Personal diaries of author and poet Charles Andrew Gunnison capturing his daily life in San Francisco, friendship with Timothy Hopkins, and travels in Europe and Asia. The journals include newspaper clippings of his poems and articles printed in the San Francisco Evening Bulletin and Sacramento Record Union.

items.title: Christian K. Binkley, a Biographical Sketch : typescript, 1977-1983
items.description: Biography of Christian K. Binkley [1870-1938], Stanford class of 1899, by his son Charles, briefly discussing his public school teaching career, his attempts at farming in Santa Clara County, and his poetry and writing. Also included is a letter from Sidney Cowell, 1983, regarding the Binkley family and this biography.

items.title: Culver family papers, 1858-1915
items.description: John Oscar Culver, born May 2, 1830, was one of ten children born to tailor James Culver and Kezia [Lee] Culver of Sandy Hill, New York (now Hudson's Falls). James Culver's grandfather, resident in New York and Connecticut, had fought for the Colonies in the Revolutionary War.

items.title: David Locke Webster, "Reminiscences of a Rolling Stone"
items.description: David Locke Webster, professor of physics (1920-1954; emeritus, 1954-1977) and chairman of the Physics Department at Stanford (1920-1942), was born in Boston November 6, 1888. He received his B.A. (1910) and Ph.D. (1913) from Harvard University.

items.title: Diario borrador : Notebook of accounts and special events, 1860-1890
items.description: Cover page states "Tepic, Cal.," but inside on the first and second pages, and on several other pages states "Hacienda de Nueva Almaden;" there are also numerous references to San Jose and Santa Clara.

items.title: Ellen Coit Elliott papers, 1891-1942
items.description: Ellen Coit Elliott, wife of Orrin Leslie Elliott, Stanford University's first registrar, was the author of several books of poetry and an autobiography, IT HAPPENED THIS WAY; AMERICAN SCENE.

items.title: Emil Fischer papers, 1865-1984
items.description: Emil Fischer (October 9, 1852 – July 15, 1919) was a German chemist who won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Emil Fischer's son, Hermann Otto Laurenz Fischer (December 16, 1888 - March 9, 1960) left Nazi Germany in the 1930s and in 1948 became a professor of biochemistry at the University of California Berkeley.

items.title: Frank Shay, "A lifetime in California, 1860-1939" typescript
items.description: California reporter and attorney. Growing up in California, Shay served in a wide variety of positions throughout his life, including special reporter for Sacramento and Virginia City newspapers, accountant and telegrapher for the Sutro Tunnel Company, and, after completing his law degree at Hastings Law College…

items.title: Gilbert Russell Jones photograph album, 1894-1935
items.description: Gilbert R. Jones attended Stanford University during 1906 and 1907; his career included teaching shop at University High School in Oakland, CA. His brother Kenneth Inskip Jones attended Stanford from 1905-1908; he was Deputy District Attorney for Solano County, CA.

items.title: Handmade keepsake commemorating the golden wedding anniversary of Mary Kellogg Crittenden and Timothy Hopkins
items.description: Timothy Hopkins was born in 1859 to an Irish housekeeper who entered the service of the fabulously wealthy Mark Hopkins, one of the four investors who funded the First Transcontinental Railroad.

items.title: Harwood family papers, 1722-1962
items.description: Over his lifetime, Andrew Allen Harwood (1802-1884), great grandson of Benjamin Franklin, kept letters and notes of interest and autographs in a collection known as ODDS & ENDS. He willed it to his grandson, Thomas Triplett Hunter Harwood.

items.title: Isabella Cass diary, 1884-1885
items.description: Diary written during her visit to the Hopkins estate, Sherwood Hall, in Menlo Park, California, with a few entries during her return trip to Massachusetts. Other people mentioned include Jane and Leland Stanford, Mr. and Mrs. Edward C. Burrage, and James C. Flood.

items.title: Leland Stanford papers, 1840-1909
items.description: Leland Stanford was born March 9, 1824 in Watervliet Township, New York. He was admitted to the practice of law in 1848 and married Jane Lathrop in 1850. In 1852, Stanford moved to California where he first worked as a storekeeper in Mother Lode mining camps and later became a successful Sacramento businessman.

items.title: Leland Stanford photograph album, 1868-1882
items.description: Images in the album are largely of Leland Stanford Jr., from the age of 3 months to 14 years; others include one image of Leland Jr. with Jane Stanford, which has been hand colored, and several images of Leland Stanford Sr. In addition there is one image of Wilsie [Wilson] Taylor, a friend of Leland Jr.

items.title: Leland Stanford, Jr. papers, 1871-1893
items.description: Leland Stanford, Jr., the only child of Senator and Mrs. Leland Stanford, was born in Sacramento, California on May 14, 1868. His early death in March 1884 just before his sixteenth birthday inspired the founding of Leland Stanford Junior University in 1885.

items.title: Mildred Crew Brooke: an unfinished manuscript of reminiscences and some extracts from her diary
items.description: Mildred Crew Brooke Hoover (1872-1940) was a California history writer who published "Historic Spots in California" in 1932. She was also the state regent of the Daughters of the American Revolution.

items.title: Minna Stillman diary
items.description: Minna Stillman earned an A.B. in mathematics at Stanford in 1903; she was a document librarian in the Stanford University library. Diary includes entries from a European trip, 1898-99, and an account of the 1906 earthquake, primarily its impact at Stanford University.

items.title: Newcomer family papers, 1850-1972
items.description: A diary or record book of Sidney's life from birth to age 24, kept by his mother, together with other of her papers. Lecture notes that H. Sidney Newcomer kept reflecting pre-World War I mathematics and optics education at the University of Wisconsin. Patents, 1929-1972, awarded to H. Sidney Newcomer.

items.title: Rosemary Benet Dawson collection of material relating to Kathleen Norris and the Norris Ranch, circa 1887-1955
items.description: Collection consists of materials created and compiled by Rosemary Benet Dawson and relating to Kathleen Norris and the Norris Ranch-"La Estancia" in Los Gatos. Rosemary Benet Dawson was daughter of Kathleen's sister Teresa and the poet William Rose Benet.

items.title: Stanford family greeting card collection, 1880-1883
items.description: Collection contains 29 greeting cards, 1880-1883 and undated; photographic reproductions of several cards; and a clipping about the collection, 1982. One card appears to be an Easter greeting, the rest are for Christmas and New Year.

items.title: Stanford family photograph collection, circa 1860-1905
items.description: Primarily studio portraits (mounted albumen prints) of Senator Leland Stanford, Jane Lathrop Stanford, Leland Stanford Jr., Gertrude Stanford, and Elizabeth Stanford. Also includes photographs of President William Harrison with Stanford during Harrison's visit to Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford family scrapbooks. 1865-1894
items.description: Leland Stanford was born March 9, 1824 in Watervliet Township, New York. He married Jane Lathrop in 1850 and on May 14, 1868, Jane and Leland's only child was born in Sacramento, California. Leland, Jr. died March 13, 1884 at the age of 15 years, 10 months. Family scrapbooks, compiled for the Stanford family.

items.title: Steinerson family photograph album, circa 1890-circa 1905
items.description: Images in this album include family portraits, houses, parades, cars, trains, the Monterey mission, Clermont (Iowa), San Francisco scenes, Stanford University buildings, and the Troy Laundry wagon (San Jose, Calif.).

items.title: Student cross country travel : photograph albums, ca. 1893
items.description: Two uncaptioned photo albums and some loose prints chronicling the travels and university studies of a student or group of students. Apparently setting out from the east coast on his way to Stanford, the photographer includes photos of Harvard University, New England, the grave markers of famous writers, Yellowstone…

items.title: Thomas M. Williams papers
items.description: Stanford Class of 1897. Williams earned his MD at Columbia College of Physicians and Surgeons in 1901. He was one of Palo Alto's first physicians, establishing his practice there in 1904; he continued a close affiliation with Stanford, serving on its Board of Athletic Control from 1916 to 1928.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: [Cabinet card of an unidentified Chinese American man].
items.description: Photographer's stamp on back.

items.title: Certificates of residence for Chinese laborers, 1894-1897
items.description: Under the provisions of the 1892 Geary Act, which amended the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, all Chinese in the United States were required to apply for, obtain, and carry a government-issued certificate of residence proving their legal presence in the United States.

items.title: Dennis J. Oliver and family diaries, 1848-1898
items.description: Dennis J. Oliver was born in Galway, Ireland, circa 1823, and emigrated to New York as a young man. There he married Bridget McGlynn on May 11, 1848, and for awhile was in partnership with her brother, John A. McGlynn, in the paint business.

items.title: Early ephemera of Japanese-Americans in Pasadena and Menlo Park California, 1906-1923
items.description: Frank Kurananga opened a successful Japanese art and curio business in Pasadena in 1903, soon expanding into a lavish restaurant and tea room. After overcoming racist roadblocks, he was bankrupted by the earthquake in San Francisco, where he had heavy investments.

items.title: Kenneth Kann papers and oral histories relating to the Petaluma (CA) Jewish chicken ranchers and egg farmers and the life of Joe Rapoport, circa 1970-1995
items.description: Kenneth Kann (1944-) was raised in the East European Jewish immigrant community of Chicago and attended the University of Wisconsin, Madison, during the 1960s. He completed a PhD in modern US history at the University of California, Berkeley in 1977.

items.title: Walter and Emma Fong collection, 1889-2001 (inclusive), 1889-1928 (bulk)
items.description: Walter Ngon Fong (1866-1906) and Emma Fong Kuno nee Howse (1873-1948) met at Stanford University and were married in Colorado, as interracial marriage was prohibited under California Law.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Augustus Taber Murray papers, 1900-1940
items.description: Augustus Taber Murray was a professor of classical literature at Stanford (1892-1932; emeritus, 1932-1940) and member of the Society of Friends. Contents include manuscript lectures and sermons, notes and newsclippings about Professor Murray, and correspondence with Herbert Hoover regarding Murray's Service as Head of…

items.title: College Park Association of Friends records [photocopy], 1889-1936
items.description: The College Park Association of Friends was located in San Jose, California. Joel Bean (1825-1914) was a Quaker minister and school teacher and a founder in 1889 of the College Park Association of Friends. Collection includes records from the semi-annual meetings of the Association, 1889-1936.

items.title: Dedication ceremonies, Odd Fellows Home, Los Gatos, California : panorama photograph, 1912 May 15.
items.description: Photo depicts Odd Fellows in parade uniform and a large group of people and dignitaries in front of the new Spanish-style Odd Fellows Home. The building still stand at 14500 Fruitvale Avenue, Saratoga, and is the center-piece for the Saratoga Retirement, still owned by the Odd Fellows.

items.title: Essays on spiritualism written for THE SARATOGA SENTINEL, 1878-1888
items.description: New York medical doctor, a spiritualist. Newspaper clippings and one manuscript written by King, together with published responses primarily by William H. Tiffany bound in a scrapbook kept by King.

items.title: Membership documents for the National Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution, 1896
items.description: One document appoints her an approved member of the national society by virtue of her descent from William Russell, who "with unfailing loyalty rendered material aid to the cause of American Independence as a Brigadier General during the Revolutionary War." The other document appoints Mrs. Leib as Chapter Regent of…

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: Edward Otho Cresap Ord letters, 1854-1885
items.description: Letters written by Ord to his wife during the period when Ord was on a survey of the Pacific Coast, including descriptions of the region, details of incidents and problems relating to the survey, Indian campaigns, and other matters relating to the West Coast.

items.title: W. F. Henry photograph of Mare Island (California) explosion, 1901 June 5
items.description: On June 5, 1901, about three-hundred pounds of black powder stored at the Mare Island Naval Ammunition Depot exploded.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: 1893 Santa Clara County, CA Index Poll Tax List & Sheriff's Register of Actions; 1895 Santa Clara County, CA Sheriff's Register of Actions #9
items.description: Collection consists of 2 volumes: 1893 Santa Clara County, CA Index Poll Tax List & Sheriff's Register of Actions; 1895 Santa Clara County, CA Sheriff's Register of Actions #9.

items.title: Chester Francis Noble scrapbook, 1899-1939 (inclusive), 1910-1939 (bulk)
items.description: Chester Francis Noble was appointed Chief of Police of the City of Palo Alto in January 1910, a position he held through June of 1924. He died in 1939.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Politics and elections

items.title: A native daughter's leadership in public affairs : oral history transcript, 1974. With an introduction by Winifred Heard
items.description: Interviews conducted 1974 by Gabrielle Morris for the Regional Oral History Office, Bancroft Library. Introduction by Winifred Heard. Copies of photographs and documentary material included. Recollections of growing up in Berkeley; student days at University of California, 1914-1918.

items.title: Searsville precinct (San Mateo County, Calif.) : Great Register, 1896-1899
items.description: Voting register, listing occupation, age, height (and other physical characteristics), country of birth, town of residence, ability to read and write, and if departed, destination.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history

items.title: [Nine pamphlets from the pen of C. E. Pickett presented to Leland Stanford by the author]
items.description: Binder's title.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Advertising and marketing

items.title: Contract for painted bulletin or wall display, 1922
items.description: The correspondence and contract are with the Merchants' Association of San Jose.

items.title: Crate, can, and bottle label collection, circa 1920s-1940s
items.description: Comprises crate, can, and bottle labels, the bulk of which were designed and created between the 1920s and 1940s by San Francisco and Los Angeles lithography companies.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Aerospace and defence

items.title: [Chinese-American pilot Wallace S. Chinn in Redwood City, California] [graphic].
items.description: A picture apparently taken at the airfield at Redwood City, California, in operation from 1915 until the 1930s as site of a School of Aviation then owned by World War I flying ace Walter Varney, an aviation pioneer who later founded a company that evolved into United Airlines.

items.title: Alfred S. Niles and Joseph S. Newell, Airplane Structures, typescript, circa 1928
items.description: Alfred S. Niles was professor of aeronautic engineering at Stanford University from 1927 until his retirement in 1959. In 1929 the first edition of Airplane Structures by Alfred S. Niles and Joseph S. Newell was published by John Wiley & Sons.

items.title: Charles Froesch papers, 1906-2023 (inclusive) 1906-1982 (bulk)
items.description: This collection consists of manuscript, printed, and photographic materials created by and related to aeronautical engineer Charles Froesch (1896-1982), and his career in the aviation industry.

items.title: David Richard David papers, ca. 1934-1945
items.description: Included are Davis's original papers and photographs for the innovative airfoil he theorized, designed, uniquely tested and finally patented. Known as the Davis Wing, it bettered performance by 20% and was used by Consolidated in production of their PBY-5 Catalina and Liberator B-24's - outstanding long-range bombers…

items.title: Elliott Reid papers, 1924-1966
items.description: Professor of aeronautics at Stanford (1929-1965). Reid was the author of APPLIED WING THEORY, 1932, and many technical papers published by the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics.

items.title: Irmgard Flugge-Lotz, Collector, Technical reports and papers, 1929-1984 (inclusive), 1929-1945 (bulk)
items.description: Irmgard Flugge-Lotz was professor of engineering at Stanford from 1949 until her retirement in 1968. Born in Germany, Dr. Flugge-Lotz earned her Doctor of Engineering degree at the Technical University of Hanover.

items.title: Leonard Eugene Root papers, 1923-1983
items.description: Leonard Eugene Root was born in Lewiston, Idaho on July 4, 1910. He spent his school years in Stockton, California, and then attended the College of the Pacific, receiving his Bachelor of Arts in Engineering and Mathematics in 1932.

items.title: Letters patent, 1938-1939
items.description: These are patents for foil for passage through a fluid (Great Britain, 9 May 1938) and improvements in fluid foil (France, 21 Apr. 1939).

items.title: Nicholas J. Hoff papers, 1903-1997 (inclusive), 1940-1997 (bulk)
items.description: Nicholas J. Hoff was a professor emeritus of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University at the time of his death in 1997. Born on Jan. 3, 1906 in the small town of Magyarovar in western Hungary, he came to Stanford in 1939 for graduate work and earned his Ph.D. in 1942.

items.title: Preliminary design of an experimental world-circling spaceship, 1946 May 2.
items.description: This report presents an engineering analysis of the possibilities of designing a man-made satellite. The question of power plants, structural weights, multiple stages, optimum design values, trajectories, stability, and landing are considered in detail.

items.title: The Grapevine : newspaper
items.description: This edition (vol. X, No.23) contains articles about the Mare Island shipyard dealing with safety issues, better tool performance and training activities.

items.title: William Frederick Durand papers, 1876-1979
items.description: William F. Durand, known as the Dean of American engineering, joined the Stanford University faculty in 1904, serving as professor and head of the Mechanical Engineering Department until his retirement at age 65 in 1924; he held the position of Professor Emeritus until 1958.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Business organizations

items.title: Riding the high-tech boom: the American Electronics Association story, 1943-1990, c. 1991
items.description: In addition to the above article, Mr. Elkind has collected various clippings, pamphlets, etc. concerning the history of the electronics industry.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computer hardware

items.title: Moore School of Electrical Engineering, Bell Telephone Laboratories, RCA Research and Engineering : RADIO-CRAFT archive, 1937-1938
items.description: An archive of six original photographs, fifteen letters, four scientific papers, one typescript of a article for RADIO-CRAFT and one news clipping, all related to three early electro-mechanical equation solving analog computers.--vendor.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Construction and civil engineering practice

items.title: Guy F. Atkinson Company records, ca. 1921-1961
items.description: The Guy F. Atkinson Company is a construction and engineering firm founded in 1926 that specializes in civil projects such as dams, tunnels, and roadbuilding. The records of a civil engineering and construction firm, spanning approximately 1921 to 1961.

items.title: Harold W. Burke papers, 1945-1985
items.description: Harold W. Burke was an engineering geologist, with particular interest in structural geology, limestone problems, and small hydroelectrics. He did field work around the world in evaluation of foundation problems, particularly for dams and tunnels.

items.title: John Kiely papers, circa 1945-1977
items.description: Project management files, personal project files, and correspondence documenting John Kiely's years as Vice-President of Bechtel Corporation's Power Division, mostly in the late 1940s-early 50s.

items.title: Palmer and McBryde papers, 1921-1927
items.description: Construction firm, San Francisco. Correspondence, contracts, bills and estimates relating to Palmer and McBryde's construction of the Stanford Stadium (1921) and reconstruction of the stadium stands (1925, 1927).

items.title: Snyder Company records, 1912-1929
items.description: Records include specifications and calculations, estimates, correspondence, engineering drawings, charts, reports, and photographs pertaining to banks, schools, factories, and other commercial buildings.

items.title: William Bruce McMillan papers, 1905-2014 1920-1946 (bulk)
items.description: William Bruce McMillan received his Bachelors and Engineers degrees from Stanford in 1911 and 1912. His father, John G. McMillan, served as the county eningeer of Santa Clara County for 24 years.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Electronics industry (national and international)

items.title: Billy Malone, "The Early History of the Magnavox Company"
items.description: One of the founders of the Magnavox Company was Edwin S. Pridham, who graduated from Stanford University in May 1909 with an a.b. in physics. Prior to the founding of Magnavox in March 1911, Pridham worked with Cyril Elwell, a 1907 Stanford graduate, on his wireless radio transmitter in Palo Alto.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Cours supérieur de tissage. École de la Salle
items.description: An exceptional technical handbook written in a student's neat calligraphic hand for textile-weaving courses, taught in Lyon at the École de la Salles by professors Brocard and Granger. The volume is richly decorated with a numerous drawings and 137 original fabric samples.

items.title: Eloesser-Heynemann Co. records, 1860-1972
items.description: The origins of Eloesser-Heymann Co. dates back to 1851 when Leonard D. Heynemann, an immigrant from Hamburg, realized there was a future in providing supplies to the miners who flocked to San Francisco and Sacramento as part of the California Gold Rush.

items.title: General Cable Corporation and Hoover Dam photo album
items.description: This collections consists of approximately 282 black and white photographs depicting the General Cable Corporation factory(ies) used to manufacture the power transmission lines for the Hoover Dam.

items.title: George P. Hurst collection of Risdon Iron Works and Union Iron Works records, circa 1890-1980
items.description: "In 1897 the Risdon Iron Works, adjoining the Union Iron Works and soon to merge with it, built the first successful gold dredge in America. It was called the Archimedes and was designed by and built for R. H. Postlethwaite, chief dredging engineer for the Risdon Iron Works, who operated it in the Yuba River east of…

items.title: Gladding, McBean and Company account book
items.description: Gladding, McBean and Company is a California firm that manufactures clay roofing tiles. Photocopy of contract book with brief entries on building, location, owner, architect, material, and amount; included are entries pertaining to buildings on the Stanford University campus.

items.title: History of Industrial Engineers, Inc. typescript
items.description: Rifenberick earned his A.B. in mechanical engineering at Stanford University in 1917 and his engineer's degree in 1919. Typescript history (written between 1953 and 1974) of the engineering company founded in 1933 by four Stanford alumni: F. L. Kallam, Gregory H. Lifur, William L. Rifenberick, and Angelo F. Semino.

items.title: Joseph D. Eisenstadt collection of Ran Battery Company documents, ca. 1930-1989
items.description: Joseph D. Eisenstadt (later Ardon) founded Ran, the Palestine and Israeli Battery company which was the predecessor of the Israeli electronics and military communications equipment firm Tadiran. Founded in 1932, Ran was the only battery manufacturer at that time in the Middle East.

items.title: Joshua Hendy Machine Works Articles of Incorporation and minutes of the proceedings of the board of directors : ledger, 1882-1909
Ralph Harrison Sherry papers, 1907-1953
items.description: Sherry earned his a.b. in chemistry at Stanford University, 1904, and his M.A. in 1905; he was a metallurgical engineer. Papers consist primarily of charts, drawings, illustrations, and photographs used in his book STEEL TREATING PRACTICE, published in 1929.

items.title: Stauffer Chemical Company records, 1881-1987
items.description: The Stauffer Chemical Company was founded in 1885 in San Francisco by two European immigrants, John Stauffer, Sr. and Christian de Guigne. The company mainly produced herbicides for corn and rice. The Stauffer Chemical Company records consists of materials documenting the company's activities.

items.title: Welton J. Crook, "Linotype metal. Part I, Preliminary study, experimental alloys, methods of manufacture" typescript
items.description: Welton J. Crook earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford in 1911 and his engineer's degree in 1919. He joined the Stanford faculty in the Department of Mining and Metallurgy in 1921. Includes bibliographical references and photographs.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: [Workers at Hickmott Canning Company in Oakland, California]
items.description: Occupational photograph showing male and female workers at Hickmott Canning Company, in which some affectionately hold hands and/or have their arms draped around each other's shoulders.

items.title: Bracero Oral History interviews
items.description: Includes thumb drive and several documents and photographs in connection with Ornelas Bracero Oral History Project.

items.title: C. Lyn Fox papers pertaining to the Longshoremen's strike and the Pacific Coast maritime strike, 1934-1937
items.description: C. Lyn Fox was assistant to Thomas G. Plant, the President of the Waterfront Employer's Union, and wrote news memoranda for the president, 1935-1936. Assistant to the President of the Waterfront Employer's Union, Thomas G. Plant. Wrote news memoranda for the president, 1935-1936.

items.title: Charles Batom papers, 1944-1975
items.description: Mr. Batom was an African American union member and a member of civil rights organizations. He lived in Oakland, California. Includes union items.

items.title: Eric Hakon Thomsen papers, 1936-1941
items.description: Correspondence with John Steinbeck, 1936-1940, including 3 cards, 4 letters, and 1 telegram from Steinbeck to Thomsen, 2 letters from Carol Steinbeck to Thomsen, and carbons of 2 letters from Thomsen to Steinbeck. Letters make reference to the migrant camps and both Tom Collins and Ray Strong.

items.title: Herbert Gregory Prichard diary recording labor strife and the shipbuilding industry in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1918-1919
items.description: The diary records first-hand observation and eyewitness accounts of the coal strikes and ensuing violence that occurred in the San Francisco Bay Area in the early 1900's.

items.title: International Longshoremen's Association Local 38-79 member Arthur Otto Tallaksen records, 1918-1948
items.description: Arthur Otto Tallaksen was a Norwegian longshoremen. He was born in Kristiansand, Norway around 1902, emigrated to the United States and became a naturalized citizen in 1922. This collection consists of materials documenting Arthur Otto Tallaksen.

items.title: Letter from Guernsey Frazer as Executive Secretary, Associated Farmers of California, San Francisco, to John T. Mills, Taylor Bates & Co., 48 Wall Street, New York
items.description: Frazer charged that "Madame Secretary Perkins" - Franklin Roosevelt's Secretary of Labor Frances Perkins, the first woman appointed to a presidential Cabinet post - had "deliberately overruled the uniform line of court decisions to protect Communists, radicals, 'pinks' and similar vermin" by refusing to deport…

items.title: Operating force, Travers and Sakata, 1933 [graphic]
items.description: Documentary photographic portrait of the workforce for a California grower at the end of the season, with 61 women and 74 men-all Caucasian-and in the center, Kyusaburo [Harry] Sakata, a Japanese immigrant who was the co-owner of the operation.

items.title: Oral history interview with Gallagher on the I.W.W. and Tom Mooney by Willa Klug Baum
Papers pertaining to the Mooney case, 1916-1933
items.description: Manuscripts, typescripts, notes, press releases, pamphlets, newspaper clippings, and ephemera related to the Mooney case, likely created or collected by San Francisco Chronicle political editor Earl C. Behrens.

items.title: Spiders in the house and workers in the field : Video interview transcript, 1971 Mar. 1.
items.description: Galarza discusses Mexican American labor history, leading up to Joseph DiGiorgio and the DiGiorgio Fruit Corporation and the union organizing and strike attempts in 1949-1950. He discusses the bracero program, illegal immigration of Mexicans, and the political maneuvering to break the strike.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Magnetic recording and data storage

items.title: Bell Labs Early Stereo Collection
items.description: The Philadelphia Orchestra conducted by Leopold Stokowski began performing live on NBC's radio network in 1929, but Stokowski was unhappy with the fidelity of these early broadcasts, and approached physicist Harvey Fletcher at Bell Laboratories seeking ways to improve the transmissions.

items.title: William Slatkin papers, circa 1940-2019
items.description: Materials related to the history of Ampex Corporation. Includes documents, photocopies, audio recordings of interviews with former Ampex executives and engineers, and a set of Ampex annual reports. Some of this material has been posted online as The Ampex Story website: www.theampexstory.com.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: 600-foot tower design for Federal Telegraph Co. : blueprints and typescript, 1912
[New England Telephone and Telegraph Company infrastructure photograph album] [graphic]
items.description: A photograph album consiting of more than one hundred 7 1/2 x 11 inch photographs each mounted on linen. The photographs are divided into sections, each under a different tab. Each section of photographs is preceded with a financial page noting the value of the infrastructure being documented.

items.title: Donald MacQuivey papers, circa 1950-1990
items.description: Donald R. MacQuivey (1913-1993) was an engineer and policy analyst in the field of telecommunications. He received several degrees from Stanford University, among them Radio Engineering in 1935, Electrical Engineering in 1939, and an MBA in 1942.

items.title: Guglielmo Marconi postcards, 1912-1913
items.description: Collection consists of 5 Guglielmo Marconi postcards from Italy.

items.title: Laying the first Pacific cable : diaries of cable engineer Henry Clifford on the ships Colonia and Anglia, 1902-1903
items.description: The diaries begin with joining the Anglia at Greenwich on January 7, 1902, and from there on there is a daily record of the voyage to Brisbane where the first leg - from Southport to Norfolk Island - begins. Here they had to build the station while the New Zealand and Fiji branches of the cable were laid.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: Baird Television : sales brochure, 1939
items.description: Describes and illustrateds different models, and describes why Baird televisions are better than the competitors.

items.title: Baird Television Limited reports and brochures, 1931-1939
items.description: "Report Of The Directors", "Statement Of Accounts "and other information provided to the shareholders.

items.description: Eitel-McCullough Inc. was founded in 1934 by radio engineers and business partners, Bill Eitel and Jack McCullough in San Bruno, California. The company started out developing innovative radio vacuum tubes that provided higher frequency transmission for radio communication and eventually transitioned into components…

items.title: Cyril Frank Elwell papers, 1930-1961
items.description: Cyril Frank Elwell (1884 – 1963) was an American inventor and pioneer in the development of radio-telegraphy and long-distance communication. Born in Melbourne, Australia in 1884 to an American father and a German mother, Elwell arrived in the United States in 1902.

items.title: Don Preist papers, circa 1934-2002
items.description: Donald Harold Preist, born in England in 1916, first became associated with various aspects of radar development in the late 1930s when conducting early experiments on the detection of ships and the development of high-power ground radar transmitters.

items.title: Eimac News, 1942-1961
items.description: Publication of the Eimac company featuring employees, events, and engineering activities at their San Bruno, California and Salt Lake City, Utah plants. Some years are incomplete.

items.title: Ervin J. Nalos papers, 1939-1993
items.description: Ervin J. Nalos, a naturalized United States citizen, was born September 10, 1924 in Prague. Dr. Nalos' undergraduate study was done at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, B.A. Sc., 1946. Graduate work, M.A. Sc., 1947, was also started in Vancouver.

items.title: Federal telegraph company : photographs
items.description: Early 20th century photographs depict the first Poulsen arc from Denmark; a wireless telephone station; generators and cabinets; interior and exterior views of various telegraph stations in the United States, Ireland and England; and construction sites for new stations.

items.title: Herbert B. Van Etten papers, 1912-1947
items.description: Notebook with diagrams and explanations of the development of the audion amplifier and oscillator, indexed, 1912. Record of patent infringement lawsuits, ca. 1933, with published record of notebook contents. "Federal Telephone and Radio Corporation : a Historical Review, 1909-1946" in ELECTRICAL COMMUNICATION, 1946.

items.title: His Master's Voice Television : sales brochure, 1937
Jack McCullough interview by Robert Herdman and Jack Strother, 25 Nov. 1997

items.title: Karl R. Spangenberg papers, 1935-1961
items.description: Karl Spangenberg (1910-1964) served as a Professor of Electrical Engineering at Stanford. He was a member of the American Physical Society and became an IRE (now IEEE) Associate in 1934, Senior Member in 1945, and Fellow in 1949.

items.title: Lester L. Libby papers, ca. 1936-1984
items.description: Lester Louis Libby was born at Hartford, Connecticut in 1914. He received the B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical engineering from the Worcester Polytechnic Institute in 1935 and 1936, respectively.

items.title: Marvin Chodorow papers, 1929-1993 (inclusive), 1943-1974 (bulk)

items.title: Oral history transcription, 21 Jan. 1974

items.title: Osram Valves : The Baird Televisor [diagram]

items.title: Ralph M. Hare photograph album and typescript documenting life at a wireless station in the Farallon Islands, 1910-1974, bulk 1918-1919

items.title: RCA's Farnsworth Patent File, 1930 : a collection of documents and manuscripts

Educated at Stanford University, physicist and inventor Russell Varian began his career with Philo Farnsworth on early television technology and with Humble Oil on instrumentation…

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Physics, correspondence, 1937-1949
