items.title: California : San Jose quadrangle
items.description: "Stanford Geological Survey Summer 1923" and "8/25/23" written in ink at top.

items.title: Fifty vara survey, 1909
items.description: Shows "the position of street monuments, monument line ties, and street and monument ties. Prepared by direction of the Board of Supervisors under resolution No. 1764 (new series), October 12 1908. Marsden Manson, City Engineer, and Charles H. Holcomb, Asst. City Engineer." [From the title page map].

items.title: Greystone area geology and topography
items.description: Relief shown by contours and spot heights. No. 2-5 include section. Pen-and-ink. Five versions of the same map. Covers quarry area, source of sandstone for Stanford University buildings. Accompanied by field notebooks. Branner set includes blueprint copies of no. 2, 4 and 5, and photocopies on cloth of no. 4 and 5.

items.title: Hollister, Quien Sabe, Gonzales, San Benito 15' quadrangles
items.description: "1924 SGS" on upper left of back of map.

items.title: Map of the Ormondale Ranch : situated in San Mateo County, California
items.description: Includes a second copy of the above, enlarged to approximately 1 inch = 400 feet. Property is adjacent of Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve. Relief shown by contours (interval 10 ft.) and spot heights. General vegetation, with actual acreage amounts shown, and percentages in various tracts. Tracts 1 and 3, Home Farm.

items.title: Quarry area geology and topography
items.description: Relief shown by contours and spot heights. No. 2-3 include section. Pen-and-ink. Three versions of the same map. Covers Greystone and Greystone Quarry areas, source of sandstone for Stanford University buildings.

items.title: San Francisquito and Corte Madera Creeks (Santa Clara County) : surveys and notes, ca. 1900
items.description: Includes, among others, lands belonging to Spring Valley Water Company, Manzanita Water Company, Leland Stanford, W.A. Newell, Morris Doyle, and Cornelius O'Conner.

items.title: The areal geology of the Livermore region
items.description: Print includes legend.

items.title: Topography : California, Morgan Hill quadrangle
items.description: "Reconnaissance" and "Stanford Geological Survey 1923" written in pen at top.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: [Pamphlet material on bus transportation]
items.description: Tile supplied by the cataloger.

items.title: [Pamphlet material on motor vehicle accidents].
items.description: Title supplied by the cataloger.

items.title: Bridges : miscellaneous pamphlet collection originally part of the Hopkins Transportation Collection, 1928-1951
items.description: Includes pamphlets produced about various bridges and bridge engineers.

items.title: Charles D. Marx Correspondence Regarding Bridges
items.description: Charles D. Marx was professor of civil engineering at Stanford University from its founding in 1891 to his retirement in 1923. After his retirement he was a consultant on many engineering projects, including serving on the technical board of the San Francisco-Alameda County Bridge Commission.

items.title: Collection of photographs related to the construction of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge
items.description: This collection consists of photographic materials showing the construction of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, in California. The materials include 11 albums containing approximately 1,050 gelatin silver prints (1934-1936) showing various aspects of bridge construction and a separate group of 52 photographs and…

items.title: Construction of the Golden Gate Bridge : photograph album, 1938-1939
items.description: The photographs were probably taken by a construction worker.

items.title: Farallon Islands photographic negatives
items.description: No documentation accompanied the collection, which was purchased from a dealer. A few of the images have circulated previously, particularly that of lighthouse keeper Charles S. Kaneen and family.

items.title: George E. Tillitson collection on railroads, 1880-1940
items.description: Collection contains outlines of corporate histories of railroads in the United States and Canada including some streetcar lines and electric interurban lines. Includes dates of incorporation, lists of points served, lists of mileage, time schedules, maps of lines, and lists or reports of accidents.

items.title: Golden Gate Bridge : daily calendar and related material, 1919-1962
items.description: This material was once a part of the Keesling papers (M0100) now held by Stanford, however it had become separated from the bulk of the papers before they came to Stanford. There is related material in M0100 boxes 61-68.

items.title: Golden Gate Bridge : photographs, publications, and clippings, 1930-1992
items.description: Includes the book THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE, report of the Chief Engineer to the Board of Directors of the Golden Gate Bridge and Highway District, California, 1937. Also, THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE, transactions of the Commonwealth Club of California, vol. xxv, #9, 1930.

items.title: Golden Gate Bridge photographs
items.description: Photographic documentation by Standard Oil Company of California of the building of The Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco (Calif.).

items.title: Hopkins transportation collection photographs, 1870-1964 (bulk 1877-1943)
items.description: Photograph collection containing various accessions of original and copy prints depicting railroads, street cars, airplanes, automobiles, and other forms of transportation. Material was formerly part of the Hopkins Transportation Library.

items.title: James Reed papers, 1907-1941
items.description: James Reed was a graduate of the United States Naval Academy and of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. As an officer of the Naval Construction Corps, he served at the Philadelphia, Puget Sound, and Mare Island Navy Yards, specializing in management and labor problems.

items.title: Joseph Strauss bridge plans, 1905-1935
items.description: Joseph Baermann Strauss (1870-1938) was an American structural engineer who revolutionized the design of bascule bridges. Strauss held numerous patents for bascule bridges, including his major innovation of using concrete counterweights coupled with a series of linkages to balance the moveable span.

items.title: Newsclipping collection, 1890-1952
items.description: The collection was probably assembled by the Transportation Librarian; the newspapers are primarily local (Palo Alto times, San Francisco Chronicle, and San Francisco Examiner), but the Tacoma News Tribune is also represented so it is assumed other people were sending in material to the library.

items.title: Railroad passes issued by and to C.H. Redington, 1873-1924
items.description: Redington received passes from many railroad companies, both before and after his retirement as Assistant Treasurer for the Southern Pacific Company.

items.title: Railroad timetables and other printed ephemera, 1838-1946
items.description: Includes timetables for the New England states (The Pathfinder Railway Guide, (1849-1854 & 1896), the west coast.

items.title: Randolph Brandt collection of photographs
items.description: Approximately 60 prints collected by Randolph Brandt depicting transportation and other subjects in California, especially railroads and street cars.

items.title: San Francisco Bay Bridge Collection, 1933-1939
items.description: Box 1 contains newsclippings, 1934-1936; box 2 contains annual progress reports, 1934-1939, and an account of the ground breaking ceremony, 1933. The progress reports contain numerous photogrpahs, and some maps and drawings.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley Interurbans, An Oral History by One who Remembers it Well
items.description: Rixford Snyder was a professor of history at Stanford University. Photocopies of photographs, illustrations, and articles with additional text by Snyder, concerning the Peninsular Railway, the electric trolley that ran between San Jose and Palo Alto, California, passing through Stanford University.

items.title: Ted Huggins photographs of the Golden Gate Bridge
items.description: Theodore (or Ted) Huggins, was a public relations executive at Standard Oil Company of California and an amateur photographer who convinced his superiors to let him document the building of the Golden Gate Bridge.

items.title: The Golden Gate Bridge leading to Marin County and the redwood empire : photoengraving, nd.
items.description: View of Golden Gate Bridge spanning the bay, direction towards Marin County.

items.title: University Avenue Underpass Project records
items.description: The University Avenue Underpass Project is the reprinting of a series of photographs taken in 1939 and 1941, before and after the construction of the underpass that connects downtown Palo Alto and Stanford University. Collection includes sets 29, 35, and 81, along with a text page explaining the project.

items.title: Waldemar F. Dietrich Mountain railroad electrification in California report
items.description: Waldemar Fenn Dietrich earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford University in 1913 and his engineer's degree in 1914; he was professor of mining engineering at Stanford, 1916-30.

items.title: William Gardiner transportation collection, 1869-1951
items.description: Collection of photographs and research material concerning railroads, street cars and other public transportation in and around Oakland and Berkeley, California from historian, collector and local railway employee William Everard Gardiner (1869-1949).

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: [Topography of part of southern Santa Clara County, Calif [cartographic material] : from Edenvale to Rucker along Coyote River].
items.description: Coordinates approximate. Relief shown by contours and hachures. Shows Southern Pacific Railroad tracks, proposed dam, waterways, Bay Cities Water Company, Spring Valley Water Company. Canals with directional arrows, land divisions, roads. Contour interval 5 ft. Oriented with north toward upper left.

items.title: A report on the underground water supply of Stanford University and vicinity
items.description: Cecil C. Killingsworth and Cooper Hyde were graduate students studying geology at Stanford during the 1930s. A report on the underground water supply of Stanford University and its vicinity from 1932.

items.title: Boulder Dam (aka Hoover Dam) : film of construction, ca. 1936
items.description: Titled "The Construction of the Boulder Dam, 1931-1936," this film was sponsored by the Six Companies, edited by Dowling & Brownell, Hollywood. The film is in black & white and has intertitles and no soundtrack.

items.title: Charles David Marx papers, 1873-1942
items.description: Charles David Marx was one of Stanford's original faculty, the Old Guard. He came to Stanford in 1891 as Professor of Civil Engineering and taught here until his retirement in 1923. He formed close friendships with his students and was affectionately known as Daddy Marx. Marx was born in Ohio in 1857.

items.title: Electrolysis Survey on Treasure Island, 1939 June 16.
items.description: Report "Requested by Mr. Charles H. Lee, Chief of Division of Water Supply and Sanitation." Describes Treasure Island's soil, the various systems on the island (such as water, gas, and sanitary), and describes the results of "tests made to determine the amount of electrical protection necessary to stop [...] leaks…

items.title: Electrolysis Tests on Treasure Island, 1939 June 5.
items.description: Report "Requested by Mr. Charles H. Lee, Chief of Division of Water Supply and Sanitation" on electrical protection installed on Treasure Island's underground pipes. Describes the method of testing and the results.

items.title: Feather River power project : reports, photographs, maps, 1904-1906
items.description: Report, correspondence, photographs (94), and maps (27 with index), relating to a project undertaken for the Western Power Company of Los Angeles (later known as the Great Western Power Company) on the feasibility of creating a large reservoir at Big Meadows, on the North Fork of the Feather River.

items.title: Felt Lake Dam photographs, 1929
items.description: The materials consist of photographs documenting the construction of the Felt Lake Dam.

items.title: Joseph W. Gross research collection pertaining to water supply/control and flooding in California, 1890-1940
items.description: Joseph Watson Gross was a graduate from the University of California in 1907 and majored in Sanitary and Irrigation Engineering. He had a long career specializing as a "municipal and reclamation" engineer.

items.title: Mill creek flood control project : photograph collection, 1939-1942
items.description: 44 cardboard sheets mounted with 138 black and white photographs. Images include personnel, work crews, equipment, aerial views, a few accidents, and site shots, some showing multiple shots of work progression at a specific location. Many of the snapshots are captioned.

items.title: Niles Dam collection
items.description: Niles Dam on Alameda Creek was built in 1887 by the Spring Valley Water Company, at the same site where Jose de Jesus Vallejo had build a dam for his grist mill in 1841. Water from the SVWC dam was diverted to the San Francisco water system. The dam was removed in 2006 as part of the Alameda Creek Restoration Project.

items.title: Report on a Coast Stream Water Supply for the Palo Alto Water District
items.description: Preliminary report showing the feasibility of a coast stream water supply for the Palo Alto Water Disctrict.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection
items.description: The Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection are materials owned and selected for digitization by the Santa Clara Valley Water District. The materials are related to water resources management in Santa Clara County, California dating in the early 1900s.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley water supply photographs, 1935-1938
items.description: The photographs depict the building of California dams. There is also one set of photographs of Wrightsville, a reservoir in Vermont. The original organization by envelope is retained. Webbs Photo Supply Store in San Jose did the photo finishing (except for Wrightsville).

items.title: William W. Helbush collection of water project records
items.description: William W. Helbush (circa 1895-1965) served as an engineer for the San Francisco Department of Public Works. During the 1930s he worked on the Hetch Hetchy project (1914-1934) and the enlargement of O'Shaughnessy Dam in Yosemite Valley (1934-1938).

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Angelo F. Semino papers, 1856-1986
items.description: Angelo F. Semino received his a.b. in mechanical engineering from Stanford in 1922. Land deeds for property in Mountain View, California (the Mayfield Mall), together with a 79 page typescript about its history. Original typed reports, copies, reprints, and manuscript notes on heat exchanges in the petroleum industry.

items.title: Toichi Domoto papers, ca. 1860-1996
items.description: Toichi Domoto was the son of first generation immigrants from Japan who settled in California. Arriving in 1883, his father and uncle worked first as laborers and within a year were able to lease and then purchase a few acres of land in Oakland, founding the Domoto Brothers Nursery in 1884.

sectors.name: Education and research — Applied physics

items.title: Bloch symposium; a Stanford centennial symposium celebrating the work of Felix Bloch [videorecording]
items.description: Physicist. Excelling in both theoretical and experimental physics, Bloch won the Nobel Prize in 1952 for his work in nuclear magnetism. Bloch was a member of the Physics Department at Stanford University from 1934 until his death in 1983. Tapes from a symposium held on October 27 and 28, 1989, at Stanford University.

items.title: David Locke Webster papers, 1914-1976
items.description: Born in Boston, November 6, 1888, David Locke Webster attended Harvard University, receiving his bachelor's in 1910 and his doctorate three years later, both in physics. While studying at Harvard, Webster also taught as an instructor in mathematics (1909-12) and as an assistant in physics (1911-14).

items.title: Fu Chun Yu lab notebooks [facsimiles], 1949-1950
items.description: Fu Chun Yu, born in Shanghai in 1914, graduated from Peking University in 1936. He came to the United States in 1946 and received his PhD from Ohio State University in 1949; he then came to Stanford to work with physicist Felix Bloch. Yu returned to China in 1951, where he continued his career as professor of physics.

items.title: Nuclear resonance : glass slides, ca. 1945
items.description: Slides show measuring equipment and graphs and measurements.

items.title: Optics and laser spectroscopy, Bell Telephone Laboratories, 1951-1961, and Stanford University since 1961 : oral history transcript / 1998
items.description: Schawlow family background, Depression years in Toronto; early aptitudes in radio engineering; college and university studies in math and physics, and World War II interruption; Malcolm Crawford and thesis research on atomic beam light source; post-doc at Columbia University, 1949-1951.

items.title: Paul Harmon Kirkpatrick autobiography, 1971
items.description: Professor of physics at Stanford University since 1931 (emeritus, 1960 - ); best known for his pioneering work in x-ray technology. General reminiscences about his life, including recollections about his work and colleagues at Stanford. Also includes a bibliography.

sectors.name: Education and research — Campus and student life

items.title: Bernice C. Rowell photographs
items.description: Grandmother grew up in Fresno and attended Stanford in the 1900 to 1905 time frame. The reference to Normal I believe is to teacher's school in San Jose (San Jose State ?). Grandfather Arthur Lowell Dahlgren attended Stanford during this time. He lived in "The Camp" as he was then a poor student.

items.title: Florence Grace Savage photographs, circa 1904-1907
items.description: Florence Mary Grace graduated from Stanford University in 1906 with an A.B. in math; while a student she was a member of the women's basketball team. In 1909 she married Harry King Savage, class of 1907.

items.title: Georgina Rolph scrapbook of her junior year, 1920-1921
items.description: A single scrapbook including mementos from Georgina Rolph's junior year at Castilleja Girls School such as concert programs, notes from friends, photographs, drawings, and more.

items.title: Myron Carlos Burr papers and memorabilia
items.description: Myron C. Burr earned his A.B. in civil engineering at Stanford University in May 1907. In the aftermath of the San Francisco Earthquake in 1906, he served with the Stanford Relief Corps and the San Francisco Water Commission.

items.title: Robert Jerome Snyder photographs, 1928
items.description: Robert Jerome Snyder earned an AB in economics at Stanford University in 1929. Collection consists of two scrapbook pages of photographs and one illustration of football players, Coach Thornhill, and the construction of the Big Game bonfire, with one image of Herbert Hoover and family in front of the Hoover home on…

items.title: Stanford Amateur Radio Club scrapbook, 1941-1957
items.description: The "ham radio" station W6YX at Stanford dates back to 1924 and is still active; electronics professor Oswald G. Villard Jr. served as faculty advisor and trustee for many years.

items.title: Student photograph album, 1889-circa 1930 (inclusive), 1905-1906 (bulk)
items.description: Album, possibly kept by John Stephens Martin, with photographs of athletic players and games (football and baseball), dormitory rooms, and groups of male students, ca. 1905-1906; most of the athletic uniforms have a "B" or "Belmont" on them, probably representing the Belmont School in Belmnont, Calif.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: Frank George Baum, "The Transformer" galleys
items.description: Baum earned his engineering degree at Stanford University in 1898; he was assistant professor of electrical engineering at Stanford from 1898 to 1903. Galleys (incomplete) from his book, THE ALTERNATING CURRENT TRANSFORMER , with his corrections and annotations.

items.title: Frederick Emmons Terman papers, 1901-1978
items.description: Chronology 1900 Born in English, Indiana on June 7, son of Lewis Madison and Anna Belle Minton Terman. 1905 Moves with family from Indiana to California. 1910 Settles permanently at Stanford when Lewis Terman joins Stanford Education Department faculty. 1914 Begins experimenting with radio as a "ham" operator.

items.title: Harris J. Ryan papers, 1908-1934
items.description: Harris J. Ryan was a professor of electrical engineering at Stanford (1905-1931; emeritus, 1931-1934), head of the Department of Electrical Engineering and first director of the Ryan High Voltage Laboratory.

items.title: Max C. Yost report on Stanford engineering curricula
items.description: Max C. Yost earned his BS in mechanical engineering at Stanford in 1952. Collection consists of tables compiled by Yost comparing engineering requirements for his years at Stanford (1944-1952), the Pioneer Class (entered 1891, graduated 1895), and the academic year 1996/97.

items.title: Principles of Electrical Engineering : 32 weekly parts
items.description: Experiments designed to illustrate fundamental points of electrical science.

items.title: Report on the proposed Electrical Engineering Laboratory of Sibley College, Cornell University, 1904-1905
Stephen Timoshenko papers, 1907-1996 (inclusive), 1921-1970 (bulk)
items.description: Stephen Prokofievitch Timoshenko, a world-renowned authority on theoretical and applied mechanics, was educated at the Munich Polytechnic Institute and at the University of Gottingen. Correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, galleys, notes, reprints, photographs, passports, awards, and other items.

sectors.name: Education and research — Library, archival and information services

items.title: Herbert Hoover letter to Frank A. Golder, 1924
items.description: Hoover, Stanford University Trustee, founded the Hoover War Library at Stanford in 1919. Letter from Hoover to Frank A. Golder, director of the Hoover War Library, indicating the forwarding of documents relating to the history of the Library.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Castilleja School, 1907-1940
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1907 by Mary Ishbel Lockey (a Stanford alumna) to offer girls a comprehensive, college preparatory education, taking its name from the first girl's school in Palo Alto known as Castilleja Hall.

items.title: College of Notre Dame (later: Notre Dame de Namur University), 1890-1976
items.description: Located in San Jose, then Belmont, California. Founded in 1851 as the Academy of Notre Dame. Chartered in 1868 as the College of Notre Dame. Moved to Belmont in 1923. In 2001 name changed to Notre Dame de Namur University.

items.title: College of San Mateo (formerly: San Mateo Junior College)
items.description: Located in San Mateo, California. Founded in 1922 as the San Mateo Junior College. In 1954 became College of San Mateo. For additional catalogs see Boxes 431-432.

items.title: George A. Merrill letters, 1885-1908
items.description: Letters from Horace Davis, A.S. Hallidie, David Starr Jordan, and L.A. Buchanan, largely pertaining to the Lick School of Mechanical Arts, of which Merrill was principal. Buchanan, largely pertaining to the Lick School of Mechanical Arts, of which Merrill was principal.

items.title: Margarita Espinosa notes on Adelante Villa, 1987-1993
items.description: Photocopy of undated notes by Espinosa on Adelante Villa, a preparatory school for girls founded by Lucy Fletcher and Eleanor Brooks Pearson and first located at Stanford. Also includes short article and letter on the history of Castilleja School, 1987, and the letter that accompanied these materials, 1993.

items.title: Palo Alto Military Academy (formerly: Manzanita Hall), 1893-1932
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1893 as Manzanita Hall. Became Palo Alto Military Academy in 1919. Closed in 1972.

items.title: San Jose State University (formerly: California State University, San Jose; formerly: San Jose State College; formerly: California State Teachers College at San Jose; formerly: California State Normal School), 1875-1982
items.description: Originally located in San Francisco, but moved to San Jose in 1871. Established in 1857 as the Minns' Evening Normal School. Became California State Normal School in 1862 and the California State Teachers College at San Jose in 1921.

items.title: St. Joseph's College (California)
items.description: Located in Mountain View, California. Opened in 1924. Closed in 1991.

items.title: University of the Pacific (formerly: College of the Pacific, formerly: University of the Pacific), 1873-1978
items.description: First located in Santa Clara, California. Chartered in 1851 as California Wesleyan College, soon changed to University of the Pacific. In 1911 became College of the Pacific. Moved to San Jose in 1871 and from San Jose to Stockton, California in 1924. In 1961 became University of the Pacific.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: A partial list of seed plants of the North Coast Ranges of California, 1929-1972
items.description: The lists name some 2,717 species collected between Sonoma and the Oregon border. In his introduction to the 1951 list he writes, "This list has been undertaken in the sheer pleasure of finding out what seed plants grow in this vast and varied region...

items.title: Bailey Willis papers, circa 1900-1962
items.description: After early studies in Germany, Bailey Willis attended Columbia University and was awarded the degree of Mining Engineer in 1878 and of Civil Engineer in 1879. In 1884 he began his career with the United States Geological Survey, working chiefly in the Pacific Northwest.

items.title: Cecil H. Green oral history interview transcript, 1995
items.description: Green was a British-born American geophysicist who trained at the University of British Columbia and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He was a founder of Texas Instruments.

items.title: Charles Stacy French papers, 1935-1989
items.description: French, plant physiologist, was director of the Dept. of Plant Biology of the Carnegie Institution, located on the Stanford University campus, from 1947 until his retirement in 1973. Prior to his arrival at Carnegie, he taught at the Harvard Medical School, the University of Chicago, and the University of Minnesota.

items.title: Chemist and administrator at UC Berkeley, Rice University, Stanford University, and the Atomic Energy Commission, 1935-1997 : oral history transcript, 1999
items.description: Interviews of Pitzer by Sally Smith Hughes and Germaine LaBerge conducted in 1996, 1997, and 1998. With introductions by Robert Curl and Marilyn Chapin Massey. Sponsored by the Regional Oral History Office of the Bancroft Library, University of California, Berkeley.

items.title: Douglas Merritt Whitaker papers, 1926-1963
items.description: Professor of Biology at Stanford (1931-1955); Dean of the School of Biological Sciences (1946-1949); Dean of Graduate Studies (1948-1951); Dean of Humanities and Sciences (1951-1952). Acting Vice-President of the University (1948-1949); and Provost (1952-1955).

items.title: Frank W. Weymouth papers, 1900-1965
items.description: MEMORIAL RESOLUTION FRANK WALTER WEYMOUTH 1884-1963. Dr. Frank W. Weymouth was born June 17, 1884, in Seattle, Washington. His death in Oakland March 19, 1963, brought to an end a career of fifty three years of teaching and research.

items.title: Geological map; San Juan Bautist Hills, 3 miles south of San Jose, California : hand-drawn and colored map, 1901, Jan..
items.description: Scale 1 : 7680, contours 25 ft. (1 inch = 640 ft.) Data of topography enlarged from San Jose sheet (U.S.G.S.).

items.title: George James Peirce papers, 1905-1926
items.description: Peirce earned his B.S. at Harvard in 1890 and his M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig, 1894. He taught at Indiana University before coming to Stanford University in 1897 as assistant professor of botany.

items.title: George Polya papers, 1884-1985
items.description: Hungarian mathematician George Pólya was educated at the University of Budapest and the University of Paris, and taught at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich from 1914 to 1940. His students included future Stanford physics professors Felix Bloch and Hans Staub.

items.title: Harry S. Mosher papers, 1944-2000
items.description: Harry S. Mosher earned his bachelor's degree in 1937 from Willamette University and his master's degree from Oregon State University in 1939. He taught briefly at Willamette before earning his doctorate in organic chemistry from Pennsylvania State University in 1942.

items.title: Interview with Arthur Kornberg [videorecording]
items.description: Biochemistry professor at Stanford University (Chairman of the Department of Biochemistry from 1959 to 1969), Kornberg received a Nobel Prize in medicine and physiology in 1959 for pioneering the synthesis of DNA in the laboratory.

items.title: Jens Clausen field notebooks, 1928-1962
items.description: Primarily herbarium specimen collection notes, arranged by number and date. Box 1, 1928-1946; box 2, 1951-1957; box 3, 1957-1962, and other notes including a list of his collections by number, and a notebook, "Edible native and naturalized plants of California," nd.

items.title: John Casper Branner papers, 1882-1921
items.description: John Casper Branner, second president of Stanford University, was born in New Market, Tennessee in 1850. He entered Cornell University in 1870, but left in 1874 for Brazil first as assistant geologist on the Geological Survey of Brazil then as assistant engineer for the Sao Cyriaco Gold Mining Company.

items.title: John Casper Branner Photographs of San Francisco Earthquake, 1906
items.description: John Casper Branner, second president of Stanford University, was born in New Market, Tennessee in 1850. He entered Cornell University in 1870, but left in 1874 for Brazil first as assistant geologist on the Geological Survey of Brazil then as assistant engineer for the Sao Cyriaco Gold Mining Company.

items.title: John E. Cox papers, 1940-1999
items.description: This collection includes photographs, lab notebooks, and a printed copy of an article. The photographs are of Cox and his wife Flora. The notebooks, one pharmacology laboratory notebook (1942) and two biochemistry laboratory notebooks (1940-1941), date from his time at Stanford School of Medicine.

items.title: John George Herriot papers, 1937-1992
items.description: John G. Herriot (1916-2003) earned a BS in mathematics and physics at the University of Manitoba in 1937 and a PhD in mathematics at Brown University in 1941. He first taught at Stanford from 1942-1944, leaving to do research in the Ames Aeronautical Laboratory at Moffett Field.

items.title: John Warvelle Harbaugh, "Memoirs"
items.description: John Warvelle Harbaugh (1926-2019) was an American geologist and Professor Emeritus in the Geological and Environmental Sciences Department and at the Energy Resources Engineering Department at Stanford University.

items.title: Pierre Van Rysselberghe papers, 1932-1973
items.description: Pierre van Rysselberghe, a chemist and chemical engineer, earned his masters (1928) and doctorate (1929) at Stanford University. He taught at the University of Oregon and at Stanford. He died in 1977.

items.title: San Francisco Earthquake Photographs
items.description: Photographs documenting the 1906 earthquake in California. Artificial collection of photographs chronicling the after-effects of the San Francisco Earthquake and Fire of 1906.

items.title: Sidney Dean Townley papers, circa 1827-1939
items.description: Astronomer. Studied at Lick Observatory on Mount Hamilton, California, and at the Universities of Berlin and Munich. Before becoming a Professor of Applied Mathematics at Stanford Unviersiy in 1907, Townley taught at U.C. Berkeley and was Astronomer at the International Latitude Observatory in Ukiah, California.

items.title: Species Lupinorum and related correspondence, 1922-1953
items.description: "A series of papers reviewing the genus Lupinus... issued in dated signatures...".

items.title: Syllabus for the courses in field geology
items.description: Cyrus F. Tolman was a professor of economic geology at Stanford University These mimeographed syllabi are for Geology 4 and 5, the summer courses on field and topographic geology. Includes parts 1 (Geology 4) and 2 (Geology 5) from June 1920 used by Thomas D. Radcliffe.

items.title: The Berkeley Hills : a detail of coast range geology / original typewritten copy, 1902
items.description: Originally a gift of the author to Stephen B. Fiske.

items.title: Thomas Jefferson Jackson See papers, 1891-1970
items.description: Thomas Jefferson Jackson See, born 19 February 1866 in Missouri, was an astronomer and mathematician who established laws of the Formation of the Solar System and founded the science of cosmogony. Consists of original drafts and copies of scientific papers.

items.title: William Russel Dudley papers, 1838-1937 (inclusive), 1864-1912 (bulk)
items.description: William Russel Dudley earned his bachelor's (1874) and master's (1876) degrees in botany at Cornell University; after graduation he pursued botanical study in Strassburg and Berlin. He taught at Cornell and Indiana University before joining the Stanford faculty in 1892.

items.title: William S. Johnson papers, 1940-1992
items.description: Johnson, professor of chemistry at Stanford University, was generally regarded as one of the major figures in 20th-century organic chemistry. He served as head of Stanford's chemistry department from 1960 to 1969, and after resigning that post, was appointed the Jackson-Wood Professor of Chemistry which he held until…

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Doris Helen Linder (1925-2008) was born in Columbia, South Dakota to Swedish immigrants Hilda and Arvid Justus Linder. Linder studied history at Stanford University, where she received a BA in 1946 and an MA in 1949. She received a Ph.D. in History from the University of Minnesota in 1961.

items.title: Ephraim Douglass Adams papers, 1730-1974 (inclusive), 1900-1931 (bulk)
items.description: Ephraim Douglass (E.D.) Adams was born in Decorah, Iowa, on December 18, 1865. Adams attended Grinnell College and graduated from the University of Michigan in 1887, receiving a doctorate in 1890.

items.title: Eric Hutchinson papers, 1891-1982 (inclusive), 1954-1982 (bulk)
items.description: Eric Hutchinson, born in England in 1920, was educated at the University of Cambridge (1938-1945), earning all three of his degrees in chemistry. He taught at Sheffield University and Fordham University, before joining the Stanford faculty in 1949.

items.title: Henry Rushton Fairclough papers, 1886-1937
items.description: Henry Rushton Fairclough (1862-1938) was a classical philologist from Ontario, Canada. He received bachelor's, master's, and Doctor of Letters degrees from the University of Toronto. He received a PhD in 1896 from Johns Hopkins. He was a fellow in Classics and lecturer in Greek at University College, Toronto.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: "Becoming Stanford: The Making of an American University" [videorecording]
items.description: Part 1, "The Founding," covers the origins and building of the university through World War I; highlights include Stanford family history, the first Big Game between Stanford and UC Berkeley, early student life, the rise of tenure, and the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Bacon family papers, 1896-1970. (inclusive)
items.description: Harriet Dunn was a friend of Jane Stanford who operated a boarding house for young faculty on what is now White Plaza. The house was later passed down to her cousin, mathematics professor Harold M. Bacon '28, MA '29, PhD '33, and his wife, Rosamond '30, MA '32 (a co-founder of the Stanford Historical Society).

items.title: Charles Anderson Gauld papers
items.description: Gauld, who earned his A.B. in history at Stanford in 1932, was a lecturer at Stanford and assistant editor of HISPANIC AMERICAN REPORT. These papers pertain largely to Stanford anecdotes and history and include his typescript articles on George E. Crothers and Jane Stanford.

items.title: David Starr Jordan Papers
items.description: The Jordan Papers span 1861-1951, although the bulk of the collection dates between 1891 and 1929. Very few items pre-date Jordan's connection with Stanford University and there is very little material after the severe stroke he suffered in the summer of 1929.

items.title: David Starr Jordan papers, 1861-1981
items.description: David Starr Jordan was born at Gainesville, New York, on January 19, 1851. In March, 1869, Jordan entered Cornell University to join the first freshman class (which had begun work in the fall of 1868).

items.title: Elinor Cogswell papers, circa 1896-1976
items.description: Elinor Cogswell received her A.B. in English at Stanford in 1916, her M.A. in 1917; she was a journalist with the PALO ALTO TIMES and served as editor from 1938 to 1954. She was one of the first women to become a Stanford Associate; she died in 1983 at the age of 90.

items.title: Francis Albert Smith papers
items.description: Francis Albert Smith earned three degrees in chemistry at Stanford University: AB 1922, AM 1923, and Ph.D 1926. Collection includes two appointment letters from Ray Lyman Wilbur, 1922-23; 3 letters from Edward C. Franklin, 1923-32; fundraising letter from Herbert Hoover re the Stanford Re-investment Fund ca. 1940.

items.title: Frederick Emmons Terman, 1900-1982: some recollections : typescript, 1982
items.description: Reminiscence regarding Frederick E. Terman as chairman of the Dept. of Electrical Engineering at Stanford University presented in a talk to the Stanford faculty women's club, 1982.

items.title: Halsey L. Royden, "The History of the Stanford Mathematics Department"
items.description: Halsey L. Royden earned his B.S. in 1948 and his M.S. in 1949 at Stanford University and his Ph.D. at Harvard in 1951, after which he returned to Stanford to join the faculty in the department of mathematics.

items.title: Nancy Mason, "A Part of his Childhood Belongs to Peter Coutts; A Reminiscence of Wendell Fletcher" typescript
items.description: Account of Wendell Fletcher's childhood, as written by Nancy Mason. Fletcher lived on campus in the Tower House with his family from 1910 to 1918. His father was a civil engineer with Stanford University during this time.

items.title: Palo Alto Times, Special Memorial Edition, March 24, 1905
items.description: Jane Eliza Lathrop was born August 25, 1828, the daughter of Dyer Lathrop of Albany, New York. In 1850 she married Leland Stanford, returning with him to California in 1855 where they settled in Sacramento. Leland Stanford later became President of the Southern Pacific Railroad and Governor of California.

items.title: Rixford Kinney Snyder, "Memories of a Santa Clara Valley Boy Who Never Left, 1908-1991" typescript
items.description: Rixford Kinney Snyder, Professor of History, Dean of Admissions, and first Director of the Alumni Association's Travel/Study Program. Snyder was born and raised in the Willow Glen area of San Jose and attended local schools. Original and revised version of Rixford's autobiography.

items.title: SRI: the founding years : videorecording, 1983
items.description: Weldon B. Gibson, who earned his MBA in 1940 and his PhD in 1950 from Stanford University, was one of the first fellows at the Stanford Research Institute and its Senior Director in the 1980's. He also taught at Stanford's Graduate School of Business and served on the Athletic Board.

items.title: Stanford Alumni Association, alumni reminiscences
items.description: Correspondence between Jack W. Shoup, secretary of the Alumni Association, and alumni concerning memories of Senator and Mrs. Stanford (1955-1956), which included attending parties at the Stanford home, Mr. Stanford observing work on Encina Hall, Mrs. Stanford observing work on Memorial Church, Mrs. Stanford visiting…

items.title: Stanford Historical Photograph collection, 1887-circa 1996
items.description: Series 1, General Photographs, documents the campus and campus life; subjects include athletics, original construction of the campus, individual buildings, students and student life activities, commencement activities, academic departments, and damage from the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society oral history program interviews
items.description: The Stanford Historical Society's Oral History Program explores the institutional history of the University, with an emphasis on the transformative post-WWII period, through interviews with leading faculty, staff, alumni, trustees, and others.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University. The files were maintained by University Archives staff from around the time of the Archives' establishment in 1965 through mid-2011 Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford…

items.title: Stanford University deeds, 1901
items.description: Two copies of the deed of grant and one copy of the deed of gift, issued by Jane Lathrop Stanford via the Board of Trustees in 1901. Parchment and ink, tied with red ribbons and sealed with red sealing wax, each copy is signed by Jane Stanford and other university officials.

items.title: Stanford: a sentimental journey : video recordings, 1987
items.description: This film in celebration of Stanford University's centennial includes interviews with faculty and alumni; scenes of academic and student activities; views of the campus; and still photographs transferred to video, primarily concerning the history of Stanford.

items.title: The Stanford years, being an excerpt from "memoranda," the unpublished autobiography of Theodore J. Hoover:
items.description: Head, Department of Mining and Metallurgy (1919- ) and founding dean of the School of Engineering (1925-1936). Stanford class of 1901. Manuscript (typescript) excerpt from "Memoranda," the unpublished autobiography of Theodore J. Hoover.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: George E. Crothers papers, 1905-1957
items.description: Correspondence (1905-1957), speeches, articles, legal documents, photographs, newsclippings and scrapbooks. Major subjects include Stanford University, Republican Party activities (1909-1930), California State Normal Schools, United States monetary policy and U.S. relations with the Republic of China (1920-1940).

items.title: Harry C. Peterson papers, 1879-1936
items.description: Peterson, born in Iowa in 1876, was curator of the Stanford Museum from 1900-1917; after leaving Stanford, he directed the Sutter's Fort Museum in Sacramento. Collection includes administrative and personal correspondence, 1888-1936.

items.title: Herbert Hoover letter to Timothy Hopkins, 1913
items.description: Herbert Hoover was elected to Stanford University's Board of Trustees in 1912. Letter from H.C. Hoover to Timothy Hopkins, President of the Board of Trustees, July 30, 1913, regarding the location of athletic fields on the Stanford campus.

items.title: Horace Davis papers, 1865-1915
items.description: Horace Davis, born in Massachusetts, graduated from Harvard in 1849. He moved to California in 1853 and pursued several business ventures before embarking in the wheat and flour trade in 1860. He was president of the Sperry Flour Company for 40 years.

items.title: Jane Lathrop Stanford papers, 1860-1983
items.description: Jane Eliza Lathrop was born August 25, 1828, the daughter of Dyer Lathrop of Albany, New York. In 1850 she married Leland Stanford, returning with him to California in 1855 where they settled in Sacramento. Leland Stanford later became President of the Southern Pacific Railroad and Governor of California.

items.title: Leland Stanford Junior Memorial Scholarship legal documents
items.description: Trust agreement and Terms and Agreements for the Scholarship; the latter document relates family history concerning the origins of the scholarship and the original source of its funds.

items.title: Leland Whitman Cutler papers, 1909-1941
items.description: Leland Whitman Cutler was President of the Board of Trustees of Stanford University (1942-1954) and insurance businessman. Chiefly correspondence and working papers of the Board of Trustees.

items.title: Ray Lyman Wilbur, president of Stanford University, papers, 1914-1951
items.description: Ray Lyman Wilbur graduated from Stanford University (B.S.1896, M.S. 1897) and from Cooper Medical College (M.D. 1899). He served as lecturer and professor of physiology and of medicine (1897-1903), Dean of the Cooper Medical College (Stanford) (1911-1916), third President of Stanford University (1916-1943)…

items.title: Samuel Franklin Leib papers, 1881-1920
items.description: The collection consists of four major components: Stanford correspondence pertaining to Judge Leib's association with the Stanford family and his responsibilities as a member of the first Board of Trustees of Stanford University (1891-1923); personal correspondence (1885-1910).

items.title: Sennet W. Gilfillan correspondence with Stanford University
items.description: Correspondence with Frederick E. Terman and David S. Jacobson regarding Gilfillan's contributions to scholarships for electrical engineering students and the Gilfillan Wing of the Electronics Laboratory; some of Terman's letters concern faculty and research projects of the department.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: Powers and Duties —The Board of Trustees is custodian of the endowment and all properties of the University. The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University.

items.title: Stanford University, Business Office, Cooper Medical College correspondence
items.description: In 1901 discussion of a union between Cooper Medical College, Lane Hospital and Stanford University began. Nothing came of the discussions until 1905 when President Jordan recommended to the trustees that Cooper be accepted on the condition that it be used for medical research.

items.title: Stanford University, Controller's Office, records, 1891-1998
items.description: The bound volumes in the collection (ledgers, journals, day books, and cash books) pertain to university finances, the Palo Alto Stock Farm, the Vina Ranch, Durham Ranch, and Lane Hospital (San Francisco). Volumes of note include board ledgers for Encina and Roble dormitories, 1892-1903.

items.title: Stanford University, Faculty Senate, records, 1891-2026(inclusive)
items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. The Council holds one regularly scheduled meeting annually.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of the President, records
items.description: The Stanford President's Office documents collection is a valuable repository of records, correspondence, and documents that provide insight into the leadership and administration of Stanford University over the years. These records include letters from the President to the Board of Trustees, 1902-1948.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, Dean's Office records, 1915-1998 (inclusive), 1925-1955 (bulk)
items.description: Civil and mechanical engineering courses were among the first taught at Stanford University, with courses in electrical and mining engineering added in 1893. In 1925, the formerly independent engineering departments were organized into the School of Engineering with Theodore Jesse Hoover as Dean.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, requisitions, 1926-1946
items.description: Requisitions from the Dept. of Civil Engineering, 1926-40, the Dept. of Electrical Engineering, 1926-40, Ryan High Voltage Laboratory, 1930-40, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, 1926-46, Guggenheim Aeronautic Laboratory, 1927-44, and the Dept. of Mining Engineering, 1936-40.

items.title: Stanford University, University Services, records, 1936-1957
items.description: The University Services office of Stanford University (1942-1954) was established to carry out a program of service on a contractual basis, focusing on the region, the nation, international studies, and business and industry.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The Business Affairs organization at Stanford provides integrated financial, technological, business and human resource services for the benefit of the university community.

sectors.name: Education and research

items.title: Correspondence concerning Dr. William Duane
items.description: Webster was professor of physics at Stanford University, 1920-1954, and emeritus professor, 1954-1976. Correspondence, 1970, between Webster, Albert A. Bartlett, physics professor at the University of Colorado, and George W. Wheelwright, III, concerning Dr. William Duane's years in the Physics department at Harvard…

items.title: George B. Dantzig papers, 1934-2005
items.description: George Bernard Dantzig (November 8, 1914 – May 13, 2005) was an American mathematical scientist who made important contributions to operations research, computer science, economics, and statistics.

items.title: Merrill S. Hugo papers, 1901-1960, 1941-1960
items.description: Hugo, a 1924 engineering graduate of Stanford and a Major with the United States Army Ordnance Department, joined the Stanford faculty in 1930 and served as director of the Gage Laboratory, School of Engineering. The materials consist of records the Gage Laboratory and the Stanford School of Engineering.

items.title: Stanford Research Institute records, 1947-1966
items.description: The Stanford Research Institute was organized in 1946 as an applied research center for industry and government. In 1970 it became independent from Stanford University and in 1977 changed its name to SRI International.

items.title: W. Conyers Herring papers, 1970-2003
items.description: Professor emeritus of applied physics at Stanford University. Herring was a leader in the field of solid-state physics, the study of the arrangement and interaction of atoms in solid materials.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Ansel Adams photograph collection
items.description: Ansel Easton Adams was born in San Francisco on February 20, 1902. Adams started photographing nature scenes around 1919 while a Sierra Club member. In 1927 Adams came under the patronage of Albert M. Bender, who helped Adams publish his first portfolio.

items.title: Arthur L. Dahl papers, 1900-1970
items.description: Missing Title 1880, Oct. 16 Born in Port Leavenworth, Kansas. 1900, Dec. 17 Becomes stenograher for George Wright, U.S. Indian Inspector for Indian Territory at Muscogee. 1901, Dec. Passes Civil Service Stenographer and Typewriter test. 1902, Dec. Post Office Department.

items.title: Bruce Bliven papers, 1906-1985
items.description: Born July 27, 1889 in Emmetsburg, Iowa, Bruce Ormsby Bliven was the son of Charles and Lilla Ormsby Bliven. Having won prizes for his writing ability as early as age fourteen, Bruce went on to work his way through Stanford University as a cub reporter for the S.F. Bulletin. He received a B.A. in English in 1911.

items.title: Chester W. Barker sheet music collection, 1891-1973
items.description: This collection contains approximately 70 items dating from 1891-1973, the majority of which are from musicals. Almost all are inscribed by Barker with notes, pasted-in lyrics, and a few programs.

items.title: Clarence Urmy papers, 1878-1936
items.description: Poet Clarence Urmy (1858-1923) was born in San Francisco on July 10, 1858. He was the grandson of Elea Thomas who was one of the founders of the Methodist church in the state of California. Urmy's father was a Methodist minister for 50 years.

items.title: Conservation treatment report, John MacQuarrie mural, 1941, Caltrain Station, Palo Alto : reports and photographs, 2003-2005
items.description: John A. MacQuarrie, San Francisco artist, painted a mural for the Palo Alto train station depicting transportation in the West and the coming of the railroad with a portrait of Leland Stanford. The train station property is owned by Stanford University and leased to the city of Palo Alto.

items.title: Frank Ernest Hill papers, 1905-1969
items.description: Frank Ernest Hill, son of photographer Andrew Putnam Hill (1853- 1922), born 29 August 1888 in San Jose, California, was a newspaperman, college professor, aviator, poet, and author. He received his A.B. (1911) and A.M. (1914) from Stanford University in English literature.

items.title: George H. McMurry papers, ca. 1890-1970
items.description: George Harold McMurry was born in Bombay (Mumbai), India on November 14, 1898, the son of American missionaries Valentine G. McMurry and Celia Ferries McMurry. He received his B.A. degree in 1921 from College of the Pacific where he studied English and History.

items.title: John W. Metcalf papers, c. 1880-1940
items.description: John W. Metcalf (1856-1926) was a composer, musician and music instructor. Metcalf considered himself the first music teacher at Stanford University, but it is more likely that he taught several students privately at Roble Hall. Unpublished listing of music titles available on request. Please contact the department.

items.title: Mary Hallock Foote papers, 1863-1924 (inclusive), 1868-1916 (bulk)
items.description: Mary Hallock Foote was born Mary Haviland Hallock on November 19, 1847, at Milton-on-Hudson, N.Y., the youngest of four children. Her close-knit farming family were Quakers, Free-Soil Republicans of English stock, sympathetic to anti-slavery, temperance, and women's rights.

items.title: Sheet music : miscellaneous collection, ca 1890-1950
items.description: Includes some early San Francisco and San Jose imprints. Also includes professional copies specifically for broadcast only.

items.title: Theodore Wores papers, 1880-1999
items.description: If the measure of a painter is the number of times that he or she has been shown, then Theodore Wores ranks higher today than any of his critics would have imagined. Includes correspondence, written works, clippings, articles, catalogs, and books, and reproductions by glass negative and print of his works.

items.title: Walter R. Miles research concerning Eadweard Muybridge, 1881-1939
items.description: Walter Miles, a professor of experimental psychology at Stanford University, endeavored to memorialize photographer Eadweard Muybridge's work by establishing a permanent exhibit at the Stanford Museum and by hosting a 50th anniversary event.

items.title: William [Bill] Riley Marken papers, 1937-2010s
items.description: Collection consists of manuscript, printed, and photographic materials created and collected by Marken, ca. 1960s-2000s. Materials focus on a variety of writing projects, including Marken's 2012 Stanford MLA thesis-California Tomorrow, 1961-1983: An Enduring Environmental Legacy; misc.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: "Frank Lloyd Wright's Hanna House" [videorecording]
items.description: Paul Turner, professor of art and specialist in architectural history from the 18th to 20th centuries, delves into the fascinating history of Stanford's Hanna House, with special focus on its architect, Frank Lloyd Wright.

items.title: An architect grows up in Palo Alto; memoirs of Birge M. Clark, F.A.I.A. : typescript, 1982
items.description: Birge M. Clark earned his A.B. in graphic art at Stanford in 1914 and his degree in architecture at Columbia in 1917. After his service as a balloon observer during World War I, he returned to Palo Alto and began his practice as an architect.

items.title: Architecture of Stanford University, 1886-1937
items.description: Primarily original correspondence concerning the early stages of planning, construction and landscaping of Stanford University, 1886-1906. The construction of Memorial Church, the Library (1906), the Gymnasium (1906), the Musuem, and parts of the Quadrangle are featured.

items.title: Arthur Brown papers, 1910-1961
items.description: Arthur Brown, Jr. and John Bakewell, Jr. formed their San Francisco architectural firm, Bakewell and Brown, in 1906. They became associated with Stanford University in 1913.

items.title: Birge M. Clark architectural drawings, 1909-1954
items.description: Collection contains architectural drawings by Birge M. Clark, his brother David B. Clark, and other partners Walter Stromquist, David F. Potter and Joseph Ehrlich, with a few drawings by his father A. B. Clark.

items.title: Birge M. Clark architectural records and personal papers, 1919-1990
items.description: Birge M. Clark earned his A.B. in graphic art at Stanford in 1914 and his degree in architecture at Columbia in 1917. After his service as a balloon observer during World War I, he returned to Palo Alto and began his practice as an architect.

items.title: Charles Edward Hodges papers, 1891-1929
items.description: Charles E. Hodges was appointed Resident Architect by Leland and Jane Stanford in 1891, a position he held until his resignation in June of 1906. Prior to this appointment, he was draftsman to Shepley, Rutan and Coolidge, the architectural firm responsible for many of the University's original buildings.

items.title: Charles Edward Hodges photograph albums, circa 1898-1905
items.description: Collection contains two photograph albums belonging to Charles E. Hodges, resident draftsman and later architect at Stanford University. Volume 28.1 (ca. 1898-1905) contains images of Memorial Arch and its frieze; the Stanford University Inn.

items.title: Hanna house collection, 1900-1995 (inclusive)
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Construction, begun in 1937, continued in four stages over 25 years.

items.title: Hanna House collection, 1935-1982 [microform]
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Construction, begun in 1937, continued in four stages over 25 years.

items.title: Henry C. Collins architectural files and drawings, 1928-1938
items.description: Collection includes correspondence, financial documents, lists of fixtures and hardware, photographs, and architectural drawings for homes built on the Stanford campus for Ida Stauf, Maurice L. Huggins, William Leonard Schwartz, and Arthur Martin Cathcart.

items.title: Lee Emerson Bassett house records
items.description: Lee Emerson Bassett, professor of Speech and Drama at Stanford University from 1900 to 1938, built his home on campus at 740 Santa Ynez Street. Included in this collection are specifications by the architect, A. W. Smith; bills and one letter from Leon S. Bean, general contractor, 1909.

items.title: Lou Henry Hoover House Papers, 1917-1960 (inclusive), 1917-1949 (bulk)
items.description: Birge M. Clark (born 1893) was the son of Arthur B. Clark, who came to Stanford in 1892 as an Instructor in Drawing. Birge Clark received his A.B. from Stanford, 1914, and B.Arch from Columbia, 1917, and was an architect in Palo Alto.

items.title: Oral history, 1982
items.description: San Francisco architect and nephew of Frank Lloyd Wright. Katherine Tobin, his aunt, was Wright's first wife. Interview conducted by Paul R. Hanna, Jean S. Hanna, and Roxanne Nilan.

items.title: Panama-Pacific international exposition, 1913-1915
items.description: Typescript report of the Division of Works about the building of the Exposition and architectural plans. Includes photographs, blueprints, maps, graphs, tables, and an appendix by Markwart, assistant director of Works and chief of construction.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society, Historic Houses III : research and production materials, 1972-2004 (inclusive), 1999-2004 (bulk)
items.description: Research and production materials for the book, HISTORIC HOUSES III: SAN JUAN NEIGHBORHOOD, STANFORD UNIVERSITY, published by the Stanford Historical Society in 2005. Includes Byron Feig's original watercolor painting used on the cover and his original pencil drawings of each house.

items.title: Stanford University quad construction records
items.description: Contracts between Jane Stanford and Nels Peterson for work on construction of the Quad (1901); bills and receipts for materials used and work completed (1901-1903).

items.title: Stanford University, Commission of Engineers, records, 1906-1908
items.description: The Commission of Engineers was charged with directing the restoration of the university's buildings after the earthquake of April 1906. The Commission, composed of Professors Charles D. Marx (civil engineering), Charles B. Wing (structural engineering), and William F. Durand (mechanical engineering), was appointed…

items.title: Stanford University, Hospital, specifications
items.description: Construction specifications, largely for power plant equipment for Stanford University Hospital at its San Francisco location; firms represented include Hunter and Hudson Consulting Engineers, Otis Elevator Company, and Bakewell and Brown Architects.

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. Architects active during the early years of the University include Bakewell and Brown; Shepley, Rutan, and Coolidge.

items.title: The autobiography of an architect
items.description: Includes a one-page letter from Mrs. Dorothy Feltham, Secretary to Mr. J.H. Clark, explaining the memoir.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Film, radio and television

items.title: Daniel Berman letters, 1929-1941
items.description: A gifted child who went on to study spectral intensity physics at Stanford, later following friends to Hollywood during its early heyday period. The letters are written to his mother, Rita Berman, founder of Educational Playthings, and his uncle, Harry Scherman, founder of the Little Leather Library and the Book of…

items.title: Exactus Photo Film Corporation records, 1914-1918
items.description: The Exactus Photo Film corporation of Palo Alto was officially incorporated on August 28 1914. The earlier part of that year had been spent in preliminary organization, establishing contacts, and deciding on a suitable site for an outdoor studio.

items.title: Rapport sur le Tirage de Developpement des Films Sonores : Rapport de Monsieur Conrard sur l'étude du film parlant & sonore en Amérique
items.description: Loose sheets held in the original binder with sliding clasp. Carbon typescript with text on rectos only, with some autograph corrections, and 14 illustrations of which 13 are pasted to the typed sheets. Verso leaf 3 stamped "PATHÉ-CINEMA / Jul 1929 / ÉTUDE JOINVILLE".

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Press, journalism and broadcasting

items.title: Crosley Corporation press release and photographs, 1939 June 16.
items.description: The press release discusses the use of six carrier pigeons to speed 32 photographs of the Cincinnati Reds - Pittsburgh Pirates baseball game to its studio four miles away for immediate transmission on the WLW-W8XUJ facsimile radio news broadcast.

items.title: Frank Kester papers and photographs
items.description: Born in Cholame Valley, California in March 1888, Frank Kester spent his youth in small towns including Alvarado, Mendocino and Watsonville. Before Kester reached his teens, his mother divorced his father, remarried and moved the family to Oakland.

items.title: Roy Pryor Collection
items.description: The Roy Pryor Collection consists of off-air recordings of local and network radio in Menlo Park, California between 1937 and 1949. Pryor used a home recording machine to make aluminum and lacquer discs of broadcasts, mostly capturing war-related news and commentary The collection contains a wide range of subject…

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Sport and recreation

items.title: Bay Area highschools' track meet results : newsarticles, 1910 and 1913
items.description: April 23, 1910 and April 12, 1913.

items.title: International Sweepstakes : Greater San Francisco Speedway. San Carlos on the Peninsula. San Francisco, Cal., Dec. 11, 1921
items.description: Photograph showing the contestants and associated folk at the Greater San Francisco Speedway in San Carlos, CA, on race day for the speedway's inaugural event. The stands, in the back-ground, are filled, so this photograph was likely taken a bit prior to the race's start.

items.title: The grand national livestock exposition, horse show, and rodeo (San Francisco, Calif) : programs, 1941-1956
items.description: Presented by No. 1-A District Agricultural Association (County of San Mateo and City and County of San Francisco). Programs for 1941, 1948, 1949, 1952, 1954, and 1956.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: A Century of Western Living, 1898-1998 : poster for centennial exhibit, 1998
Bjarne B. Dahl restoration reports, 1929-2007
items.description: Bjarne B. Dahl was a piano and harpsichord restorer from Sunnyvale, California. Materials include photographic reports (consisting of a written description, photographic prints, and negatives) documenting Dahl's restoration work on antique keyboard instruments.

items.title: James Ladd Delkin papers, 1918-1954
items.description: Local printer who published mainly San Francisco and vicinity guides and histories. Examples of his books and pamphlets, as well as wood and metal printers blocks, original illustrations, and a bit of personal material.

items.title: Panama-Pacific International Exposition : guide books and postcards, 1915
items.description: Folder 1: 4 postcards. Folder 2: The Wahlgreen Co. OFFICIAL GUIDE PANAMA-PACIFIC INTERNATIONAL EXPOSITION, San Francisco, 1915. Folder 3: Sheldon Cheney. ART-LOVER'S GUIDE TO THE EXPOSITION. Berkeley; at the sign of the Berkeley Oak, 1915; and E.R. Gudehus. THE LIBERTY BELL.

items.title: Panama-Pacific International Exposition photographs, 1915
items.description: An artifical collection from four sources, however the earliest and largest part of the collection (154 prints) came from Leon Kolb (no date available).

items.title: San Jose, CA : album of theater clippings, ca. 1910
items.description: Includes several articles by Clarence Urmy and Walter Anthony, and includes such groups as the The Whitney Opera Company and the Savoy, Victory, and Columbia theaters. Three black and white glossy photos are slipped in, including a portrait of Sigrid Onegin and a group portrait of the English Singers.

items.title: Stanford University Press archival book copies, 1900-2013
items.description: The Stanford University Press was established as an independent printing operation at Stanford University in 1892. The university purchased it in 1917, and expanded it into a full-service publishing house in 1925. The collection consists of archival copies of books published by Stanford University Press.

items.title: Sunset Magazine : video, 18 Oct. 1998
items.description: Includes interviews of Mel and Bill Lane. Discusses the role of Sunset Magazine over the last one hundred years.

items.title: William R. Hewlett library
items.description: These CD-ROMs contain a database for William R. Hewlett's personal library (1997); the PC version also contains childhood photographs of Hewlett, scanned on the ocassion of his 85th birthday (1998).

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: Alice Park collection of papers relating to the American League to Abolish Capital Punishment, 1914-1940
items.description: Alice Locke Park was born in Boston in 1861 but lived most of her life in Palo Alto, Calif. She was active in many socially progressive organizations.

items.title: Alice Park papers, 1920-1936
items.description: Alice Park was an American pacifist, a feminist and a socialist. Correspondence, pamphlets, newsclippings and flyers pertaining to the subject of birth contol and planned parenthood.

items.title: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California records, 1900-2000 bulk 1934-2000
items.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is a non-profit organization committed to the defense, preservation, and extension of civil liberties in the United States.

Shockley, with letters to and from him and other members of the A.I.M.E., typescript arguments for simplified spelling…

items.title: California biography collection

items.title: California history : scrapbook and miscellaneous pamphlets, 1857-1955
items.description: The scrapbook consists primarily of clippings about Santa Clara County history, as well as Monterey, Stanford, and Yosemite. There are also two poems by John E. Richards (pp. 123 & 146).

items.title: California photographs, circa 1882-1940
items.description: Of unknown origin. 49 photographs. Includes Sierras, boats, Golden Gate Bridge under construction, one unidentified portrait, Pacific Coast Amateur photography association meeting 1889 photographing a solar eclipse, Higuera House in Warm Springs (Fremont) in 1882, interior views.

items.title: California photographs, circa 1900-1950
items.description: Artificial collection created by Stanford. Three boxes of photo prints and lithographs depicting various locations in California.

items.description: Includes several pieces: 1. Carnegie; historical landmark in Corral Hollow (11 p.). 2. Tesla, Pottery and Carnegie in Corral Hollow, 1892-1912 (17 pp.), by Mrs. Josephine Leary, of Stockton, Calif. 3. Notes about California registered historical landmarks No. 740 and 755 (including the home of Edward B. Carrell).

items.title: General Subjects photography collection
items.description: Contains photographs and picture postcards depicting scenes of California places, people, activities, and cultural resources, mainly from the 1870s to the 1980s. Each listing represents a file containing from one to more than fifty images.

items.title: Harry C. Peterson lantern slides, 1892-1917
items.description: Harry Claude Peterson was born in Algona, Iowa, in 1876, son of Julius E. Peterson, a Norwegian mechanician. Leland Stanford had learned of the elder Peterson in Europe and brought him to Stanford University to teach machine shop. Young Harry was educated in public schools in Algona and Palo Alto.

items.title: Harry C. Peterson papers, ca. 1880-1944
items.description: Harry Claude Peterson never met a historical fact or artifact that he didn't like. The inveterate historian spent his entire adult life in one position after another related to history, particularly California Gold Rush Days. Harry was born in Algona, Iowa, in 1876, son of Julius E. Peterson, a Norwegian mechanician.

items.title: Henry A. Holden stereograph collection, 1911
items.description: Henry Ambrose Holden attended Stanford University between 1911 and his death in 1914. Views taken by Holden and published by Underwood and Underwood as a boxed set. Subjects include Stanford University buildings and a student race on Lake Lagunita; homes in Palo Alto.

items.title: Illustrated newspapers reporting news from Santa Clara County, 1897-1900
items.description: Articles describe leading business establishments and institutions in Santa Clara County and its cities. Includes many illustrations and several pages of advertisements. The 1900 edition states that this is the oldest illustrated paper in California, established in 1870.

items.title: John C. Beckett collection of Stanford and Palo Alto dance cards, 1931-1939
items.description: Collection includes invitations and dance cards to Stanford events, including the Jolly-Up; dances at the Palo Alto High School; private dance parties in Palo Alto and nearby locations, including one at the Duveneck's Hidden Villa Ranch; and dances at other schools.

items.title: Mayfield, Calif. promotional leaflet
items.description: Mayfield was a municipality adjacent to Stanford University; it is now part of Palo Alto. Promotional leaflet with map detailing the advantages of Mayfield; two copies.

items.title: Rosebrook family glass plate negatives of Palo Alto and Stanford University, c.1890-1920
items.description: The plates came to Stanford in 1993 from Catherine and Joseph Rosebrook's daughters Genevieve "Gene" Rosebrook Snow (1903-1998) and her younger sister Margaret Rosebrook Westall (1911-1995). Joseph Rosebrook was the son of Margaret and George Rosebrook.

items.title: Santa Clara County, Fiesta de las rosas records, 1926-1932
items.description: Includes some administrative material including financial records, files, and correspondence, as well as programs and newsclippings.

items.title: Sherwood Hall photograph album, 1939-1957
items.description: Librarian at Stanford University. Photographs by William Moran, 1942, and clippings, 1942-54, regarding Sherwood Hall, the Menlo Park residence of Timothy Hopkins; estate sale catalog, 1942; letters to Hitchcock from Mary Hopkins, 1939, and William Moran, 1943; two postcards.

items.title: Ted Huggins photographs of San Francisco and other California locations
items.description: Contains images of San Francisco, including the Golden Gate Bridge, Treasure Island and the Golden Gate International Exposition, the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, various ships, various locations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Northern California. Includes a few photos of Southern California.

items.description: Includes minutes of the Executive Committee, Planning Committee of the Western States Division, and the Administrative Committee; Stanford and Palo Alto people represented include Ray Lyman Wilbur, Thomas A. Storey, and Dr. Russel V. Lee.

items.title: Children's Hospital at Stanford records, 1917-1977
items.description: Originally the Stanford Convalescent Home, established on the Stanford campus in 1919 for needy children with long term illness, this privately supported organization changed its name to the Children's Hospital at Stanford in 1970.

items.title: Clelia Duel Mosher papers, 1886-1940
items.description: Clelia Duel Mosher, the daughter of Cornelius Duel Mosher, M.D. and Sarah Burritt Mosher, was born on December 16, 1863 in Albany, New York. She graduated from Wellesley College in 1891, and spent the next year studying at both Cornell University and the University of Wisconsin.

items.title: Contagious disease reporting requirement : broadside, 1906
items.description: Notice issued by Dr. James W. Ward, President, San Francisco Health Commission, requesting all persons having knowldege of contagious disease to report to headquarters of the Board of Health. Broadside refers to the San Francisco earthquake and fire of 1906.

items.title: Esther Bridgman Clark papers, 1891-ca. 1980 (bulk 1914-1968)
items.description: Esther Bridgman Clark, daughter of Arthur B. Clark, Stanford's first art professor, was one of the first women doctors in Palo Alto. She earned her a.b. from Stanford University in 1921 and her M.D. from Stanford University Medical School in 1925.

items.title: Esther Clark papers, 1947-1973
items.description: Collection includes Clark's work with childhood accident prevention, the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, personal subject files, reprints, and photographs.

items.title: Halsted Holman papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: The papers of Halsted Holman include publications; newspaper and magazine clippings pertaining to Holman's research interests; correspondence; typescript and handwritten manuscripts and outlines for talks; anonymous patient surveys; self-care materials for patients; project reports; email and website print-outs.

items.title: Harold K. Faber papers, 1895-1979
items.description: A founder of the Childrens Hospital at Stanford, Harold K. Faber was a professor of Pediatrics known for his polio research. Collection includes plans for the H.K. Faber Library; personal family papers and photos; the minutes of the Stanford Convalescent Home Auxiliary, 1933-1935.

items.description: Leo Stanley was born in Oregon in 1886 and raised in San Luis Obispo County, California. After receiving his bachelor's degree at Stanford University in 1903 and matriculating to Cooper Medical College in 1908, Stanley served his medical residency at San Quentin State Prison.

items.title: Leo Leonidas Stanley papers, 1916-1950
items.description: Chiefly diaries entitled Events of the Day from period of professional work as the Resident Physician of the Medical Department of the California State Prison at San Quentin.

items.title: Maison de Santé de la Société Française de Bienfaisance Mutuelle logbook, 1903-1908
items.description: Logbook for the French Hospital in San Francisco, with entries spanning the years 1903 to 1908. Each entry contains information about a patient, such as name, nationality, date of entry, doctor, and diagnosis. Includes entries on and around April 18, 1906, when San Francisco suffered a major earthquake and fire.

items.title: Maison de Santé de la Société Française de Bienfaisance Mutuelle logbook
items.description: The French Hospital was founded as La Societe Francaise de Bienfaisance Mutuelle on December 28, 1851. It was established by the French Benevolent Society to serve French-Americans in the San Francisco Bay Area and was the first private hospital in San Francisco.

items.title: Peninsula Hospital, Incorporated, records
items.description: The hospital established by Peninsula Hospital, Incorporated, was Palo Alto's second hospital; the first was opened by the Students Guild of Leland Stanford Junior University during the typhoid epidemic of 1902-03. Includes list of original stockholders, 1908.
