items.title: Russel V. Lee family papers, circa 1895-2014, bulk 1940s-1970s.
items.description: Dr. Russel Van Arsdale Lee founded the Palo Alto Medical Clinic (PAMC), one of the first group practice clinics in the United States. He was a champion of rights for abortion, prepaid medical care and free drugs for addicts, and a leader in health education. His five sons all became doctors.

items.title: Russel V.A. Lee papers, 1935-1976
items.description: Chiefly correspondence together with supporting subject material, including pamphlets, minutes, and newsletters, related to work as Founder and Director of the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, 1924-61. Major subject groupings in health insurance, health care for the aging, community medical clinics and group medical practice.

items.description: At the time of these reports the Stanford University Hospital (also known as Lane Hospital) was located in San Francisco. In addition to a census of patients, these typescript reports cover the nursing school, medical supplies, dietary kitchens, operating room, housekeeping, engineering services, clinics, social…

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Anderson family papers, 1848-1963
items.description: The Anderson Family Papers cover the history of a distinguished family that, up to a point, followed a somewhat typical pattern in America. Of Scottish-English origins, with a short history in the Maritime Provinces, Canada, the family came to the United States in the middle of the nineteenth century.

items.title: Archive of Takeo Shikamura and Hatsu Shikamura
items.description: Collection of Takeo Shikamura’s papers and photo albums, Hatsu (Helen) Yamamoto's and her family’s papers, photos albums, journals.

items.title: Brasch family papers, 1891-1920
items.description: Otto and Caroline Brasch had immigrated from Germany sometime during the 1870's and gave encouragement to their children to improve themselves by the writing of letters. Collection consists primarily of letters written by the children of Otto and Caroline Brasch to their brother Frederick E. Brasch.

items.title: Charles J. Sullivan papers, 1918-1921
items.description: Charles J. Sullivan attended Stanford University 1916-18; he married Rowena Gray on Feb. 12, 1920. These letters were written to his fiancée Rowena Gray, in Chowchilla, CA, while Sullivan was at Stanford and training for the military, 1918, and then working in Los Angeles, June-August 1919, and Salinas, 1919-21.

items.title: Christian K. Binkley, a Biographical Sketch : typescript, 1977-1983
items.description: Biography of Christian K. Binkley [1870-1938], Stanford class of 1899, by his son Charles, briefly discussing his public school teaching career, his attempts at farming in Santa Clara County, and his poetry and writing. Also included is a letter from Sidney Cowell, 1983, regarding the Binkley family and this biography.

items.title: David Locke Webster, "Reminiscences of a Rolling Stone"
items.description: David Locke Webster, professor of physics (1920-1954; emeritus, 1954-1977) and chairman of the Physics Department at Stanford (1920-1942), was born in Boston November 6, 1888. He received his B.A. (1910) and Ph.D. (1913) from Harvard University.

items.title: Diary of William Harrison Hanns
items.description: A manuscript diary of William Harrison Hanns, future newspaper editor, Indian trader, and I.W.W. supporter, born in Arlington Heights, Illinois, kept while living in Palo Alto and Los Angeles, California, and while in Gallup, New Mexico from 1906-1909. [From dealer description].

items.title: Ellen Coit Elliott papers, 1891-1942
items.description: Ellen Coit Elliott, wife of Orrin Leslie Elliott, Stanford University's first registrar, was the author of several books of poetry and an autobiography, IT HAPPENED THIS WAY; AMERICAN SCENE.

items.title: Emil Fischer papers, 1865-1984
items.description: Emil Fischer (October 9, 1852 – July 15, 1919) was a German chemist who won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Emil Fischer's son, Hermann Otto Laurenz Fischer (December 16, 1888 - March 9, 1960) left Nazi Germany in the 1930s and in 1948 became a professor of biochemistry at the University of California Berkeley.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza photographs, 1900-1972
items.description: Includes photostatic pictures of Ernesto Galarza's mother, Henrietta Galarza, ca. 1900, sisters Nora and Henrietta and younger brother, ca. 1905, and pictures as an adult in 1959, 1965, and 1972.

items.title: Farris Family Papers, 1908-1976
items.description: Fauna Wynne "Pat" Farris and Edna Esther Ingles Farris both earned A.B. degrees in English from Stanford University in May 1917. They were married in 1920. Correspondence, photographs, diaries, and ephemera Correspondence, photographs, diaries, and ephemera.

items.title: Gilbert Russell Jones photograph album, 1894-1935
items.description: Gilbert R. Jones attended Stanford University during 1906 and 1907; his career included teaching shop at University High School in Oakland, CA. His brother Kenneth Inskip Jones attended Stanford from 1905-1908; he was Deputy District Attorney for Solano County, CA.

items.title: Handmade keepsake commemorating the golden wedding anniversary of Mary Kellogg Crittenden and Timothy Hopkins
items.description: Timothy Hopkins was born in 1859 to an Irish housekeeper who entered the service of the fabulously wealthy Mark Hopkins, one of the four investors who funded the First Transcontinental Railroad.

items.title: Helen Stanford Canfield papers, 1913-1945
items.description: Daughter of Josiah Winslow Stanford, Jr., and grand-niece of Leland Stanford. Correspondence, memorabilia, newsclippings, photographs, and albums, belonging to Helen Stanford Canfield and her husband David Canfield.

items.title: Journal and letters
items.description: Consists of: 1) bound manuscript with t.p.: A.B. Saroyan, 114 King Street, New-York, Nov. 24th '905, Journey from Erzeroum to New-York City : second part, from Trabizond to Marseille; 2) letter dated 1906; 3) letter dated Campbell, Cal. Mar. 26, 11.

items.title: Leo L. Stanley diaries, 1918-1968
items.description: Leo L. Stanley, born 1886 in Oregon, graduated from Cooper Medical College of Stanford University in 1912. He spent most of his life as Chief Physician and Surgeon at the California State Prison at San Quentin. He did take time out to travel, however, usually as the ship's doctor on large luxury cruises.

items.title: Martin E. Johnson photograph album, 1926-1950
items.description: Mr. Martin was a merchant seaman, probably of Swedish descent, with family apparently in the Seattle area.

items.title: Meyer family papers, 1850-1971
items.description: A native Californian, J. Henry Meyer was a successful San Francisco businessman. He was an executive, a banker, and served on the boards of many companies including Wells Fargo Bank, the Spring Valley Water Company, and the California Street Cable Railroad Company. In 1878 he married Eugenie Hillegass of Berkeley.

items.title: Mildred Crew Brooke: an unfinished manuscript of reminiscences and some extracts from her diary
items.description: Mildred Crew Brooke Hoover (1872-1940) was a California history writer who published "Historic Spots in California" in 1932. She was also the state regent of the Daughters of the American Revolution.

items.title: Minna Stillman diary
items.description: Minna Stillman earned an A.B. in mathematics at Stanford in 1903; she was a document librarian in the Stanford University library. Diary includes entries from a European trip, 1898-99, and an account of the 1906 earthquake, primarily its impact at Stanford University.

items.title: Misselwitz and Crawford family papers, 1870-1968
items.description: This collection concerns two American families, related by marriage, who chose not to remain in their native Kansas, but sought opportunity wherever it took them. Their individual perambulations are reflected chiefly in their collection of photographs; very little correspondence is contained in their papers.

items.title: Mrs. Sanford's scrapbook calendar
items.description: Scrapbook containing a page for each week of the year created by various friends of a woman, Mrs. Sanford, of Palo Alto, in convalesence. Pages feature poems, photographs and cyanotypes, drawings and watercolors, letters, graphs and postcards contributed by different people.

items.title: Newcomer family papers, 1850-1972
items.description: A diary or record book of Sidney's life from birth to age 24, kept by his mother, together with other of her papers. Lecture notes that H. Sidney Newcomer kept reflecting pre-World War I mathematics and optics education at the University of Wisconsin. Patents, 1929-1972, awarded to H. Sidney Newcomer.

items.title: Ray Lyman Wilbur personal papers, 1829-1949 (inclusive) 1875-1949 (bulk)
items.description: Ray Lyman Wilbur graduated from Stanford University (B.S. 1896, M.S. 1897) and from Cooper Medical College (M.D. 1899). He served as lecturer and professor of physiology and of medicine (1897-1903), Dean of the Cooper Medical College (Stanford) (1911-1916), third President of Stanford University (1916-1943)… Includes…

items.title: Rosemary Benet Dawson collection of material relating to Kathleen Norris and the Norris Ranch, circa 1887-1955
items.description: Collection consists of materials created and compiled by Rosemary Benet Dawson and relating to Kathleen Norris and the Norris Ranch-"La Estancia" in Los Gatos. Rosemary Benet Dawson was daughter of Kathleen's sister Teresa and the poet William Rose Benet.

items.title: Samuel Franklin Leib photograph album, circa 1900
items.description: Lawyer and one of the original trustees of Stanford University. Photographs of Leib's home and gardens in San Jose; also includes four views of Stanford University and one view from Mount Hamilton Photographs of Leib's home and gardens in San Jose.

items.title: Shafter Family scrapbook, 1910-1914

Founded in 1932, Ran was the only battery manufacturer at that time in the Middle East.

items.title: Ralph Heintz prints, tracings, and sketches, undated
items.description: Ralph M. Heintz was chemical engineer and a physical chemist. He was a leading figure in early electronics and radio engineering. After serving in the U.S. Army Signal Corps in World War I, Heintz earned a chemistry degree from Stanford University.

items.title: Stauffer Chemical Company records, 1881-1987
items.description: The Stauffer Chemical Company was founded in 1885 in San Francisco by two European immigrants, John Stauffer, Sr. and Christian de Guigne. The company mainly produced herbicides for corn and rice. The Stauffer Chemical Company records consists of materials documenting the company's activities.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Internet and the web

items.title: A History of the Internet, 1962-1992 : poster
items.description: Includes a time-line of key events, together with graphics and portraits.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: Anne Draper papers, 1938-1973
items.description: Correspondence, articles, statements, reports, newsletters, newsclippings, notes, photographs and posters, primarily concerned with agricultural labor organizations and issues in California. The Anne Draper Papers reflect Draper's work as a trade union organizer, writer, and champion of the rights of farm workers.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Cesar Chavez East Coast & Canada Tour 1969
items.description: In the fall of 1969, Cesar Chavez toured the East Coast of the United States and Canada to build support for a national boycott of non-union harvested grapes and other produce.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Cesar Chavez/UFW gallery, 1968-1974
items.description: United Farmworkers Union (UFW, AFL-CIO) - organizing & field work. Between 1968 and 1974, at the invitation of the UFW President and organizer Cesar Chavez, Bob Fitch photographed union organizing activities including.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Farmworker Union Field Organizing & Special Actions, 1969-1975
items.description: For nearly 100 years, California's pastures of plenty were controlled by a coalition of growers, bankers, and political interests who systematically and often brutally suppressed labor organizing efforts.

items.title: Bracero Oral History interviews
items.description: Includes thumb drive and several documents and photographs in connection with Ornelas Bracero Oral History Project.

items.title: Charles Batom papers, 1944-1975
items.description: Mr. Batom was an African American union member and a member of civil rights organizations. He lived in Oakland, California. Includes union items.

items.title: Eric Hakon Thomsen papers, 1936-1941
items.description: Correspondence with John Steinbeck, 1936-1940, including 3 cards, 4 letters, and 1 telegram from Steinbeck to Thomsen, 2 letters from Carol Steinbeck to Thomsen, and carbons of 2 letters from Thomsen to Steinbeck. Letters make reference to the migrant camps and both Tom Collins and Ray Strong.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza papers, 1936-1993
items.description: Ernesto Galarza was born in Jalcocotan in the state of Nayarit, Mexico, in 1905. In 1910, Ernesto, his mother, and two maternal uncles left their village to find employment and escape the depredations during the Madero Revolt. They spent three years traveling northward before settling in Sacramento, California.

items.title: Frank Bardacke papers, 1960-1990
items.description: Frank Bardacke is a historian, author, educator, trade unionist, and political activist. Contains manuscript drafts of his book "Trampling Out The Vintage," United Farm Worker administrative material, research files, correspondence, and recordings of interviews and UFW meetings.

items.title: Fred Ross papers, 1920-2003
items.description: Fred W. Ross was born August 23, 1910 in San Francisco to Fred W. and Daisy C. Ross. He grew up in the Echo Park neighborhood of Los Angeles and attended Belmont High School until 1929. An English literature and social science major, he graduated from the University of Southern California in 1937.

items.title: James L. Vizzard papers, 1942-1983
items.description: Correspondence, reports, legislative testimony, speeches, articles, minutes, agendas, newsclippings, oral history tape and transcript, and photographs, documenting Vizzard's career as a lobbyist and worker on behalf of rural poor, migrants and braceros.

items.title: Joan London papers, 1962-1970
items.description: Joan London (1901-1971) was the librarian for the California Labor Federation from the 1940s until her retirement in 1962. Afterwards, continued to be active in workers' movements and was a member of the Citizens for Farm Labor.

items.title: Marion Moses, M.D., papers
items.description: Marion Moses (1936-2020) was a nurse, physician, activist, and author. Marion Moses was born on January 24, 1936 in Wheeling, West Virginia. After graduating from Charleston Catholic High School, Moses attend Georgetown University where she graduated with a degree in nursing in 1957.

items.title: Nosotros venceremos : digital videodisc (dvd, 11 minutes)and portfolio of 24 photographs, 1960-2004
items.description: The film, in Spanish, is "made from still photographs as an organizing tool for the United Farm Workers. The film-maker combines his photogrpahs with the sounds of the movement: from the march to Sacramento, through Cesar's fast, to the union label on a grape box." [from promotional brochure].

items.title: Original broadsides and circulars relating to the 1966 Farmworkers Peregrinacion from Delano to Sacramento, 1966
items.description: Collection of five mimeographed documents on various paper stocks, each 8.5 x 11 inches; three printed on recto only, two printed on both sides. These pieces document one of the seminal events in Mexican-American political history.

items.title: Spiders in the house and workers in the field : Video interview transcript, 1971 Mar. 1.
items.description: Galarza discusses Mexican American labor history, leading up to Joseph DiGiorgio and the DiGiorgio Fruit Corporation and the union organizing and strike attempts in 1949-1950. He discusses the bracero program, illegal immigration of Mexicans, and the political maneuvering to break the strike.

items.title: Viva la causa! : Songs and sound from the Delano strike, por los huelguistas del Delano y el Teatro Campesino
items.description: The recording recounts the farm workers' 300 mile pilgrimage from Delano to Sacramento, California, in March, 1966. Live recordings of song and spoken word performances.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Magnetic recording and data storage

items.title: Alex Maxey papers, circa 1950s
items.description: Collection consits of Maxey’s lab book of mechanical drawings, patent applications, large-scale drawings, and photographs from his time working for AMPEX.

items.title: Ampex Collection Addenda
items.description: Various smaller collections related to the Ampex Corporation, the development of magnetic recording on tape, and stereophonic sound. This is a group of small collections, assembled from various donors, related to the history of the Ampex Corporation and its role in the development of sound recording on tape and…

items.title: Ampex Corporation historical videotapes
items.description: Video recordings produced or used by Ampex. Five reels of 1960s-70s video tape recordings, all labeled "Ampex Training Department." Most were produced by Ampex themselves. The tapes were given to Stanford by John Eckland.

items.title: Ampex Corporation records, ca. 1944-2005 (bulk 1944-1999)
items.description: Founded in 1944 in San Carlos, California by Alexander M. Poniatoff, an electrical engineer born in Russia. Ampex is a technology leader in high-performance digital information recording and storage products utilized in a variety of fields, including scientific, government, finance, telecommunications, manufacturing…

items.title: Crosby-Mullin B-42 (pre-Ampex video machine) slides and ephemera, circa 1985
items.description: This collection consists of a single carousel of slides documenting videorecording equipment developed at Bing Crosby Enterprises (BCE) under Jack Mullin's direction as well as notes and ephemera. The slides were taken by Hans Dietze.

items.title: Florence James collection of Alexander M. Poniatoff and Ampex Corporation papers, 1964-1978
items.description: Included in box 1 is a biography of Poniatoff (probably an autobiography), circa 1978, written when Mr. Poniatoff was 86 years old. There are also original photographs, excerpts from the Ampex Monitor, and some correspondence. Box 2 contains the tape recorder.

items.title: Fred Pfost papers, 1952-2018
items.description: Born near Boise, Idaho, Fred Pfost (1928-2023) was an American engineer and the last surviving member of the pioneering 1956 Ampex video tape recorder development team which included Ray Dolby, Charles Ginsburg, Alex Maxey, Charles Anderson, and Shelby Henderson.

items.title: James Arthur Miller papers, 1912-1971
items.description: James Arthur Miller (1891-1971) was an inventor, engineer and businessman best known for his 1930s audio recording system Millertape. Miller was born in Crescent City, California and graduated from Stanford University in 1913 after having built his first radio in 1907.

items.title: Neal Kyser McNaughten papers, 1951-2001
items.description: Neal Kyser McNaughten served as Ampex's Vice President for Professional Products from 1957 to 1962. The papers include copies of corporate memos, personal correspondence, photographs, and other documents related to Neal Kyser McNaughten's career at Ampex.

items.title: Philip Rice papers, 1953-1981
items.description: Philip Rice was an American physicist with a particular interest in vision, ultrasound, optics, and electronics. From 1942-1945 he was a staff member at the Radiation Lab at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology working on the development of radar systems for the US Navy.

items.title: Ray Dolby papers, circa 1940s - 2000s
items.description: Ray Milton Dolby was an American engineer whose inventions and company, Dolby Laboratories, have had a profound effect on the storage, transmission, and reproduction of audio and video. Born in Portland, Oregon in 1933, Ray Dolby grew up in the area that later became Silicon Valley.

items.title: Richard Hess Mullin-Palmer Tape Restoration Project Collection
items.description: The Richard Hess Mullin-Palmer Tape Restoration Project Collection chronicles the widespread dissemination of one of the most important advances in sound recording technology: magnetic recording on tape. The Richard Hess Collection chronicles the early history of tape recording in the United States.

items.title: The Joe Roizen film archive [videorecording], ca. 1955-1975
items.description: Joe Roizen was a television and broadcasting technologist, author, and consultant. These films were preserved as part of the Roizen estate. They were created by Roizen to represent global telecommunication samples.

items.title: Tom Rose collection documenting the electronics industry, 1964 - 1988
items.description: Tom Rose worked as a Design Engineer at Dynasonic Systems of Dallas, Texas. He held the same position at Continental Electronics, also located in Dallas.

items.title: William Slatkin papers, circa 1940-2019
items.description: Materials related to the history of Ampex Corporation. Includes documents, photocopies, audio recordings of interviews with former Ampex executives and engineers, and a set of Ampex annual reports. Some of this material has been posted online as The Ampex Story website: www.theampexstory.com.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: Donald MacQuivey papers, circa 1950-1990
items.description: Donald R. MacQuivey (1913-1993) was an engineer and policy analyst in the field of telecommunications. He received several degrees from Stanford University, among them Radio Engineering in 1935, Electrical Engineering in 1939, and an MBA in 1942.

items.title: The Lenkurt Demodulator, 1961-1976
items.description: General telephone and electronics: video, voice and data transmission systems. The Lenkurt Demodulator is circulated monthly to technicians, engineers, and managers employed by companies of government agencies who use and operate communications systems, and to educational institutions. Incomplete run.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: 10th anniversary celebration of founding : cassette audio tape, 1958 Nov. 2.
items.description: The tape begins with comments by Russel Varian. Apparently his opening words were lost in transcribing from reel-to-reel to cassette. Numerous speakers follow.

items.title: CPI/Eimac (Communication & Power Industries, Eimac Division) media collection and files, circa 1944-1990
items.description: Eitel-McCullough Inc. was founded in 1934 by radio engineers and business partners, Bill Eitel and Jack McCullough in San Bruno, California. The company started out developing innovative radio vacuum tubes that provided higher frequency transmission for radio communication and eventually transitioned into components…

items.title: Cyril Frank Elwell papers, 1930-1961
items.description: Cyril Frank Elwell (1884 – 1963) was an American inventor and pioneer in the development of radio-telegraphy and long-distance communication. Born in Melbourne, Australia in 1884 to an American father and a German mother, Elwell arrived in the United States in 1902.

items.title: Don Preist papers, circa 1934-2002
items.description: Donald Harold Preist, born in England in 1916, first became associated with various aspects of radar development in the late 1930s when conducting early experiments on the detection of ships and the development of high-power ground radar transmitters.

items.title: Edward Ginzton papers, circa 1937-1992
items.description: Co-founder of Varian Associates and a pioneer in microwave tube technology and linear accelerator development. As a graduate student at Stanford during the 1930's, Ginzton joined Russell and Sigurd Varian and physics professors William W. Hansen and David L. Webster to develop the klystron tube, an integral part of…

items.title: Eimac Historical artifacts, ca. 1950-1980
items.description: Eitel-McCullough Inc. ("Eimac") was a company based in San Bruno, California and an early innovator of radio transmitter tubes. Diode cuff links and tie clasp, together with a lighter with the Eimac logo.

items.title: Eimac News, 1942-1961
items.description: Publication of the Eimac company featuring employees, events, and engineering activities at their San Bruno, California and Salt Lake City, Utah plants. Some years are incomplete.

items.title: Ervin J. Nalos papers, 1939-1993
items.description: Ervin J. Nalos, a naturalized United States citizen, was born September 10, 1924 in Prague. Dr. Nalos' undergraduate study was done at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, B.A. Sc., 1946. Graduate work, M.A. Sc., 1947, was also started in Vancouver.

items.title: Jack McCullough interview by Robert Herdman and Jack Strother, 25 Nov. 1997
items.description: Co-founder of Eitel-McCullough Inc. (EIMAC), now a division of Varian Associates.

items.title: John Paul (J.P.) Smith papers, circa 1927-1970
items.description: John Paul Smith (frequently referred to as J.P.) was born in 1905 and received a Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering in 1927 from Texas A & M College. John Paul (frequently referred to as J.P.) Smith worked on the early development of television at Radio Corporation of America (RCA).

items.title: Karl R. Spangenberg papers, 1935-1961
items.description: Karl Spangenberg (1910-1964) served as a Professor of Electrical Engineering at Stanford. He was a member of the American Physical Society and became an IRE (now IEEE) Associate in 1934, Senior Member in 1945, and Fellow in 1949.

items.title: Lester L. Libby papers, ca. 1936-1984
items.description: Lester Louis Libby was born at Hartford, Connecticut in 1914. He received the B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical engineering from the Worcester Polytechnic Institute in 1935 and 1936, respectively.

items.title: Marvin Chodorow papers, 1929-1993 (inclusive), 1943-1974 (bulk)
items.description: Chodorow received his B.A. in 1934 at the University of Buffalo, and his Ph.D., 1939, at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He taught at Pennsylvania State College and College of the City of New York and worked with the Sperry Gyroscope Company (1943-47), before joining the faculty at Stanford in 1947.

items.title: Oral history transcription, 21 Jan. 1974
items.description: The interview by Arthur L. Norberg covers high school and first jobs (1-8), interest in amateur radio (8-18), Heintz and Kaufman, Inc. (18-44), Eitel McCullough, Inc. (44-96), and appendices (including copies of photographs).

items.title: Oswald G. Villard papers, 1932-1998 (inclusive), 1958-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Oswald Garrison Villard Jr. (1916-2004), a leader in electromagnetic theory and experimental methods, earned his engineer's degree in 1943 and his Ph.D. in 1949 at Stanford, studying with Dr. F. E. Terman.

items.title: Pert-o-graph (Program evaluation and review technique) : time estimate computer, 1962
items.description: A time estimate computer with resource cost scale. Scales include expected time, pessimistic time, most likely time, optimistic time, and on the reverse, the resources cost. The accompanying booklet explains how to use it.

items.title: Rudolf Kompfner papers, 1937-1981
items.description: Professor of Applied Physics at Stanford University and world renowned communications scientist, Rudolf Kompfner came to Stanford in 1973 after a distinguished career at Bell Telephone Laboratories, Oxford University, and with British government research.

items.title: Russell and Sigurd Varian papers, 1892-1988
items.description: Russsell and Sigurd Varian were co-inventors, with William W. Hansen, of the klystron and rhumbatron and co-founders of Varian Associates. Educated at Stanford University, physicist and inventor Russell Varian began his career with Philo Farnsworth on early television technology and with Humble Oil on instrumentation…

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Physics, correspondence, 1937-1949
items.description: Correspondence and news clippings regarding the Klystron Tube Research Project, 1937-1945; correspondence between department chairman Paul Kirkpatrick and Stanford President Donald B. Tresidder regarding budget and faculty matters, 1943-1947.

items.title: Stanford University, W.W. Hansen Laboratories, klystron reports and patents, 1936-1949
items.description: Brothers Sigurd and Russell Varian worked in collaboration with Prof. William W. Hansen beginning in 1937 to invent and perfect the Klystron, a device for generating high-power microwaves. Much of the work was conducted at the Sperry Gyroscope Company.

items.title: Sterling McNees papers, undated
items.description: Consists of the personal papers of Sterling McNees. The addendum contains a Report on RRL Project A500 (Tuba) from the Radio Research Laboratory, Harvard University along with research materials about Project A500.

items.title: U.S. Patent #2,558,021, 1951 June 26.
items.description: Includes early petitions, correspondence, and final patent for thermionic vacuum tubes and circuits, which was invented by Russell Varian and David Packard, and assigned to the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University in 1951 for 17 years.

items.title: William W. Eitel papers, ca. 1953-1979
items.description: William W. Eitel joined Heinz & Kaufman in 1929; he was manager of the tube manufacturing department for five years. He was a co-founder of Eitel-McCollough Inc. (EIMAC), now a division of Varian Associates. Files, both correspondence and subject, as well as the film, Eimac Richfield Success Story kinescope, 1953.

items.title: William Webster Hansen papers, 1925-1945
items.description: William Webster Hansen was Professor of Physics and Director of the Microwave Laboratory at Stanford University, 1929-1949. Memorial Resolution for William Webster Hansen. William Webster Hansen died May 23, 1949.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Semiconductors

items.title: "The Legacy of Shockley Semiconductor" [videorecording]
items.description: Videorecording of the roundtable discussion held on September 27, 2005, moderated by Leslie Berlin, featuring Gordon Moore, Jay Last, Julius Blank, all co-founders of Fairchild Semiconductor, and James F. Gibbons, professor of electrical engineering at Stanford.

items.title: A case study in realizing the American dream : Sanders and Advanced Micro Devices : the first fifteen years, 1969-1984 : typescript, 2004
items.description: Insider's story of the development of AMD, originally written in 1984 and reworked in 2004.

items.title: Armen Sahagun papers, 1954-1965
items.description: The Armen Sahagun papers consist of material related to the development of semiconductor technology during the 1950s-60s. Included are two binders of engineering data, price lists, and other reports from American Micro Devices, a semiconductor manufacturing company founded in Minnesota in 1961.

items.title: Bruce E. Deal collection of Fairchild Semiconductor publications, 1958-1987
items.description: Bruce E. Deal was born in Lincoln, Nebraska in 1927. After serving in the U.S. Army, he attended Nebraska Wesleyan University where he received an A.B. in Chemistry in 1950. Subsequently, he received M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in 1953 and 1955 from Iowa State University at Ames, Iowa, majoring in Physical Chemistry.

items.title: Christophe Lécuyer research material on the history of Silicon Valley, 1999-2003
items.description: Christophe Lécuyer (born 1963) is an economic analyst, author, and professor. He has written books on Fairchild Semiconductor and the history of Silicon Valley. A graduate of the Ecole Normale Supérieure, he earned his Ph.D. in history from Stanford University in 2002.

items.title: Fairchild Camera and Instrument 35 mm slides, 1960-1970
items.description: Includes early pictures of researchers and projects, including a progression of chips from the early transistor to the latest 4500. These were used in Rob Walker's SILICON DESTINY, 1992.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor 50th anniversary [videorecording]
items.description: On October 4, 2007, Julius Blank, Jay Last, Gordon Moore, and Arthur Rock--three Fairchild Semiconductor founders and the venture capitalist who backed them -- discussed the firm's early years and its significance in a panel discussion moderated by Leslie Berlin of the Silicon Valley Archives at Stanford University.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor Corporation: files of Steve Allen, photographer, circa 1960-1985
items.description: In 1957, New York based Fairchild Camera and Instrument Corporation made a historic business decision when they sponsored the formation of Fairchild Semiconductor in Palo Alto, California. The collection documents executive employees, sales force, fabrication facilities, and products of Fairchild Semiconductor.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor technical reports and progress reports, 1965-1987
items.description: Arranged chronologically, the published listing includes authors of technical reports and dates of progress reports.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor, 1957-1977 : booklet of reproduced historical documents, ca. 1978
items.description: Includes important letters, telegrams, photographs, newsclippings, etc.

items.title: Fairchild, The Fairchild chronicles [videorecording]
items.description: Tells the story of the company that invented the integrated circuit, describing the events that spawned the first generation of Silicon Valley technology companies. It covers the period from Fairchild's founding in 1957 to the purchase of the company by National Semiconductor in 1986.

items.title: Gerald Pearson papers, 1934-1987
items.description: Professor of Electrical Engineering at Stanford University from 1960 to 1987 and Director of Stanford Solid State Electronics Laboratory. Research Physicist at Bell Telephone Laboratories from 1929 to 1960 in the field of solid-state electronics.

items.title: Gordon Moore Fairchild Semiconductor patent notebooks, 1957-1968
items.description: Gordon Earle Moore (1929- ), was co-founder of Intel Corporation and progenitor of "Moore's Law." Moore worked at Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory, was one of the "Traitorous Eight" who left Shockley to start Fairchild Semiconductor Corporation in 1957 and, with Robert Noyce, co-founded Intel Corporation in 1968.

items.title: Interview with Victor Grinich by Christophe Lécuyer : typscript, 1996
items.description: Victor Grinich (November 24, 1924 - November 5, 2000) was a pioneer in the semiconductor industry. He worked at the seminal Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory of Beckman Instruments, and then left with other disgruntled members to create the influential Fairchild Semiconductor corporation.

items.title: Interviews conducted for research on THE INTEGRATED CIRCUIT; a case study of product innovation in the electronics industry, 1965
items.description: References to Fairchild Semiconductor are numerous.

items.title: Jay T. Last papers, 1940-2012
items.description: Jay T. Last (1929-2021) was an American engineer active in the early days of Silicon Valley. He completed a BS in optics at the University of Rochester in 1951 before completing a PhD in physics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

items.title: Jean Hoerni papers, 1950-2000
items.description: Jean A. Hoerni (1924-1997) was a Swiss-American engineer active in the early days of Silicon Valley. He completed a BS in mathematics from the University of Geneva before completing two physics PhDs. at Geneva and Cambridge.

items.title: Letters from William Shockley to Julius Blank, 1956 March 18 and 19.
items.description: An employment offer with terms, together with a follow-up letter asking Blank to discuss the offer with his supervisor at Western Electric so that there be no suggestion of "indirect methods.".

items.title: Photographs of integrated circuits, etc., ca. 1964-1995
items.description: Primarily manufacturing images relating to the work of Robert C. Hall at Fairchild Semiconductor; also some failure analysis photos. There are also some historical reports from the 1960s relating to the work of G. Tripp and J.H. Friedrich.

items.title: Podfather : Robert Noyce and the rise of Silicon Valley
items.description: The epic story of silicon chip inventor Robert Noyce, godfather of today's digital world. Recalls the heady days of Silicon Valley's seminal start-ups and tells how Noyce also founded Intel, the company responsible for more than 80% of the microprocessors in personal computers.

items.title: Proposal for custom integrated circuit organization : photocopy of typescript by Jean A. Hoerni, circa 1966-1967
items.description: Hoerni's summary of this paper states, "the new organization will be geared to provide not only diffusion and epitaxial capabilities, but also sputtering and die-electric isolation techniques in order to achieve greatest flexibility in custom circuits fabrication." He discusses the market and the forecast for custom…

items.title: Raytheon Semiconductor files kept to monitor the electronics industry, 1965-1986
items.description: Raytheon's Semiconductor Division was established in Mountain View, California in 1968 by its parent company, Raytheon Company of Lexington, Massachusetts, which, in 1990, was described as "one of the largest and most diversified electronics companies in the United States." In the early 1990s, the company was…

items.title: Research material about Robert Noyce, ca. 1970-2005
items.description: Leslie Berlin received her Ph.D. in History from Stanford in 2001. She is currently (2005) a visiting scholar in the Program in the History and Philosophy of Science and Technology. She is also the Project Historian for the Silicon Valley Archives at Stanford.

items.title: Robert H. Norman microcomputing materials
items.description: 1. Photo of first MOS/LSI chip -- 2. Mock-up of 2000 Gae computer fabricated using Micrologic in TO-18 cans (which were not used) -- 3a. Color print of an actual Victor EC-3900 Logic Board with 28 LSI-ICs of 23 types. Picture of calculator is in background -- 3b.

items.title: Robert Lipp oral history : interview by Rob Walker, 1991
items.description: CEO and founder of California Devices Inc. (CDI).

items.title: Robert N. Noyce; an interview conducted by Michael F. Wolff : transcript, 1975 September 19.
The 30th anniversary of the integrated circuit; thirty who made a difference : a history of the integrated circuit, 1988
The Fairchild Chronicles : DVD, 2005
items.description: The is the story of the pioneering semiconductor company from it's founding in 1957 to it's sale to National Semiconductor in 1986. The story is told in the words of those who were there.

items.title: Victor Grinich papers and photographs, 1942-1985
items.description: Box 1. Folder 1 - biographical material. Folder 2 - diplomas, patent, 1945-1962 Folder 3 - "Waveform distortion in phase-rotation (sideband-cancellation) in single-sideband systems," 1951. Folder 4 - Newsclippings, 1942-1967. Folder 5 - Photographs, undated.

items.title: William Bradford Shockley papers, 1860-2002 (inclusive), 1940-1988 (bulk)
items.description: Professor of engineering at Stanford (1958-1975; emeritus 1975-1989). Shockley was co-recipient of the Nobel Prize in physics, 1956. Professional and personal papers relating to Professor Shockley's controversial interests in environment and genetic influences on intelligence; research on transistors and electronics.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Silicon Valley technology industry as a whole

items.title: Austin Randall collection of photographic negatives, circa 1955-2000
items.description: Black and white negatives related to Silicon Valley corporate culture. Images depict primarily electronic equipment, though people and buildings (including a number by developer Joseph Eichler) are also represented in the collection.

items.title: Bernard M. Oliver oral history interview
items.description: Oliver earned his a.b. in engineering at Stanford University in 1935, studying with Frederick Terman. After graduate work at the California Institute of Technology, he joined Bell Laboratories. In 1950 He joined the Hewlett-Packard company as director of research.

items.title: Frederick E. Terman biographical collection, 1948-1997
items.description: Frederick Emmons Terman (1900-1982) was an American electrical engineer known for his contributions to electronics research and anti-radar technology. He was the former dean of engineering and later the provost of Stanford University.

items.title: Hewlett-Packard ephemera collection, 1957-1994
items.description: Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard were friends and fellow graduates of Stanford University. Following their graduation from Stanford, the two founded the electronics firm Hewlett-Packard Co. in 1938.

items.title: HP Memory Project Collection
items.description: HP Memory Project Collection.

items.title: Silicon Valley genealogy : posters, 1984 and 1995
items.description: Two schematic diagrams showing connections among the major electronics industries and their founders in Silicon Valley from 1946 to 1996.

items.title: Stanford University, Development Office, Hewlett Packard project video recordings, 1995
items.description: Source tapes used in the production of FOUNDERS OF THE FUTURE, a video project honoring William Hewlett and David Packard and their contributions to Stanford University, and several copies of the final edited version.

items.title: Vernon Russell Anderson papers, 1953-2000
items.description: Papers include class notes, files, and records relating to the Vidar Corporation and Silicon Graphics. In addition to the bound memoir covering Anderson's life, there is a 14-page review written by Anderson about his engineering career.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Software

items.title: Ned Chapin papers, 1960-2008
items.description: Dr. Ned Chapin passed away on December 27, 2014. He was born on the Olympic Peninsula and grew up living in various locations in Washington, Oregon, and California. After graduating from Eureka Senior High School in 1945, he attended Stanford University where he played percussion in the Symphony Orchestra.

items.title: Robert W. Floyd papers, 1960-1995
items.description: Robert W. Floyd joined the Stanford faculty in 1968 as an associate professor of computer science. He was appointed full professor in 1970 and from 1973 to 1975 he was chair of the department. He retired from Stanford in 1994. These papers include his Stanford course files, 1976-94.

items.title: SPIRES retrospectives by the original developers
items.description: SPIRES [Stanford Physics Information Retrieval System] was first developed to provide access to preprints of physics research; it then grew to be a broader based data management and retrieval tool, with the acronym meaning Stanford Public Information Retrieval System.

items.title: Ted Nelson papers, 1950s-2019
items.description: Theodor Holm "Ted" Nelson is an information technology pioneer and systems humanist. Born in 1937, in Chicago, Nelson is the son of Academy Award-winning actor Celeste Holm. Nelson received his Bachelor's degree in Philosophy from Swarthmore University in 1959 and a Masters' degree in Sociology from Harvard in 1962.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: Southern Pacific Company public relations collection, 1900, 1959-1972
items.description: Typescripts generated by the Southern Pacific public relations office concerning historical material, the Southern Pacific Pipe Lines, Inc., and the Southern Pacific Transportation Company. Also included is a bibliography, a photocopy of a speech by C.P. Huntington, May 1900, and two publications.

items.title: Southern Pacific Company: drawings and maps
items.description: The collection includes 78 maps produced by Southern Pacific Railroad of lines, sidings, stations, and rail yards in California, primarily in the San Francisco Bay Area but also including the Santa Barbara region.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records, 1862-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. It was the first railroad to connect Los Angeles to the rest of California and its lines extended as far as New Orleans.

Water from the SVWC dam was diverted to the San Francisco water system. The dam was removed in 2006 as part of the Alameda Creek Restoration Project.

items.description: The Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection are materials owned and selected for digitization by the Santa Clara Valley Water District. The materials are related to water resources management in Santa Clara County, California dating in the early 1900s.

items.description: Albert Wilson (1903–1996), was an American botanist, landscape architect, author, teacher and lecturer on gardening and landscaping, and a TV and radio talk show personality who wrote several books popularizing gardening, as well as an autobiography. Albert Wilson was born in San Francisco and placed in an orphanage.

items.title: California Flower Market records, 1890-2014
items.description: The flower industry in San Francisco and the extended Bay Area dates back to the late 1800s when flower sellers would gather at an outdoor flower market at the corner of Kearney Street and Market Street in San Francisco.

items.title: Toichi Domoto papers, ca. 1860-1996
items.description: Toichi Domoto was the son of first generation immigrants from Japan who settled in California. Arriving in 1883, his father and uncle worked first as laborers and within a year were able to lease and then purchase a few acres of land in Oakland, founding the Domoto Brothers Nursery in 1884.

items.title: Albert V. Baez papers, 1949-1995
items.description: Albert Vinicio Baez, Ph.D. (1912-2007) was a prominent Mexican-American physicist, and the father of singers Joan Baez and Mimi Fariña. Dr. Baez earned his bachelor's degree in mathematics from Drew University in 1933 and his master's degree in physics from Syracuse University in 1935.

items.title: Anthony Edward Siegman papers, 1916-2013 (inclusive)
items.description: Anthony Siegman was an electrical engineer, primarily focused on masers and lasers. Siegman earned an AB from Harvard in 1952, the MS in Applied Physics from the University of California at Los Angeles in 1954, and a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from Stanford University in 1957.

items.title: Bloch symposium; a Stanford centennial symposium celebrating the work of Felix Bloch [videorecording]
items.description: Physicist. Excelling in both theoretical and experimental physics, Bloch won the Nobel Prize in 1952 for his work in nuclear magnetism. Bloch was a member of the Physics Department at Stanford University from 1934 until his death in 1983. Tapes from a symposium held on October 27 and 28, 1989, at Stanford University.

items.title: C. F. Quate papers, circa 1961-1984
items.description: Calvin F. Quate earned his degrees in electrical engineering at the University of Utah (B.S., 1944) and Stanford University (Ph.D., 1950). He joined the Stanford faculty in 1961 as professor in the applied physics and electrical engineering departments, serving two terms as chair of the department of applied physics.

items.title: David Locke Webster papers, 1914-1976
items.description: Born in Boston, November 6, 1888, David Locke Webster attended Harvard University, receiving his bachelor's in 1910 and his doctorate three years later, both in physics. While studying at Harvard, Webster also taught as an instructor in mathematics (1909-12) and as an assistant in physics (1911-14).

items.title: Felix Bloch papers, 1928-1987
items.description: Professional and research papers including correspondence, research notes and notebooks, grant proposals, license agreements, patents, apparatus designs, papers, talks, articles, minutes, teaching materials, lecture notes, scientific reprints, and photographs.

items.title: Fu Chun Yu lab notebooks [facsimiles], 1949-1950
items.description: Fu Chun Yu, born in Shanghai in 1914, graduated from Peking University in 1936. He came to the United States in 1946 and received his PhD from Ohio State University in 1949; he then came to Stanford to work with physicist Felix Bloch. Yu returned to China in 1951, where he continued his career as professor of physics.

items.title: High Frequency Direct Writing Oscillograph Project Lantern Slides, circa 1960s
items.description: Richard G. Sweet developed an ink-jet recorder at Stanford University in the early 1960s. Funded by an Army Signal Corps contract, Sweet developed a technique for selective charging and deflection of individual ink droplets, resulting in higher recording speeds for ink-jet printers.

items.description: Schawlow family background, Depression years in Toronto; early aptitudes in radio engineering; college and university studies in math and physics, and World War II interruption; Malcolm Crawford and thesis research on atomic beam light source; post-doc at Columbia University, 1949-1951.

items.description: Professor of physics at Stanford University since 1931 (emeritus, 1960 - ); best known for his pioneering work in x-ray technology. General reminiscences about his life, including recollections about his work and colleagues at Stanford. Also includes a bibliography.

Maslow, "Emotional Blocks to Creativity, " presented to U.S. Army engineers at Fort Belvoir, VA, 1958; a chart on creative process.
