items.title: Wilhelm Flügge papers, 1937-1980
items.description: Wilhelm Flügge, internationally known specialist in engineering mechanics, is best known for his research on shell structures. He came to Stanford University in 1948 as an associate professor of mechanical engineering. Prior to World War II, he taught at Gottingen University in Germany, specializing in aerodynamics.

sectors.name: Education and research — Library, archival and information services

items.title: ARS Audiotape Collection
items.description: Miscellaneous tape recordings, mostly small donations, that span the history of the Archive of Recorded Sound. The ARS Audio Miscellany Collection consists of audio recordings on tape, largely from small donations and with limited documentation and context.

sectors.name: Education and research — Musical acoustics and computer music

items.title: John R. Pierce papers, 1933-2002 (inclusive), 1960-2002 (bulk)
items.description: John R. Pierce earned all three of his degrees at the California Institute of Technology: B.S. in 1933, M.S. in 1934, and Ph.D. in 1936. He worked at Bell Telephone Laboratories from 1936 to 1971, where his work included electronic tubes, microwave communications, and psychoacoustics.

items.title: Musical Acoustics Research Library collection, 1956-2007
items.description: Contains research materials, research papers, correspondence, journal run , photographs, glass slides, wood samples, and other artifacts (woodwind and brass mouthpieces). The MARL collection is dedicated to the study of all aspects of musical acoustics.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: College of Notre Dame (later: Notre Dame de Namur University), 1890-1976
items.description: Located in San Jose, then Belmont, California. Founded in 1851 as the Academy of Notre Dame. Chartered in 1868 as the College of Notre Dame. Moved to Belmont in 1923. In 2001 name changed to Notre Dame de Namur University.

items.title: College of San Mateo (formerly: San Mateo Junior College)
items.description: Located in San Mateo, California. Founded in 1922 as the San Mateo Junior College. In 1954 became College of San Mateo. For additional catalogs see Boxes 431-432.

items.title: College of San Mateo (formerly: San Mateo Junior College)
items.description: Located in San Mateo, California. Founded in 1922 as the San Mateo Junior College. In 1954 became College of San Mateo. For additional catalogs see Box 1609.

items.title: De Anza College, 1967-1979
items.description: Located in Cupertino, California. Opened in 1967.

items.title: Foothill College
items.description: Located in Los Altos Hills, California. Founded in 1957.

items.title: Gavilan College (formerly: San Benito County Junior College)
items.description: Located in Gilroy, California. Established in 1919 as San Benito County Junior College in Hollister, California. Became Gavilan College in 1963.

items.title: Menlo College and School of Business Administration, 1928-1977
items.description: Located in Menlo Park, California. Menlo School was founded in 1915, Menlo Junior College in 1927, and the School of Business Administration in 1949.

items.title: San Jose Bible College (later: William Jessup University), 1956-1971
items.description: Located in San Jose, California. Founded in 1939 as San Jose Bible College. Became San Jose Christian College in 1989 and moved in 2003 to Rocklin, California becoming William Jessup University in 2004.

items.title: San Jose City College, 1955-1978
items.description: Located in San Jose, California. Founded in 1921 as San Jose Junior College. Became San Jose City College in 1958.

items.title: San Jose State University (formerly: California State University, San Jose; formerly: San Jose State College; formerly: California State Teachers College at San Jose; formerly: California State Normal School), 1875-1982
items.description: Originally located in San Francisco, but moved to San Jose in 1871. Established in 1857 as the Minns' Evening Normal School. Became California State Normal School in 1862 and the California State Teachers College at San Jose in 1921.

items.title: St. Patrick's Seminary (later: St. Patrick's Seminary and University)
items.description: Located in Menlo Park, California. Founded in 1898.

items.title: To Mr. George Murray in remembrance of the 1969-1970 school year at Nairobi High
items.description: A one-off yearbook of sorts, made from the plain thick card covers of a spiralbound notebook with the pages removed, photos and text mounted on the inside of the boards.

items.title: University of Santa Clara (formerly: Santa Clara College; later Santa Clara University)
items.description: Located in Santa Clara, California. Founded in 1851 as Santa Clara College. Became University of Santa Clara in 1912 and Santa Clara University in 1985.

items.title: University of the Pacific (formerly: College of the Pacific, formerly: University of the Pacific), 1873-1978
items.description: First located in Santa Clara, California. Chartered in 1851 as California Wesleyan College, soon changed to University of the Pacific. In 1911 became College of the Pacific. Moved to San Jose in 1871 and from San Jose to Stockton, California in 1924. In 1961 became University of the Pacific.

items.title: West Valley College
items.description: Founded in 1963 in Campbell, California. Later moved to Saratoga, California.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: A partial list of seed plants of the North Coast Ranges of California, 1929-1972
items.description: The lists name some 2,717 species collected between Sonoma and the Oregon border. In his introduction to the 1951 list he writes, "This list has been undertaken in the sheer pleasure of finding out what seed plants grow in this vast and varied region...

items.title: Armin Dale Kaiser papers, circa 1956-1982
items.description: Armin Dale Kaiser (1927-2020) was a professor of Biochemistry at Stanford University, 1959-1982. He was among the first to investigate the quantitative genetics of bacterial viruses. Correspondence, 1966-1972; research notebooks, 1956-ca. 1980; and faculty notebooks, 1979-1982.

items.title: Arthur Kornberg papers, 1938-2007
items.description: With a research career spanning more than sixty years, Arthur Kornberg made many outstanding contributions to molecular biology. He was the first to isolate DNA polymerase, the enzyme that assembles DNA from its components, and the first to synthesize DNA in a test tube, which earned him a Nobel Prize in 1959.

items.title: Bailey Willis papers, circa 1900-1962
items.description: After early studies in Germany, Bailey Willis attended Columbia University and was awarded the degree of Mining Engineer in 1878 and of Civil Engineer in 1879. In 1884 he began his career with the United States Geological Survey, working chiefly in the Pacific Northwest.

items.title: Benjamin M. Page papers, 1929-1996
items.description: Geologist. Page, a member of the Stanford class of 1933, also earned his master's degree in 1934 and his Ph.D in 1940 at Stanford. He joined the Stanford faculty in 1943, becoming full professor in 1952; he was head of the Geology Department from 1957-62 and again from 1965-68. He retired in 1976.

items.title: C.B. Niel papers, 1923-1977
items.description: In 1929, Dr. C. B. van Niel (1897-1985) started his career as an associate professor at the Jacques Loeb Laboratory, Hopkins Marine Station, Stanford University. He was appointed Herzstein Professor of Microbiology in 1946.

items.title: Carl Djerassi papers, 1952-2006 (inclusive)
items.description: University research scientist and industrialist, Djerassi is most famous for synthesizing the first oral contraceptive. Born in Vienna, Austria, in 1923, he emigrated to the United States in 1939.

items.title: Cecil H. Green oral history interview transcript, 1995
items.description: Green was a British-born American geophysicist who trained at the University of British Columbia and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He was a founder of Texas Instruments.

items.title: Charles Stacy French papers, 1935-1989
items.description: French, plant physiologist, was director of the Dept. of Plant Biology of the Carnegie Institution, located on the Stanford University campus, from 1947 until his retirement in 1973. Prior to his arrival at Carnegie, he taught at the Harvard Medical School, the University of Chicago, and the University of Minnesota.

items.title: Chemist and administrator at UC Berkeley, Rice University, Stanford University, and the Atomic Energy Commission, 1935-1997 : oral history transcript, 1999
items.description: Interviews of Pitzer by Sally Smith Hughes and Germaine LaBerge conducted in 1996, 1997, and 1998. With introductions by Robert Curl and Marilyn Chapin Massey. Sponsored by the Regional Oral History Office of the Bancroft Library, University of California, Berkeley.

items.title: Classical electricity and magnetism, 1949
items.description: Edited by Roger Wallace and Howard Chang. Lectures, as covered in 33 chapters.

items.title: Donald Leland Carpenter memoirs
items.description: Emeritus professor of Engineering, Carpenter earned his PhD at Stanford in 1962. In 1974, he joined the faculty. Carpenter's research focused on very low frequency radio propagation and solar terrestrial physics. He is a former member of the Executive Committee of Commission IV of the USA National Committee of URSI.

items.title: Donald Leland Carpenter papers, 1959-1993
items.description: Donald Leland Carpenter was a Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus at Stanford University. He was on faculty for more than four decades. His research primarly focused on Very Low Frequency Radio Propogation and Solar Terrestrial Physics. He passed away in February 2019.

items.title: Douglas Merritt Whitaker papers, 1926-1963
items.description: Professor of Biology at Stanford (1931-1955); Dean of the School of Biological Sciences (1946-1949); Dean of Graduate Studies (1948-1951); Dean of Humanities and Sciences (1951-1952). Acting Vice-President of the University (1948-1949); and Provost (1952-1955).

items.title: Ecological study of San Francisquito Creek : typescript, 1968 Sept
items.description: Part of "Resources and Ecology Projects" sponsored by the City of Menlo Park, California. The report refers to slides which are not included.

items.title: Esther M. Lederberg papers, 1906-1998 (inclusive), 1937-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Esther Miriam Zimmer Lederberg, PhD, professor emeritus of microbiology and immunology at the Stanford University School of Medicine, earned her AB at Hunter College in 1942. She then came to Stanford to study genetics, earning her MA in 1946. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin, Madison in 1950.

items.title: Gabor Szego papers
items.description: Mathematician. Professor of Mathematics at Stanford University and chairman of the department from 1938 to 1958. He retired in 1960 as an emeriti professor. Professional and personal correspondence, ephemera, manuscripts, photographs, technical reports and publications, ca. 1910 to 1980. 1910 to 1980.

items.title: Geology of area east of Page Mill Road
items.description: Submitted to the Department of Geology. Student Report--Stanford University, 1942.

items.title: Geology of the Alum Rock Canyon sector, Diablo Range, California
items.description: Student Report--Stanford University, 194-. Submitted to the Department of Geology.

items.title: Geology southeast of Page Mill Road, Palo Alto quadrangle
items.description: Student Report--Stanford University, 194-. Submitted to the Department of Geology.

items.title: George Polya papers, 1884-1985
items.description: Hungarian mathematician George Pólya was educated at the University of Budapest and the University of Paris, and taught at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich from 1914 to 1940. His students included future Stanford physics professors Felix Bloch and Hans Staub.

items.title: Harry S. Mosher papers, 1944-2000
items.description: Harry S. Mosher earned his bachelor's degree in 1937 from Willamette University and his master's degree from Oregon State University in 1939. He taught briefly at Willamette before earning his doctorate in organic chemistry from Pennsylvania State University in 1942.

items.title: Ingram Olkin papers, 1875-2014, bulk 1950-2014
items.description: Ingram Olkin is best known for developing statistical analyses for evaluating policies, particularly in education. Throughout his career, Olkin conducted highly significant research concerning new and innovative statistical models and methods for the behavioral medical, and social sciences, often simultaneously.

items.title: Interview with Arthur Kornberg [videorecording]
items.description: Biochemistry professor at Stanford University (Chairman of the Department of Biochemistry from 1959 to 1969), Kornberg received a Nobel Prize in medicine and physiology in 1959 for pioneering the synthesis of DNA in the laboratory.

items.title: James Murray Luck papers, 1930-1979
items.description: Professor of biochemistry at Stanford (1926-1965; emeritus, 1965- ). Primarily correspondence and subject files relating to Professor Luck's professional activities, the Stanford Chemistry Department and his position as acting Science Attaché at the United States embassies in London, Stockholm and Bern.

items.title: Jens Clausen field notebooks, 1928-1962
items.description: Primarily herbarium specimen collection notes, arranged by number and date. Box 1, 1928-1946; box 2, 1951-1957; box 3, 1957-1962, and other notes including a list of his collections by number, and a notebook, "Edible native and naturalized plants of California," nd.

items.title: John C. Lilly papers, 1933-2012
items.description: John Cunningham Lilly (1915-2001) was a physiologist, biologist, and medical doctor known for his work with dolphins and interspecies communication, as well as research on the brain and consciousness which resulted in his invention of the isolation tank. Lilly was born the son of a banker in St. Paul, Minnesota.

items.title: John George Herriot papers, 1937-1992
items.description: John G. Herriot (1916-2003) earned a BS in mathematics and physics at the University of Manitoba in 1937 and a PhD in mathematics at Brown University in 1941. He first taught at Stanford from 1942-1944, leaving to do research in the Ames Aeronautical Laboratory at Moffett Field.

items.title: John Warvelle Harbaugh, "Memoirs"
items.description: John Warvelle Harbaugh (1926-2019) was an American geologist and Professor Emeritus in the Geological and Environmental Sciences Department and at the Energy Resources Engineering Department at Stanford University.

items.title: Martin Gardner papers, 1957-1986
items.description: Martin Gardner was the Mathematical Games columnist for SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN from its inception in 1956 until 1986. He earned his B.A. in philosophy at the University of Chicago in 1936; after his service in the Navy during World War II, he became a writer.

items.title: Paul R. Ehrlich papers, 1954-2001
items.description: Paul R. Ehrlich (1932-2026) was the Bing Professor of Population Studies, Emeritus. Ehrlich was an evolutionary and population biologist who gained worldwide attention for his 1968 book, The Population Bomb , which predicted dire consequences due to the rapidly increasing human population and advocated population…

items.title: Peter A. Sturrock papers, 1952-2020
items.description: Peter Andrew Sturrock is an emeritus professor of applied physics at Stanford University. Sturrock taught applied physics at Stanford from 1961-1998. In 1990 Sturrock was awarded the Arctowski Medal from the National Academy of Sciences.

items.title: Photographs from unmanned NASA space exploration, circa 1967-1976
items.description: The five images come from these NASA explorations: 1. Viking lander, 1-3 August 1976, the surface of Mars.

items.title: Pierre Van Rysselberghe papers, 1932-1973
items.description: Pierre van Rysselberghe, a chemist and chemical engineer, earned his masters (1928) and doctorate (1929) at Stanford University. He taught at the University of Oregon and at Stanford. He died in 1977.

items.title: Richard H. Jahns papers, circa 1916-1983
items.description: Professor of Geology and Applied Sciences and Dean of the School of Earth Sciences at Stanford University, 1965-1983. Jahns came to Stanford following teaching positions at Cal Tech and Penn State, where he also served as Dean of the College of Mineral Industries. Correspondence, memoranda, reports, and articles.

items.title: Robert Arthur Helliwell papers, 1950-1999
items.description: Helliwell graduated from Stanford with his bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees. In 1946, he joined the faculty in Stanford's Department of Electrical Engineering. Helliwell's research on whistlers led to many prominent journal articles and technical reports on the subject. He passed away in 2011.

items.title: Robert Hofstadter papers, 1931-1993
items.description: Robert (Rubvin) Hofstadter was born in New York City, on February 5, 1915. He was one of four children of Polish immigrants, Louis and Henrietta (Koenigsberg) Hofstadter. Hofstadter was educated in New York City and attended the City College of New York (CCNY) receiving his B.S. degree magna cum laude.

items.title: Ronald Bracewell papers, 1958-2007
items.description: Ronald Newbold Bracewell (July 22, 1921 – August 12, 2007) was the Lewis M. Terman Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus of the Space, Telecommunications and Radioscience Laboratory at Stanford University. He was born in Sydney, Australia, in 1921, and educated at Sydney Boys High School.

items.title: Science, biotechnology, and recombinant DNA: a personal history
items.description: Interview conducted in 1995.

items.title: Species Lupinorum and related correspondence, 1922-1953
items.description: "A series of papers reviewing the genus Lupinus... issued in dated signatures...".

items.title: Stanford booklets
items.description: Booklet contains text on the proposed linear accelerator project at Stanford, text on the academic program at Stanford, and photographs. Images include the Mark III linear electron accelerator, the engineering corner of the Quad, site plan of the proposed two-mile accelerator, Edward Ginzton, Robert Hofstadter…

items.title: Stanford-Cambridge Radar Film Digitization Project
items.description: The Stanford-Cambridge Radar Film Digitization Project is an Antarctic survey conducted by an international consortium of American, British and Danish geoscientists.

items.title: Stanford: I. Its two-mile-long atom smasher II. A university on the march; June 1959
items.description: Booklet contains text on the proposed linear accelerator project at Stanford, text on the academic program at Stanford, and photographs. Images include the Mark III linear electron accelerator, the engineering corner of the Quad, site plan of the proposed two-mile accelerator, Edward Ginzton, Robert Hofstadter…

items.title: Stephen Jay Gould papers, 1899-2004 (inclusive), 1941-2002 (bulk)
items.description: Stephen Jay Gould, notable American paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, and historian of science was born on September 10, 1941, in New York City, the son of Leonard and Eleanor (Rosenberg) Gould. His father Leonard was a court stenographer, and his mother Eleanor was an artist.

items.title: Telford H. Work notebook
items.description: Telford H. Work earned his A.B. in biological sciences at Stanford University in 1942 and his M.D. in 1946. Notes on a trip to collect eggs from eagle nests near the Calaveras reservoir, April 1942.

items.title: Willard J. Classen miscellaneous papers, 1955-1991
items.description: This collection contains a reprint of an article by Classen and Joseph J. Graham, "A Lower Eocene Foraminiferal Faunule from the Woodside Area, San Mateo County, California," 1955, with the original illustrations.

items.title: Willard J. Classen papers
items.description: Willard J. Classen was born October 3, 1899, in San Francisco of gold rush descendants, and after the 1906 earthquake, his family relocated on the Peninsula to "Fair Oaks," now known as Atherton. Willard attended Manzanita Hall, a private Palo Alto high school, and entered Stanford University in the fall of 1917.

items.title: William M. Fairbank papers, 1961-1989
items.description: William M. Fairbank (1917-1989) was a physics professor at Stanford University. Fairbank earned his Ph.D. from Yale in 1948 and taught at Amherst College and Duke University before joining the Stanford faculty in 1959. His research interests included superconductivity, gravity waves, individual quarks and monopoles.

items.title: William S. Johnson papers, 1940-1992
items.description: Johnson, professor of chemistry at Stanford University, was generally regarded as one of the major figures in 20th-century organic chemistry. He served as head of Stanford's chemistry department from 1960 to 1969, and after resigning that post, was appointed the Jackson-Wood Professor of Chemistry which he held until…

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Albert Léon Guérard papers addenda, 1908-1960
items.description: Frenchman Albert Léon Guérard (1880-1959) spent most of his life as an American academic, and his work reflects an engagement with both France and the United States. Guérard came to the United States from France in 1906 to teach at Williams College.

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Doris Helen Linder (1925-2008) was born in Columbia, South Dakota to Swedish immigrants Hilda and Arvid Justus Linder. Linder studied history at Stanford University, where she received a BA in 1946 and an MA in 1949. She received a Ph.D. in History from the University of Minnesota in 1961.

items.title: Eugene J. Webb papers, 1961-1994
items.description: Eugene J. Webb, a pioneer in the development of research and teaching of organizational behavior in business schools, joined the faculty of the Graduate School of Business at Stanford in 1968. He earned his A.B. at SUNY Albany in 1954 and his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago in 1956.

items.title: Lewis Madison Terman papers, 1910-1992
items.description: Lewis Madison Terman was born in Johnson County, Indiana, on January 15, 1877. He received his A.B. and A. M. from Indiana University and his Ph.D. from Clark University. He came to Stanford in 1910 to teach in the Department of Education; Correspondence and data for Terman's study of the gifted.

items.title: Lois Meek Stolz psychology case interviews, 1957-1958
items.description: Born in Washington, D.C. in 1891, Lois Meek Stolz attended public schools, graduating from Washington Normal Schools in 1912. She taught school in the primary grades and attended George Washington University, graduating with an A.B. cum laude in 1921.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: "Becoming Stanford: The Making of an American University" [videorecording]
items.description: Part 1, "The Founding," covers the origins and building of the university through World War I; highlights include Stanford family history, the first Big Game between Stanford and UC Berkeley, early student life, the rise of tenure, and the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Charles Anderson Gauld papers
items.description: Gauld, who earned his A.B. in history at Stanford in 1932, was a lecturer at Stanford and assistant editor of HISPANIC AMERICAN REPORT. These papers pertain largely to Stanford anecdotes and history and include his typescript articles on George E. Crothers and Jane Stanford.

items.title: Charles Babbage Institute Oral History collection, 1979-1991
items.description: Founded in 1978, the Charles Babbage Institute is the University of Minnesota's research center for advancing the understanding of computing, information, and culture.

items.title: Franklin Chiang Photographs, circa 1966-1972
items.description: Franklin Chiang (1925-2016) was the son of Chinese military general Sun-Pu Chiang in Chengdu, Sichuan, China. During World War II, Chiang flew for the China National Aviation Corporation and was based out of Kunming, 1942-1945. From 1945-1948, Chiang attended Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

items.title: Halsey L. Royden, "The History of the Stanford Mathematics Department"
items.description: Halsey L. Royden earned his B.S. in 1948 and his M.S. in 1949 at Stanford University and his Ph.D. at Harvard in 1951, after which he returned to Stanford to join the faculty in the department of mathematics.

items.title: Jack Fields photograph collection, 1960
items.description: Professional photographer. Photographs taken on commission in September 1960 regarding Stanford University, used to illustrate a feature article in SATURDAY EVENING POST, 13 December 1960.

items.title: Patrick Suppes : an interview conducted by David W. Mitchell : transcript, 2007
items.description: Oral history interview conducted in May 2007. Topics include his activities with Dr. Fred Terman; Stanford’s development into a major research university; his interests in logic, computers, learning theory and brain function; and the teaching of math.

items.title: Peninsula-Times Tribune  photographs of Stanford University
items.description: The Peninsula-Times Tribune was organized in April 1979 from a merger of the Palo Alto Times and the Redwood City Tribune, both owned by the parent company Peninsula Newspapers Incorported. The paper ceased publishing in 1993.

items.title: Rixford Kinney Snyder, "Memories of a Santa Clara Valley Boy Who Never Left, 1908-1991" typescript
items.description: Rixford Kinney Snyder, Professor of History, Dean of Admissions, and first Director of the Alumni Association's Travel/Study Program. Snyder was born and raised in the Willow Glen area of San Jose and attended local schools. Original and revised version of Rixford's autobiography.

items.title: SRI: the founding years : videorecording, 1983
items.description: Weldon B. Gibson, who earned his MBA in 1940 and his PhD in 1950 from Stanford University, was one of the first fellows at the Stanford Research Institute and its Senior Director in the 1980's. He also taught at Stanford's Graduate School of Business and served on the Athletic Board.

items.title: Stanford Historical Photograph collection, 1887-circa 1996
items.description: Series 1, General Photographs, documents the campus and campus life; subjects include athletics, original construction of the campus, individual buildings, students and student life activities, commencement activities, academic departments, and damage from the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society oral history program interviews
items.description: The Stanford Historical Society's Oral History Program explores the institutional history of the University, with an emphasis on the transformative post-WWII period, through interviews with leading faculty, staff, alumni, trustees, and others.

items.title: Stanford News Service records 1931-2023
items.description: Records include subject files compiled by the News Service in the course of its work, news releases prepared by the News Service, proof sheets of photographs produced by the News Service photographers, taped interviews, office files of the Director of News and Publications Service and of the directors of the…

items.title: Stanford Speech Collection
items.description: The Stanford Speech Collection consists of audio recordings on open reel tape of speeches, lectures, interviews and panel discussions at or sponsored by Stanford University from the 1950s through the early 70s.

items.title: Stanford Tape Collection
items.description: Historic music and speech recordings on open reel tape, made on the campus of Stanford University. aqa The Stanford Tape Collection consists of historic music and speech recordings made on the campus of Stanford University. Many were used in the production of broadcasts by university radio station KZSU.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University. The files were maintained by University Archives staff from around the time of the Archives' establishment in 1965 through mid-2011 Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford…

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Records, 1950-2008
items.description: This collection consists of 50th anniversary celebration materials from 2008 and research figures and diagrams from 1950. While the current Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics was structured in 1958, it's previously entitled the Department of Aeronautical Engineering, a department that was formed in 1927 with…

items.title: Stanford: a sentimental journey : video recordings, 1987
items.description: This film in celebration of Stanford University's centennial includes interviews with faculty and alumni; scenes of academic and student activities; views of the campus; and still photographs transferred to video, primarily concerning the history of Stanford.

items.title: The living legends: a discussion about the establishment of the Computer Science Department at Stanford University : videorecording, 1997
items.description: A discussion amongst John McCarthy, Edward Feigenbaum, Robert W. Floyd, Donald Knuth, Gene Golub, Gio Wiederhold, John G. Herriot, and William F. Miller on the history of computer science at Stanford, recorded on March 22, 1997 by Andy Kacsman.

items.title: Williamson M. Evers papers
items.description: Williamson M. Evers is an American libertarian and member of the Libertarian Party National Committee. He was a former research fellow at the Hoover Institution where he specialized in research on education policy.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: Herbert Hoover Stanford fund-raising letters
items.description: These two letters, addressed to Mrs. Lynn Smith Abbott (who attended Stanford from 1893-94), pertain to the Stanford Futures campaign to raise money for scholarships.

items.title: Herbert Hoover typed letter signed to Harry Chandler, 1942 Aug. 27
items.description: Hoover, president of Stanford University at this time, sends his thanks for Chandler's service on the Board of Trustees, and expresses the sentiment that Mrs. Roger Gordan (May), his replacement, was elected not only for her "splendid qualities, but out of ... respect to you...".

items.title: Hugh Hildreth Skilling papers, 1954-1964
items.description: Hugh H. Skilling was professor of electrical engineering at Stanford (1928-1929, 1931-1971; emeritus 1971-1990) and served as head of the Department of Electrical Engineering from 1944 to 1967.

items.title: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson papers, 1941-1990
items.description: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Stanford in 1940 and returned after his wartime service in the Navy to earn his MBA in 1947. After seven years in the business world, he returned to Stanford in 1954 as assistant to university president J. E. Wallace Sterling.

items.title: Kenneth S. Pitzer, President of Stanford University, papers, circa 1968-1970 (inclusive)
items.description: Sixth president of Stanford University, December 1968 to September 1, 1970. The materials consist of inauguration materials, administrative records, records concerning gifts, subject files, speeches, and organizational records, including those of Stanford Research Institute and the American Associations of…

items.title: Richard W. Lyman, Provost of Stanford University, papers, 1959-1972
items.description: Lyman was born in Philadelphia in 1923 and raised in New Haven, Conn. His father, a chemist who lost his job during the recession that followed World War I, became an attorney. His mother taught French. His exposure to the world began with a summer visit to Belgium to visit his maternal grandmother.

items.title: Robert Averill Walker papers, 1950-1995
items.description: Robert A. Walker was professor of political science at Stanford University from 1949 until his retirement in 1976. He was a co-founder of the overseas studies program at Stanford, and active on university committees dealing with land use planning and faculty/staff housing.

items.title: Sennet W. Gilfillan correspondence with Stanford University
items.description: Correspondence with Frederick E. Terman and David S. Jacobson regarding Gilfillan's contributions to scholarships for electrical engineering students and the Gilfillan Wing of the Electronics Laboratory; some of Terman's letters concern faculty and research projects of the department.

items.title: Stanford Computation Center photographs, circa 1968-1972
items.description: 42 photographs of the Stanford Computation Center created by Elizabeth Westlake.

items.title: Stanford Construction Institute correspondence
items.description: The Stanford Construction Institute was a graduate level construction engineering and management program. Includes correspondence with Prof. Clark Oglesby, Engineering Dean Lauress L. Wise, and Pres.

items.title: Stanford University, ACME Project, records, 1961-1973
items.description: Joshua Lederberg (1925-2008) was a molecular biologist and professor of genetics at Stanford Medical School (1959-1978). Lederberg received a Nobel prize in 1958 and became president of Rockefeller University in 1978. Professor of Genetics at Stanford Medical School (1959-1978).

items.title: Stanford University, Assistant to the President for Black Affairs, records
items.description: In 1968, Stanford University created the new office of Assistant Provost for Minority Affairs, naming James E. Simmons to the post; in 1969, Mr. Simmon's title was changed to Assistant to the President for Black Affairs.

items.title: Stanford University, Associate Provost for Computing, records, 1968-1971
items.description: William F. Miller (1925-1917), who earned three degrees in physics from Purdue University (B.S. 1949, M.S. 1951, Ph.D. 1956), joined Stanford in 1965 as a professor of computer science. He was appointed professor and head of the computation group at the Stanford Linear Acceleration Center in 1965.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: Powers and Duties —The Board of Trustees is custodian of the endowment and all properties of the University. The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University.

items.title: Stanford University, Career Planning and Placement Center, records
items.description: Established in 1952 as the Stanford Placement Service, the office changed its name and concentration to Career Planning and Placement Center in 1965.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Physics, records, 1905-2025 (inclusive), 1960-1994 (bulk)
items.description: Collection includes minutes of faculty meetings (1905-1948), administrative files, budget and financial records, grant files, technical reports, correspondence, and other materials.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Physics, research grants
items.description: Research grant files containing abstracts, proposals, correspondence, and budget memoranda; faculty members represented include William Fairbank, Melvin Schwartz, John Dirk Walecka, Robert Hofstadter, and Felix Bloch. Research grant files containing abstracts, proposals, correspondence, and budget memoranda.

items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. items.title: Stanford University, Food Research Institute, records, 1916-1990
items.description: The Food Research Institute at Stanford was founded in 1921 for the study of worldwide problems of food supply, distribution, and consumption. William O. Jones was its executive secretary from 1955 to 1962 and became the Director in 1964. The Institute was closed in June 1998.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of Vice President for Business and Finance, records, 1949-1985
items.description: Files, 1960-1967, which include correspondence, notes, memos and reports dealing with the Ford Foundation, the Plan of Action for a Challenging Era (PACE), Palo Alto-Stanford Hospital Center and the Stanford Children's Convalescent Hospital.

items.title: Stanford University, President's Office, Sterling - Pitzer transitional records, 1946-1970 (inclusive), 1964-1970 (bulk)
items.description: J. E. Wallace Sterling, Stanford's fifth president, served from 1949 through 1968. Kenneth Pitzer took office on December 1, 1968 and served until September 1970. items.title: Stanford University, Public Affairs Office, records, 1960-1980
items.description: The University Relations Office acted as liaison between the University and the public. items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, Dean's Office records, 1915-1998 (inclusive), 1925-1955 (bulk)
items.description: Civil and mechanical engineering courses were among the first taught at Stanford University, with courses in electrical and mining engineering added in 1893. items.title: Stanford University, Special Services Office, records
items.description: Series I - Office records of the Special Services Office. These six boxes contain mainly office correspondence and informative material pertaining to the draft and draft counseling. Also included are 5 volumes of computer printouts of statistical analyses concerning Stanford students and their draft classifications.

items.title: Stanford University, Sponsored Projects Office, records, 1935-1995
items.description: Records from the Sponsored Projects Office pertain to administrative matters and to individual projects; included are correspondence, memoranda, reports, minutes, patent files, and financial records. Many of the correspondence files are those of Earl Cilley.

items.title: Stanford University, University Services, records, 1936-1957
items.description: The University Services office of Stanford University (1942-1954) was established to carry out a program of service on a contractual basis, focusing on the region, the nation, international studies, and business and industry.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The Business Affairs organization at Stanford provides integrated financial, technological, business and human resource services for the benefit of the university community.

items.title: Stanford-SRI Study Committee records, 1954-1969 (inclusive), 1968-1969 (bulk)
items.description: The Stanford-SRI Study Committee was appointed by the Stanford University president in October 1968 "to explore in detail the relationships between Stanford University and the Stanford Research Institute (SRI)." The committee was composed of five faculty, five students, and two members appointed by the president.

items.title: Study and Evaluation of the Status of University Programs...in Computers, Data-processing and Related Fields, report
items.description: Report of a study undertaken at the request of Dr. Albert H. Bowker, head of the Stanford University Statistics Department, with recommendations for building a program at Stanford University.

items.title: William R. Rambo papers, 1939-1992 (inclusive), 1954-1974 (bulk)
items.description: William R. Rambo was born September 3, 1916. He received his B.A. and Electrical Engineering degrees from Stanford University in 1938 and 1941. He was a research associate at the Harvard Radio Research Lab and a research engineer with Airborne Instruments Lab in New York before coming to Stanford as a research… These…

items.title: Gene Golub papers, 1950-2007
items.description: Gene Golub (1932-2007) was a Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University. Golub earned his bachelors, masters and PhD, all in mathematics, from the University of Illinois.

items.description: George Bernard Dantzig (November 8, 1914 – May 13, 2005) was an American mathematical scientist who made important contributions to operations research, computer science, economics, and statistics.

items.description: Professor Lydik S. Jacobsen (1897-1976) began his teaching career at Stanford in 1924. He headed the Mechanical Engineering Department, 1940-1943, and directed the Earthquake Research Laboratory, 1926-1943 and 1946-1962. He earned an AB in mechanical engineering from Stanford in 1921 and a PhD in physics in 1927.

items.title: Merrill S. Hugo papers, 1901-1960, 1941-1960
items.description: Hugo, a 1924 engineering graduate of Stanford and a Major with the United States Army Ordnance Department, joined the Stanford faculty in 1930 and served as director of the Gage Laboratory, School of Engineering. The materials consist of records the Gage Laboratory and the Stanford School of Engineering.

items.description: An illustrated history of the SRI Physics Division of Stanford Research Institute (now SRI International).

items.title: Stanford Research Institute records, 1947-1966
items.description: The Stanford Research Institute was organized in 1946 as an applied research center for industry and government. In 1970 it became independent from Stanford University and in 1977 changed its name to SRI International.

items.title: Stanford University technical reports, 1956-1970
items.description: Archival copies of technical reports resulting from sponsored research at Stanford.

items.title: Stanford University, Stanford Electronics Laboratories, records, 1948-1990
items.description: Stanford Electronics Laboratories technical reports, electronics research reviews, and research notebooks including three volumes on early traveling wave tube research.

items.description: Video copy of a 1954 film produced by Caryl Coleman about electronics research at Stanford University. Persons appearing in the film include Donald B. Harris, Russell H. Varian, Frederick E. Terman, William R. Hewlett, David Packard, and Marvin Chodorow.

items.title: W. Conyers Herring papers, 1970-2003
items.description: Professor emeritus of applied physics at Stanford University. Herring was a leader in the field of solid-state physics, the study of the arrangement and interaction of atoms in solid materials.

items.title: Ann Rosener papers, circa 1900-2013
items.description: Ann Rosener in her long life was active as a photographer, designer, and private press publisher. She was a native of San Francisco, where her grandparents settled in the mid-19th century; her father was a civil engineer.

When he was 21, Kahn joined Stanford's Department of Art (now the Department of Art and Art History).

Children's Hospital at Stanford records, 1917-1977
items.description: Originally the Stanford Convalescent Home, established on the Stanford campus in 1919 for needy children with long term illness, this privately supported organization changed its name to the Children's Hospital at Stanford in 1970.

items.title: Esther Clark papers, 1947-1973
items.description: Collection includes Clark's work with childhood accident prevention, the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, personal subject files, reprints, and photographs.

items.title: Halsted Holman papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: The papers of Halsted Holman include publications; newspaper and magazine clippings pertaining to Holman's research interests; correspondence; typescript and handwritten manuscripts and outlines for talks; anonymous patient surveys; self-care materials for patients; project reports; email and website print-outs.

items.title: Henry S. Kaplan papers, circa 1960-1983
items.description: Radiologist, cancer research pioneer and educator. Henry S. Kaplan, 1918-1985, began his teaching career at the Stanford University School of Medicine in 1948. He served as professor and chair of the Dept. of Radiology (1948 to 1972) and was named D'Ambrogio Professor of Radiology in 1975.

items.title: Herewith is submitted a record of abstract histories of surgical work
items.description: Typescript.

items.title: Herewith is submitted a record of detailed histories of surgical work
items.description: Typescript.

items.title: Jay Haley papers, 1957-2007
items.description: Jay Haley (1923-2007) was born in an oil town in Wyoming. He was a pioneer in family therapy, and his work traces its birth and development during half a century. He was a founder and first editor of Family Process , the first journal in family therapy.

items.title: Kenneth D. Brock journals, 1949-2018
items.description: Brock was hired in 1984 by the State of California, Department of Health Services, to work as a consultant with the Centers for Disease Control to establish a registry of AIDS cases in California. It was a quasi-legislative appointment by Senator David Roberti's office after he authored the first AIDS bill in 1983.

items.title: Leo Leonidas Stanley papers, 1916-1950
items.description: Chiefly diaries entitled Events of the Day from period of professional work as the Resident Physician of the Medical Department of the California State Prison at San Quentin.

items.title: Mental Research Institute (MRI) records
items.description: The Mental Research Institute (MRI) was founded by Don Jackson in 1959 in Palo Alto, California. Originally a division on the Palo Alto Medical Research Foundation, in 1963 MRI became an independent, multi-disciplinary, non-profit corporation devoted to research and training.

items.title: Palo Alto-Stanford Hospital collection, 1916-1966 (inclusive), 1952-1966 (bulk)
items.description: In 1921 Stanford University took over the administration of Palo Alto's Peninsula Hospital; ownership was jointly shared by Palo Alto and Stanford. In 1931 a new hospital building was opened on university land. In July 1968 Stanford University became the sole owner of the Palo Alto-Stanford Hospital.

items.title: Roy B. Cohn papers, 1963-1982
items.description: Chiefly articles and correspondence related to work with Samuel Kountz in renal transplantation and the prevention and treatment of transplant rejection. Includes: The Immunological reaction in the vascular system of allogenic renal homotransplants: its early detection and treatment / Roy Cohn and Samuel Kountz.

items.title: Russel V. Lee family papers, circa 1895-2014, bulk 1940s-1970s.
items.description: Dr. Russel Van Arsdale Lee founded the Palo Alto Medical Clinic (PAMC), one of the first group practice clinics in the United States. He was a champion of rights for abortion, prepaid medical care and free drugs for addicts, and a leader in health education. His five sons all became doctors.

items.title: Russel V.A. Lee papers, 1935-1976
items.description: Chiefly correspondence together with supporting subject material, including pamphlets, minutes, and newsletters, related to work as Founder and Director of the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, 1924-61. Major subject groupings in health insurance, health care for the aging, community medical clinics and group medical practice.

items.title: S.O.S. Program Collection
items.description: Lecture recordings and transcripts from the S.O.S. Program, a pioneering divorce therapy group founded in Palo Alto, California in 1963 by Sally Spray (now Sally Moltzen).

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Archive of Takeo Shikamura and Hatsu Shikamura
items.description: Collection of Takeo Shikamura’s papers and photo albums, Hatsu (Helen) Yamamoto's and her family’s papers, photos albums, journals.
items.era_note: Shown here on a reading of the collection, rather than on the dates above.

items.title: David Locke Webster, "Reminiscences of a Rolling Stone"
items.description: David Locke Webster, professor of physics (1920-1954; emeritus, 1954-1977) and chairman of the Physics Department at Stanford (1920-1942), was born in Boston November 6, 1888. He received his B.A. (1910) and Ph.D. (1913) from Harvard University.

items.title: Emanuel B. McDonald papers, 1912-1958 (inclusive), 1953-1958 (bulk)
items.description: Emanuel B. "Sam" McDonald joined the Stanford staff in 1903 and became supervisor of athletic grounds. He retired in 1954. Typescript draft of his autobiography SAM MCDONALD'S FARM (Stanford University press, 1954); miscellaneous business papers, pamphlets, and clippings, 1912-1958; photographs.

items.title: Emil Fischer papers, 1865-1984
items.description: Emil Fischer (October 9, 1852 – July 15, 1919) was a German chemist who won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Emil Fischer's son, Hermann Otto Laurenz Fischer (December 16, 1888 - March 9, 1960) left Nazi Germany in the 1930s and in 1948 became a professor of biochemistry at the University of California Berkeley.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza photographs, 1900-1972
items.description: Includes photostatic pictures of Ernesto Galarza's mother, Henrietta Galarza, ca. 1900, sisters Nora and Henrietta and younger brother, ca. 1905, and pictures as an adult in 1959, 1965, and 1972.

items.title: Leland Stanford collection, 1869-1975
items.description: Leland Stanford was born March 9, 1824 in Waltervliet Township, New York. He was admitted to the practice of law in 1848 and married Jane Lathrop in 1850. In 1852 Stanford moved to California where he first worked as a storekeeper in Mother Lode mining camps and later became a successful Sacramento businessman.

items.title: Michael L. Belangie papers, 1945-1980
items.description: Born in Butte Montana, on June 29, 1907, Michael Louis Belangie was the eldest of three children. His father was of French-Canadian origin, and spent his working life as a miner. Personal and professional papers, some also pertaining to his wife, Mary.

items.title: Newcomer family papers, 1850-1972
items.description: A diary or record book of Sidney's life from birth to age 24, kept by his mother, together with other of her papers. Lecture notes that H. Sidney Newcomer kept reflecting pre-World War I mathematics and optics education at the University of Wisconsin. Patents, 1929-1972, awarded to H. Sidney Newcomer.

items.title: Peter Coutts collection, 1881-1956
items.description: Jean-Baptiste Paulin Caperon (better known in California as Peter Coutts), was a successful French businessman, book collector and editor of the republican, anti-royalist paper, LA LIBERTÉ. Political disputes and health problems caused him to leave France and take up residence in California.

items.title: Ray Lyman Wilbur personal papers, 1829-1949 (inclusive) 1875-1949 (bulk)
items.description: Ray Lyman Wilbur graduated from Stanford University (B.S. 1896, M.S. 1897) and from Cooper Medical College (M.D. 1899). He served as lecturer and professor of physiology and of medicine (1897-1903), Dean of the Cooper Medical College (Stanford) (1911-1916), third President of Stanford University (1916-1943)… Includes…

sectors.name: Society and community — Philanthropy and foundations

items.title: Ben and A. Jess Shenson papers, circa 20th century
items.description: Collection consists of material related to the brothers Ben and A. Jess Shenson, their philanthropic activities, connections to local artists, family history and time at Stanford.

items.title: David and Lucile Packard: A lifetime of Stanford philanthropy
items.description: Dave and Lucile Packard's philanthropic activities have had a major impact on Stanford University through grants provided through the the David and Lucile Packard Foundation.

items.title: System Development Foundation records, 1957-1993
items.description: The System Development Foundation (SDF) got its start in the 1950s as a not-for-profit corporation researching and developing computer software in the information sciences. Of most interest to researchers will be the research files and project reports.

items.title: William Hewlett papers, 1907-2018 (bulk 1960-2001)
items.description: William Hewlett was the co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, one of the most successful technology start-up companies in the history of Silicon Valley. He and his business partner and longtime friend David Packard flipped a coin to determine the order of their names when starting their company.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: Black Alumni Stories and Oral Histories
items.description: Records pertaining to the Stanford National Black Alumni Association, including video from events and oral history interviews with alumni. Collection includes two series. Series 1 contains interviews from the 2019 National Black Alumni Summit.

items.title: Japanese-American summer retreats at the Gilroy Yamato Hot Springs Resort : photographs, 1954-1960
items.description: Two 10 x 8 inch black-and-white photographs depicting large groups seated in front of a building at the resort; the site is identified in a Japanese caption on the 1954 photo; the other one includes part of a banner in the background which includes the date.

items.title: Kazuyuki Takahashi papers
items.description: Kazuyuki Takahashi received his B.S. in Biology from Stanford in 1940, and his MD from the same institution in 1949. Takahashi was incarcerated with his wife, Soyo Takahashi, at Santa Anita Assembly Center and Manzanar War Relocation Center during World War II.

items.title: Kenneth Kann papers and oral histories relating to the Petaluma (CA) Jewish chicken ranchers and egg farmers and the life of Joe Rapoport, circa 1970-1995
items.description: Kenneth Kann (1944-) was raised in the East European Jewish immigrant community of Chicago and attended the University of Wisconsin, Madison, during the 1960s. He completed a PhD in modern US history at the University of California, Berkeley in 1977.

items.title: Mary Jane Hamachi papers, 1938-1973
items.description: This collection consists of correspondence, photographs, photo albums,school records, financial documents, certificates, and other documents. The correspondence is from Mary Jane Hamachi's family, friends, and acquaintances during World War II.

items.title: Peter M. Takaichi papers, 1927-1946
items.description: Peter M. Takaichi owned and operated the National Printing Company in San Jose,California. When in 1942 Franklin Delano Roosevelt issued Executive Order No. 9102 authorizing the evacuation of all Japanese Americans from the West Coast, Takaichi and his family were ordered to gather at the Santa Anita Aseembly Center…

items.title: Photograph album : Japanese American families and communities. C1933-1958
items.description: This collection consists of a photo album with 116 black and white photographs. The photographs depict Japanese American families and communities in Berkeley, Oakland, San Jose, and other locations.

items.title: Stan Steiner papers, ca. 1961-1987
items.description: Stan Steiner was born on January 1, 1925, son of Bernard and Regina Storch Steiner of Brooklyn. After attending the University of Wisconsin for a year, Steiner hitchhiked West from New York in 1945 and began a forty year love affair with the people and places of the American West.

items.title: The Baltic video archive : Baltic video testimonies at Stanford Libraries
items.description: "The Baltic Video Archive of Stanford Libraries consists of four oral history collections, each of which tells the story of the Baltic countries through video testimonies of the Baltic peoples.

items.title: Palo Alto Rebekah Cook Book : typed copy, ca. 1944
items.description: The cookbook, compiled by Leona Andrieu and Clara Oeschger, contains favorite recipes of members and friends. It is dedicated to the President of the Rebekah Assembly, Rena A. Trimble.

items.title: Stanford University Medical Center Auxiliary, 1920-2015
items.description: This collection includes materials from the Stanford University Medical Center Auxiliary from its beginning in 1959 as the Palo Alto Hospital Auxiliary to its dissolution in 2015.

items.title: The Pacific Rocket Society : historical report
items.description: Volume 1. Summary of the history of the Pacific Rocket Society -- A Pacific Rocket Society Mojave test trip -- Mojave test area revisited -- Volume 2.

items.title: Anne Guthrie papers, ca. 1929-1957
items.description: Secretary and advisor to the Y.W.C.A., particularly in The Philippines. Representative of The International Alliance of Women to the General Assembly of The United Nations, Biographer of Vijaya Lakshimi Pandit, High Commissioner from Irelia to The United Kingdom. Box 1 contains books, photographs, and correspondence.

sectors.name: Society and community

items.title: Kaiser Shipyards women's chorus : photographs, 1942-1945
items.description: A collection of 19 original photographs documenting the activities of an all-girl chorus comprised of a dozen young women who also worked at the Kaiser Permanente Shipyard in Richmond, CA during World War II.

items.title: Wendell P. Hammon collection of papers relating to the Economic Opportunity Commission of Santa Clara County, Inc., 1964-1971
items.description: Box 1. Correspondence, memos, commission meeting agendas and minutes, proposals. Box 2. Operating manual, The Community Action Program Guide, 1964; The Santa Clara Community Action Program; an evaluation , 1968; Proposed program for EOC of Santa Clara County presented to the Office of Economic Opportunity, 1965.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: Fred J. Buenzle papers. circa 1870-1946
items.description: Fred J. Buenzle (1872-1946) was a yeoman in the United States Navy in the late nineteenth century. As a yeoman, his main duties were stenography and typing for officers. Buenzle also chronicled his tours of duty in the Carribean, England, and China.

items.title: National management of high-energy physics facilities papers
items.description: Professor of physics and director of the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center. Memoranda, letters, and a background paper by Panofsky prepared for a meeting of University Presidents concerning national management of high-energy physics facilities.

items.title: Herbert Hoover off the record talks typescripts
items.description: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States, 1929-1933, earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford University in May 1895. He founded the Hoover War Library at Stanford in 1919 and was instrumental in creating the Food Research Institute and the Graduate School of Business at Stanford.

items.title: Nixon-Krushchev "Kitchen debate," Moscow, 1959 : [videorecording] / recorded by Joseph Roizen
items.description: Footage of the famous "kitchen debate" between Vice President Richard Nixon and Premier Nikita Khrushchev at the American National Exhibition in Moscow on July 24, 1959.

items.title: Richard A. Stepp papers, 1937-1995
items.description: Richard A. Stepp earned his A.B. in social sciences at Stanford University in 1939 and his MBA in 1941. While a student he was business manager for the Stanford Daily, 1938-39, and a member of the Alpha Tau Omega fraternity.

items.title: William M. Roth papers, 1914-1973 (bulk 1950-1973)
items.description: United States Ambassador, American businessman, negotiator.

items.title: Business and industry's effect on the financing of Palo Alto city services and the Palo Alto Unified School District, 1965 Mar. 1.
items.description: Both tangible and intangible criteria were sought; cross-analyses were made to develop forecasts on probable effects to the city services, the school system, and the city's population growth based on projected changes in business and industry.

items.title: Francis V. Keesling papers, 1908-1972 (bulk 1947-1972)
items.description: Francis Valentine Keesling, Jr., born 3 March 1908 in San Francisco, California, graduated from Yale University in 1930 and from Stanford University Law School in 1933. He practiced law in San Francisco from 1934 to 1955, and was with West Coast Life Insurance Co. 1936-1977.

items.title: Olaf Pitt Jenkins papers, 1929-1973 (bulk 1946-1958)
items.description: Olaf P. Jenkins, son of Stanford University professor Oliver P. Jenkins, earned his A.B., 1913, M.A., 1915, and PhD., 1930, from Stanford University. He worked for state geological surveys in Tennessee, Washington, and Arizona and held positions with several private companies.

items.title: Project MKULTRA collection, 1977
items.description: Project MKULTRA, sponsored by the Central Intelligence Agency, conducted research on various aspects of human behavioral control in the 1950s and 1960s, some of which involved the Stanford University Medical School.

items.title: Frank B. Yoakum diaries, 1932-1990
items.description: Founding partner in the Los Angeles law firm of Iverson, Yoakum, Papiano and Hatch where he worked until he was 84. Trained at Stanford ('29), he went on to represent numerous important clients in various important cases.

items.title: In the matter of the estate of Jane L. Stanford, deceased: legal briefs, correspondence, and clippings
items.description: Collection pertains to claims against Jane L. Stanford's estate from the adopted children of her niece Amy L. Hansen, who was a legatee in Jane Stanford's will, and includes three legal briefs, clippings, and correspondence between James D. Adams of the law firm representing Stanford and Ruth Scibird, curator of the…

items.title: Lowell Turrentine papers, 1913-1956
items.description: Lowell Turrentine earned his undergraduate degree at Princeton in 1917 and his law degrees at Harvard in 1922 and 1929. items.description: Interviews conducted 1974 by Gabrielle Morris for the Regional Oral History Office, Bancroft Library. Introduction by Winifred Heard. Copies of photographs and documentary material included. Recollections of growing up in Berkeley; student days at University of California, 1914-1918.

items.title: Collection of political match book covers, 1950-1970
items.description: Album containing 695 match book covers, each promoting a politician in California. The album is heavily weighted toward local candidates and is organized by political office. The earliest dates are in the 1950s; the last dates appear to be mid-1970s.

items.title: Francis V. Keesling papers, 1906-1957
items.description: Correspondence, political and business papers. Major subjects include Republican campaigns and policies, the Progressive-Regular Republican split in California (1910-1920), the San Francisco charter of 1931, building of the Golden Gate Bridge, the San Francisco earthquake and fire of 1910 and activities of the…

items.title: J. Arthur Younger papers, 1951-1968
items.description: Jesse Arthur Younger, born 11 April 1893, Albany, Oregon, moved to Kirkland, Washington, graduated from the University of Washington at Seattle in 1915, and served in World War I.

items.title: J. Arthur Younger papers, 1964-1968
items.description: Jesse Arthur Younger, born 11 April 1893, Albany, Oregon, moved to Kirkland, Washington, graduated from the University of Washington at Seattle in 1915, and served in World War I.

items.title: Fred Turner papers, 1968-2019
items.description: Fred Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Communication at Stanford University and Director of Stanford's Program in Science, Technology, and Society.

items.title: From Satori to Silicon Valley : San Francisco and the American counterculture / Theodore Roszak
items.description: The collection contains the editorial files of Stewart Brand and Jay Kinney, reader correspondence, photographic materials, and memorabilia. Also contains correspondence, clippings, photographs, promotional material, and issues of the magazines. The Jay Kinney Editorial files span the years 1982 through 1984.

items.title: Midpeninsula Free University publications, 1966-1970
items.description: The Midpeninsula Free University (MFU) was a free university, operating primarily between 1966 and 1971 on the San Francisco Midpeninsula. The MFU offered an open curriculum; anyone who paid the nominal membership fee of $10 could offer a course in any subject.

items.title: Midpeninsula Free University, 1967-1970
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, Menlo Park, and Mountain View, California. Founded in 1966 and closed in 1971.

items.title: Point foundation records, 1964-1975
items.description: The Point foundation (not to be confused with the National LGBTQ Scholarship Fund of the same name) was a nonprofit organization based in San Francisco and founded by Stewart Brand and Richard "Dick" Raymond, growing out of their work with the Portola Institute and the Whole Earth Catalog.

items.title: Stewart Brand papers, 1954-2000
items.description: Writer, editor, entrepreneur, and futurist Stewart Brand was born December 14, 1938 in Rockford, Illinois. He attended Phillips Exeter Academy in New Hampshire, and attended Stanford University where he studied biology with Paul Ehrlich.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history

items.title: R. Buckminster Fuller materials from Herbert Matter, circa 1960-1969 and undated
items.description: Two short 16 mm film reels of World Game activities as well as numerous negatives related to the World Game and Dymaxion maps. Also included are some manuscript notes (by Herbert Matter or his wife, Mercedes Matter?) on the subject of drawing.

items.title: Walter A. Huston collection of R. Buckminster Fuller material, circa 1965-1975
items.description: Collection contains books, articles, manuscripts, ephemera, audio cassettes, tapes, film, photographs and slides collected by Walter A. Huston about R. Buckminster Fuller. Many of the items are signed or inscribed to Huston or his father, John Huston. Box 1-2 contain books and articles by or about Fuller.

items.title: William Shockley and eugenics collection, 1966-1978
items.description: William Shockley was a Professor of engineering at Stanford (1958-1975; emeritus 1975-1989). He was a co-recipient of the Nobel Prize in physics, 1956. While working at Stanford, Shockley embraced and advocated for eugenics.

items.description: Archie Boston was born in Clewiston, Florida in 1943 and was raised in St. Petersburg, Florida. Boston graduated from the Chouinard Art Institute in Los Angeles, California with a Bachelors of Fine Arts degree in Advertising Design in 1964.

items.title: Regis McKenna papers, 1973-2012
items.description: Regis McKenna is known for pioneering several theories and practices of technology marketing and is credited with helping to launch some of the most important technological innovations developed in Silicon Valley from the 1970s through the 1990s, including the first microprocessor (Intel), the first personal computer…

items.title: Howard Seifert papers
items.description: Howard S. Seifert (1911-1977), an authority on rocket propulsion of space vehicles, was professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford from 1960 to 1976. He also directed the Physical Sciences Laboratory at the United Aircraft Corporation (1960-65) and was president of the American Rocket Society (1960).

items.title: Jay Arthurs papers, 1971 and 1983
items.description: Includes publicity material and photographs of Apollo 15 and transcriptions of the landing dialog from the first Challenger mission.

items.title: Joseph D. Cusick collection of Lockheed Missiles & Space Co. and the U.S. Air Force Satellite Test Center records, 1962-1991
items.description: History, policies, organization, personnel, and technical training materials collected by Joseph D. Cusick during employment. Includes the serial, TRW Space Log, 1968-1979.

items.title: Nicholas J. Hoff papers, 1903-1997 (inclusive), 1940-1997 (bulk)
items.description: Nicholas J. Hoff was a professor emeritus of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University at the time of his death in 1997. Born on Jan. 3, 1906 in the small town of Magyarovar in western Hungary, he came to Stanford in 1939 for graduate work and earned his Ph.D. in 1942.

items.title: Rich Potter collection of Ford Aerospace materials, 1969-1989
items.description: Ford Aerospace was a division of the Ford Motor Company that existed from 1956-1990. It was based in Newport Beach, California. Rich Potter worked as an intern in Human Resources for Ford Aerospace in 1989.

items.title: Robert T. Jones papers, 1912-1996 (inclusive), 1930-1996 (bulk)
items.description: Robert T. Jones, one of the premier theoretical aerodynamicists of the twentieth century, was a research scientist with NASA, and its predecessor NACA, from 1934 until his retirement in 1982, when he joined the Stanford faculty as a consulting professor in aeronautics.

items.title: Terence O'Laughlin collection of manuals and documentation for several ELINT systems manufactured by the Watkins-Johnson Company, circa 1970s
items.description: The collection consists of notebooks and manuals related to systems manufactured by the Watkins-Johnson Company.

items.title: William Francis Whitmore papers, 1945-1991
items.description: William Francis Whitmore (1917-1996) was an American mathematician, physicist, and scientist with a focus on the field of oceanography who was heavily involved in the development of weapons and ocean technology for the United States Navy.
items.era_note: Shown here on the 376 dated folders its finding aid lists, rather than on the dates above.

items.description: These round table discussions on the history of artificial intelligence research were held at SRI on December 1, 1999. Speakers included Charles Rosen, Peter Hart, Nils Nilsson, Thomas Garvey, Martin Fischler, Robert Bowles, John Lowrance, Richard Waldinger, and Jerry Hobbs.

items.title: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence records, 1969-2011
items.description: Correspondence, manuscripts submitted to AI Magazine, conference presentations, audio visual materials, and a full run of AI Magazine.

items.description: David Glenn Hays (November 17, 1928 - July 26, 1995) was born in Memphis, TN. He graduated from Harvard College in 1951, and received his PhD in Sociology, also from Harvard, in 1954. Contains research notes, correspondence, typescript drafts and articles by Hays and others.

items.description: Documentary regarding expert systems and focusing on the Stanford Heuristic Programming Project.

items.description: The materials consist of videorecordings of lectures by Pat Hayes (Xerox PARC and Stanford University) and Nils Nilsson (Stanford University) on the topic of knowledge representation.

items.description: Richard Earl Fikes is Professor (Research) Emeritus in the Computer Science department of Stanford University. items.title: Robert Engelmore papers, 1976-1998 (inclusive), 1978-1986 (bulk)
items.description: Robert Engelmore earned three degrees in physics from Carnegie Mellon University: BS 1956, MS 1958, and PhD 1962. He came to Stanford University in 1970 as research associate in the Heuristic Programming Project, Dept. of Computer Science, becoming Executive Director in 1985. He retired from Stanford in 1998.

Harman (1918-1997) was a professor emeritus of engineering at Stanford University, senior social scientist at SRI International of Menlo Park, president of the Institute of Noetic Sciences, cofounder of the World Business Academy, and served on the University of California Board of Regents.

items.title: Charles Babbage Institute Oral History collection, 1979-1991
items.description: Founded in 1978, the Charles Babbage Institute is the University of Minnesota's research center for advancing the understanding of computing, information, and culture.

items.description: Mitterand visited Stanford's Center for Integrated Systems on March 26, 1984 and spoke with academic researchers, capitalists, and industry representatives concerning high technology research and industry. Participants included Donald Kennedy, Stanford's President.

items.title: Dorothy Regnery papers, 1980-1991
items.description: Historian, particularly interested in central California and Stanford University. Research materials for several projects, including the Stanford's Sacramento house and the Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve history.

items.title: Franklin Chiang Photographs, circa 1966-1972
items.description: Franklin Chiang (1925-2016) was the son of Chinese military general Sun-Pu Chiang in Chengdu, Sichuan, China. During World War II, Chiang flew for the China National Aviation Corporation and was based out of Kunming, 1942-1945. From 1945-1948, Chiang attended Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

items.title: John F. Manley papers, 1946-2000 (inclusive), 1983-2000 (bulk)
items.description: John F. Manley (1939-2020) was a professor of political science, emeritus at Stanford University with a thirty-year tenure, which began in 1971. As a political scientist, Manley's scholarship focused on presidential power, public policy making and the function of Congress.

items.title: Materials on the history of the Stanford University endowment, 1903-2004
items.description: Robert Augsburger was Stanford's vice president for business and finance from 1971 to 1977 and a lecturer in management at the Graduate School of Business from 1971 until he retired in 1995.

items.description: Presents Congressman John Anderson's visit to Stanford University in 1981.

items.title: Patrick Suppes : an interview conducted by David W. Mitchell : transcript, 2007
items.description: Oral history interview conducted in May 2007. Topics include his activities with Dr. Fred Terman; Stanford’s development into a major research university; his interests in logic, computers, learning theory and brain function; and the teaching of math.

items.title: Peninsula-Times Tribune  photographs of Stanford University
items.description: The Peninsula-Times Tribune was organized in April 1979 from a merger of the Palo Alto Times and the Redwood City Tribune, both owned by the parent company Peninsula Newspapers Incorported. The paper ceased publishing in 1993.

items.title: Rixford Kinney Snyder, "Memories of a Santa Clara Valley Boy Who Never Left, 1908-1991" typescript
items.description: Rixford Kinney Snyder, Professor of History, Dean of Admissions, and first Director of the Alumni Association's Travel/Study Program. items.title: Stanford Alumni Association, the Audible Stanford
items.description: Founded in 1892 by the University's inaugural graduates, Stanford Alumni Association (SAA) orchestrates a wide spectrum of offerings and programming to provide support throughout individuals' Stanford journeys, encompassing their student years and subsequent lives as alumni.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society oral history program interviews
items.description: The Stanford Historical Society's Oral History Program explores the institutional history of the University, with an emphasis on the transformative post-WWII period, through interviews with leading faculty, staff, alumni, trustees, and others.

items.title: Stanford News Service records 1931-2023

items.title: Stanford Oral History Project interviews, 1971-1995
items.description: The oral history interviews in the SOHP collection are carefully planned historical documents which we hope will serve a wide range of scholarly interests. Five additional sets of oral history interviews are listed separately: a set of interviews with members of the early Aurora newspaper collection.

items.title: Stanford Speech Collection
items.description: The Stanford Speech Collection consists of audio recordings on open reel tape of speeches, lectures, interviews and panel discussions at or sponsored by Stanford University from the 1950s through the early 70s.

items.title: Stanford Tape Collection
items.description: Historic music and speech recordings on open reel tape, made on the campus of Stanford University. aqa The Stanford Tape Collection consists of historic music and speech recordings made on the campus of Stanford University. Many were used in the production of broadcasts by university radio station KZSU.

items.title: Stanford University Audio collection, circa 1949-2006 (inclusive)
items.description: The materials consist of audio recordings of Stanford events and activities.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: Biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University. items.description: This film in celebration of Stanford University's centennial includes interviews with faculty and alumni; scenes of academic and student activities; views of the campus; and still photographs transferred to video, primarily concerning the history of Stanford.

items.title: The living legends: a discussion about the establishment of the Computer Science Department at Stanford University : videorecording, 1997
items.description: A discussion amongst John McCarthy, Edward Feigenbaum, Robert W. Floyd, Donald Knuth, Gene Golub, Gio Wiederhold, John G. Herriot, and William F. Miller on the history of computer science at Stanford, recorded on March 22, 1997 by Andy Kacsman.

items.title: Uncommon man dinner [videorecording]
items.description: Awards presented to William R. Hewlett, Lucille Packard, and David Packard; speakers included Peggy Menzinger, president of Stanford Associates, William R. Hewlett, and David W. Packard. Event also included "Uncommon Musical Salute," created and narrated by Peter Arnot.

items.title: Visit of Li Peng to Stanford University : video recording, 1985
items.description: Li Peng, vice premier of China, visited Stanford University and the Center for Integrated Systems as part of a tour of Silicon Valley industries in July of 1985. While at Stanford he participated in a panel discussion with Stanford professors and Silicon Valley experts and gave a talk.

items.title: Williamson M. Evers papers
items.description: Williamson M. Evers is an American libertarian and member of the Libertarian Party National Committee. He was a former research fellow at the Hoover Institution where he specialized in research on education policy.
