items.description: Academic Computing provides technology expertise, resources, and services directly to students and faculty, and to other organizations that in turn support aspects of the mission This collection consists of Jefferey Olson's doctoral research materials and recorded inteviews held in 1986 with administrators in charge…

items.title: Donald Kennedy, President of Stanford University, papers
items.description: Kennedy, holder of three degrees from Harvard, joined Stanford's biology faculty in 1960; while on leave from 1977 to 1979 he served in Washington, D.C., as commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration. Kennedy was Stanford's eighth president, serving from 1980 to 1992.

items.title: Edward E. Shaw papers
items.description: Edward E. Shaw, born November 8, 1942, Stanford B.A. in economics 1965, joined the administrative staff of Stanford in the fall of 1965 as a contract administrator in the controller's office. In 1970 he became Assistant to the Vice President for Research, William F. Miller.

items.title: H. Bruce Franklin Collection
items.description: This collection includes newspapers clippings, Stanford news releases, leaflets and pamphlets relating to Franklin's tenure and dismissal hearings, the full text of the Advisory Board's recommendations, and transcripts of hearing proceedings.

items.title: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve records, 1931-1992
items.description: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve, which lies on 1,189 acres of Stanford land, routinely supports 45 to 50 research projects annually, with the majority directed by Stanford faculty and students. Parts of Jasper Ridge have been used for educational and research purposes since the founding of the university in 1891.

items.title: Joshua Lederberg papers, 1959-1979
items.description: Lederberg earned his Ph.D. at Yale University in 1947. He taught genetics at the University of Wisconsin before coming to the Stanford University School of Medicine in 1959 as Professor of genetics and biology.

items.title: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson papers, 1941-1990
items.description: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Stanford in 1940 and returned after his wartime service in the Navy to earn his MBA in 1947. After seven years in the business world, he returned to Stanford in 1954 as assistant to university president J. E. Wallace Sterling.

items.title: Richard W. Lyman personal papers, 1778-2011
items.description: Lyman was born in Philadelphia in 1923 and raised in New Haven, Conn. His father, a chemist who lost his job during the recession that followed World War I, became an attorney. His mother taught French. His exposure to the world began with a summer visit to Belgium to visit his maternal grandmother.

items.title: Stanford Computation Center photographs, circa 1968-1972

items.title: Stanford University, Assistant to the President for Black Affairs, records
items.description: In 1968, Stanford University created the new office of Assistant Provost for Minority Affairs, naming James E. Simmons to the post; in 1969, Mr. Simmon's title was changed to Assistant to the President for Black Affairs.

items.title: Stanford University, Career Planning and Placement Center, records
items.description: Established in 1952 as the Stanford Placement Service, the office changed its name and concentration to Career Planning and Placement Center in 1965.

items.title: Stanford University, Committee on Land and Building Development, records, 1950-1999
items.description: The Committee on Land and Building Development is responsible for providing input and/or recommendations to the President and other administrative officers on the planning and development of academic campus lands; on basic design guidelines for architecture and landscaping; and planning for transportation services.

items.title: Stanford University, University Committee on Minority Issues, records
items.description: The University Committe on Minority Issues was established by the President and Provost in October 1987 in response to a demand by the Rainbow Agenda (a coalition of minority groups) to explore the critical concerns of minority students, faculty, and staff at Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The Business Affairs organization at Stanford provides integrated financial, technological, business and human resource services for the benefit of the university community.

items.title: Bruce Bliven papers, 1906-1985

He received a B.A. in English in 1911.

items.description: Contains the taped Califas Conference (held at the University of California, Santa Cruz, in 1982) as well as presentations of musical and theatrical works, interviews with performers, artists, and authors, and exhibitions of art. A comprehensive presentation of Chicano culture and society in California.

items.description: Carolyn Caddes (1935- ) is an American photographer who spent years photographing portraits of famous Californian innovators. Her book, Portraits of Success: Impressions of Silicon Valley Pioneers, focused on Silicon Valley technology visionaries such as Steve Jobs, Robert Noyce and David Packard.

items.description: Doug Menuez spent over fifteen years documenting the leading innovators of the digital revolution in Silicon Valley. The project begain when Steve Jobs granted Menuez exclusive access to record his new start-up, NeXT Computer for LIFE magazine.

items.title: Gerd Stern papers, 1938-2012
items.description: Gerd Stern is a poet, artist, and multimedia innovator whose remarkable life spans 40s bohemia, 50s Beat culture, 60s hippiedom, 70s hip capitalism, and onward. This collection is primarily correspondence, and dated outgoing drafts predominate.

items.description: Sound recordings from Stanford University professor and choral director Harold C. Schmidt (1910-1993), including performances from the Stanford University Chorus, Choir, and Chamber Chorale.

items.description: A collection of approximately 160 photographs, chiefly comprised of portraits, taken by Ilka Hartmann, ca. 1960s-2000s, and focusing on notable activists, environmentalists, writers, poets, artists, musicians in Northern California.

items.title: Ira Nowinski photograph collection, ca. 1965-2017
items.description: Ira Nowinski is an American photographer of Polish and Hungarian Jewish descent. Born ca. 1942 and raised in New York, he was the first person in his family born in the United States. At the age of 42, he was prodded by opera singer Regina Resnick to do a photo essay around the Jewish milieu.

items.title: José Antonio Burciaga papers, circa 1940-1997
items.description: After receiving his B.A. in fine arts from the University of Texas El Paso in 1968, Jose Antonio "Tony" Burciaga (1940–1996) began working as an illustrator and graphic arts designer, while also nurturing an interest in poetry. items.title: Linda Connor photography collection
items.description: Accession 2018-559: this accession consists of a total of 33 photographs from Connor's Lick Observatory series (ten (10) 8” x 10” gelatin silver prints, twenty‐two (22) 11” x 14” gelatin silver prints, and one (1) 20” x 24” gelatin silver print). items.description: Lola de la Riva (born 1938 in Stockton, California) is a Chicana activist and artist. Includes documents, correspondence, research material, artworks, books and other publications, audio cassettes, and other materials.

items.description: Mary Jane Moffat (1933-2004) was an poet and memoirist who taught creative writing at San Francisco State, Foothill College, and other venues. She focused on the art of autobiography and the writing of memoirs.

When he was 21, Kahn joined Stanford's Department of Art (now the Department of Art and Art History).

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Birge M. Clark papers, 1914-1985
items.description: Palo Alto architect. Received his AB from Stanford in 1914 and B.Arch. from Columbia in 1917. Served as advising architect on the Lou Henry Hoover house and created numerous distinctive public buildings and private homes in Palo Alto.

items.title: Building 1; history and changes of Varian's Building 1, Palo Alto, 1993
items.description: Text, site plans, architectural drawings, additions, master plan, and drawings.

items.title: Claude Stoller collection of R. Buckminster Fuller material, 1955-1980
items.description: Claude Stoller (born 1921) was a faculty member in the Department of Architecture at the University of California. His main passion centered on social issues such as inequities in housing, community concerns about redevelopment plans, and creating energy-efficient designs.

items.title: Hanna House board of governors meeting minutes, 1989-1998
items.description: In 1937, the distinguished architect Frank Lloyd Wright finalized the design of a residence for the Hanna family atop a hill overlooking Stanford University. the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake left it empty and desolate.

items.title: Hanna house collection, 1900-1995 (inclusive)
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Construction, begun in 1937, continued in four stages over 25 years.

items.title: Hanna House collection, 1935-1982 [microform]
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Construction, begun in 1937, continued in four stages over 25 years.

items.title: Harry Sanders; a Stanford Planner Charts the History of Campus Planning, and Church's Contribution
items.description: Harry L. Sanders was the first full-time director of planning at Stanford University. He joined the Planning Office in 1956, was appointed director in 1960, and retired in 1976; during his tenure, Stanford experienced its greatest period of development since its opening in 1891.

items.title: Lee Emerson Bassett house records
items.description: Lee Emerson Bassett, professor of Speech and Drama at Stanford University from 1900 to 1938, built his home on campus at 740 Santa Ynez Street. Included in this collection are specifications by the architect, A. W. Smith; bills and one letter from Leon S. Bean, general contractor, 1909.

items.title: Memorial Church acoustics papers
items.description: Typescript paper "Acoustical Renovation of Memorial Church at Stanford University," 1996, a copy of ACOUSTICS OF WORSHIP SPACES (edited by Wetherill and David Lubman, 1983), which has an entry on Memorial Church, and 99 slides of the interior and exterior of the church, 1979-87.

items.title: Morley Baer photographs
items.description: Morley Baer, former head of the photography department of the San Francisco Art Institute, was a prize-winning photographer, well-known for his photographs of Victorian houses in San Francisco as well as images of California's farmlands and coastline.

items.title: Sabin and O'Neal, Architects : photograph catalog of firm's designs, circa 1983
items.description: Residential, civic, industrial, and commercial architectural designs and photographs, primarily from the San Francisco Bay Area and within it primarily in Palo Alto and Stanford.

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. Architects active during the early years of the University include Bakewell and Brown; Shepley, Rutan, and Coolidge.

items.title: Stanford University, University Architect / Campus Planning and Design, records, 1945-2018
items.description: The Planning Office was officially organized in 1945 under the directorship of Eldridge T. Spencer. In addition to overseeing the architectural aspects of the campus, the office was also responsible for overseeing land use and traffic circulation.

items.title: Synergetics folio : set of ten screen printed posters, 1976-1977
items.description: This folio was published as a result of an exhibition on the work of Buckminster Fuller presented at the Penang Museum in 1978. This is set #7 of an edition of 44.

items.title: Victor K. Thompson Architectural Drawings, 1948-2000
items.description: Victor King Thompson (1913-2007) was a Stanford University professor emeritus of architecture. Thompson joined the University in 1948 and coordinated Stanford's architecture program, inviting practicing architects as guest lecturers, and taught art history for 25 years before his retirement.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Film, radio and television

items.title: Dorothy Fadiman/Concentric Media papers, 1955-2018
items.description: Dorothy Fadiman is the founder of Concentric Media, and has been producing films for 40 years. Awards include an Emmy, an Oscar nomination, and a Gold Medal from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. She currently lives in Menlo Park, CA, with her husband James Fadiman. They have two daughters, Renee and Maria.

items.title: HEARTS & QUARKS : production materials, 1987-1988
items.description: Jane Wagner received her B.Sc and M.Sc in political sociology from the London School of Economics . She completed her master's degree in documentary film production at Stanford University in 1988.

items.title: KSFO Collection
items.description: The KSFO collection consists of audiovisual material and ephemera from this San Francisco radio station's years owned by Golden West Broadcasting, 1956-1983.

items.title: Pacifica Foundation ephemera collection, 1949-1984
items.description: Lew Hill founded the Pacifica Foundation and its flagship radio station KPFA in 1949. KPFA began broadcasting in Berkeley, California on April 15th, 1949, and was was the first listener-subscription FM educational radio station in the country.

items.title: Peter Conn papers, circa early 1970s-1996
items.description: Peter Conn is a director and producer known for his advances in 3D computer-generated animation, graphics, and motion capture technology, primarily through his production company Homer & Associates.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Press, journalism and broadcasting

items.title: David Bohrman archive of innovation in media & journalism, circa 1960s-2014
items.description: Materials include Bohrman's papers as well as ephemera, and two servers of digital files, and additional digital files received via electronic transfer.
items.era_note: Shown here on a reading of the collection, rather than on the dates above.

items.title: Kate Coleman papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of print, manuscript, photographs and some audiovisual materials relating to the journalism career of Kate Coleman.

items.title: Reese Erlich papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: Reese Erlich (1947-2021) was an author and freelance journalist living and working in the Bay Area for much of his career. Erlich graduated from UC Berkeley in 1970 with a BA in Political and Social Change. Reese Erlich's papers consist of his journalism and book research as well as historical political publications.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Sport and recreation

items.title: Basic mountaineering course : typescript, 1971
items.description: Includes chapters on equipment (Ed Goddard), food, map and compass, weather, first aid, and a reprint of a John Fowles article, "Weeds, Bugs, Americans." Also included are cartoon drawings by Jack Dreyfuss and 8 pages of sources (books, food, equipment, etc.) Also includes the training schedule with a list of the…

items.title: Camp Unalayee Association records, 1949-2025
items.description: Camp Unalayee was founded in 1949 with Lucile Manley's donation of her home and land in the Santa Cruz Mountains to the American Friends Service Committee (AFSC) with the intent to operate an "interracial camp managed by Friends." The camp operated as the Ben Lomond Friends' Camp throughout the 1950s and was closely…

items.title: Leigh N. Ortenburger papers and photographs, 1929-1996
items.description: Leigh Natus Ortenburger was born in Norman, Oklahoma in 1929, the youngest of three brothers. Correspondence, manuscripts, subject files, photographs, and negatives.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: A Century of Western Living, 1898-1998 : poster for centennial exhibit, 1998
Bjarne B. Dahl restoration reports, 1929-2007
items.description: Bjarne B. Dahl was a piano and harpsichord restorer from Sunnyvale, California. Materials include photographic reports (consisting of a written description, photographic prints, and negatives) documenting Dahl's restoration work on antique keyboard instruments.

items.title: Fidelity Sound Recordings Collection
items.description: Reg McGovern (1920-2015) had a 36-year career as a newspaper photographer in Redwood City and Palo Alto, and he received many journalism awards for his photography.

items.title: Fine press keepsakes sponsored by William P. Wreden, 1953-1995
items.description: Bookman and owner of William P. Wreden Books & Manuscripts, established in 1938. In addition to 15 keepsakes sponsored by Mr. Wreden, there is REMINISCENCES, published in 1988 by his son, Bo Wreden, to celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of the opening of the bookshop, as well as Mr. Wreden's memorial service program…

items.title: Jalonen theater & music program collection
items.description: Performances are mostly from San Francisco and the Peninsula, as well as some items from Portland, New York, and a few other cities in the United States and Europe. Collection of playbills and programs from theater, opera, ballet, and musical performances in the Bay Area between the 1940s and early 2000s.

items.title: Stanford University Press archival book copies, 1900-2013
items.description: The Stanford University Press was established as an independent printing operation at Stanford University in 1892. The university purchased it in 1917, and expanded it into a full-service publishing house in 1925. The collection consists of archival copies of books published by Stanford University Press.

items.title: Sunset Magazine : video, 18 Oct. 1998
items.description: Includes interviews of Mel and Bill Lane. Discusses the role of Sunset Magazine over the last one hundred years.

items.title: Sunset Magazine records, 1931-1998
items.description: Collection primarily consists of over 100,000 photographs, prints, slides, transparencies and layouts as published in the magazine from 1948-1969 and 1977-1998.

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: "Freiheit für Angela Davis" ephemera collection, 1971-1972
items.description: Angela Davis (born 1944) is an American political activist, who was arrested in 1970 in relation to a murder case. Campaigns for solidarity with Davis were popular throughout both West and East Germany. Materials include correspondence from the East German "Freiheit für Angela Davis" Campaign, 1971-1972.

items.title: Adele Panofsky collection of Mid-Peninsula Citizens for Fair Housing materials, 1963-2009
items.description: Adele Panofsky was a resident of Los Altos, California. She was a member of the Mid-Peninsula Citizens for Fair Housing (MCFH) and served as the Treasurer from 1969-1978. The MCFH was originally created in 1964 to oppose Propistion 14.

items.title: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California records, 1900-2000 bulk 1934-2000
items.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is a non-profit organization committed to the defense, preservation, and extension of civil liberties in the United States.

items.title: Armando Valdez papers, 1965-2005
items.description: Armando Valdez, born January 2, 1944, received his bachelor's degree in Sociology from San Jose State College in January 1967. Valdez was a work-study student in the Economic Opportunity Program and in 1965 he was assigned to coordinate a special summer program in the Physics Department of Stanford University…

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- David Harris & Joan Baez, 1967-2014
items.description: David Harris, opponent of U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War, appeared at the Oakland, California, Federal Induction Center demonstrations during October and December of 1967. On January 17, 1968, he publicly refused to cooperate with the military draft.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Dorothy Day and the Catholic Worker Movement, 1968-1973
items.description: Dorothy Day (November 8, 1897 - November 29, 1980) was an American journalist, social activist, and devout Catholic convert. In the 1930s, Day worked closely with fellow activist Peter Maurin to establish the Catholic Worker Movement, a nonviolent, pacifist movement that continues to combine direct aid for the poor…

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive, 1965-2013
items.description: Bob Dewitt Fitch (1939-2016) was an activist, photojournalist, union steward, community organizer, minister, housing program manager, and musician. He was born in Los Angeles, California on July 20, 1939. His father, Robert, was a professor of Christian ethics and a United Church of Christ minister.

items.title: California social, protest, and counterculture movements ephemera collection, 1965-1980
items.description: Consists of a variety of ephemera related to social, protest, and counterculture movements in California, particularly in San Francisco and the greater Bay Area. The bulk of the materials dates from 1965-1980.

items.title: Christopher Jones papers, 1965-2016
items.description: Christopher William "Colorado" Jones (January 12, 1949 - June 29, 2019) was born in 1949 in Palo Alto. He attended the Peninsula School and Pacific High School. Jones was a Vietnam War draft resister and was sentenced to Safford Federal Prison from 1970-1971.

items.title: Collection of materials opposing the Simpson-Mazzoli Bill, 1982
items.description: The Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1982 (the Simpson-Mazzoli Bill) called on employers to attest to employee immigration status and made it illegal to knowingly hire unauthorized immigrants. This first attempt was defeated, but the bill was eventually passed in 1986.

items.title: Community Service Organization History Project records, 1997-2009
items.description: The Community Service Organization was an important California Latino civil rights organization, most famous for training Cesar Chavez. It was founded in 1948 by Fred Ross, Antonio Rios and Edward Roybal to empower immigrants through such programs such as voter registration drives, citizenship classes, lawsuits and…

items.title: Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR) records, 1980-2004
items.description: Records of the policy group Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR), consisting of correspondence, memoranda, newsletters, board minutes, publications, media, and other material. Finding aid contains folder listing only; collection has not been physically processed.

items.title: East Palo Alto Council of Tenants records, undated
items.description: The East Palo Alto Council of Tenants, founded in 1982, is an organization dedicated to protecting tenants' rights in East Palo Alto, California.

items.title: John W. Gardner papers, 1912-2004
items.description: John Gardner earned his B.A. and M.A. in Psychology from Stanford University and his Ph.D. in Psychology from the University of California, Berkeley. Gardner served as the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare under President Lyndon Johnson from 1965-1968.

items.title: Lois Crozier Hogle papers, 1950-2002
items.description: Lois Crozier Hogle (1913-2005) was born in Coalinga and raised in California's San Joaquín Valley by Clare and Hubert Crozier. Her father was a farmer and a lawyer.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund was incorporated in 1967 by Pete Tijerina, following a meeting convened by Jack Greenberg of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, between Tijerina, San Antonians Albert Peña and Roy Padilla, and Bill Pincus, a Ford Foundation representative.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1967-1993
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund was incorporated in 1967 by Pete Tijerina, following a meeting convened by Jack Greenberg of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, between Tijerina, San Antonians Albert Peña and Roy Padilla, and Bill Pincus, a Ford Foundation representative.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 5, Legal Programs Department, 1968-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund was incorporated in 1967 by Pete Tijerina, following a meeting convened by Jack Greenberg of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, between Tijerina, San Antonians Albert Peña and Roy Padilla, and Bill Pincus, a Ford Foundation representative.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 6, Community Education and Activation program, 1976-1982
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund was incorporated in 1967 by Pete Tijerina, following a meeting convened by Jack Greenberg of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, between Tijerina, San Antonians Albert Peña and Roy Padilla, and Bill Pincus, a Ford Foundation representative.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 6.5, Leadership Programs, 1979-1994
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund was incorporated in 1967 by Pete Tijerina, following a meeting convened by Jack Greenberg of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, between Tijerina, San Antonians Albert Peña and Roy Padilla, and Bill Pincus, a Ford Foundation representative.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 9, Regional and Program Offices, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund was incorporated in 1967 by Pete Tijerina, following a meeting convened by Jack Greenberg of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, between Tijerina, San Antonians Albert Peña and Roy Padilla, and Bill Pincus, a Ford Foundation representative.

items.title: Michelle Vignes collection, 1966-1974
items.description: Collection of photographs and photographic negatives taken by Michelle Vignes. Included are: Part 1. Portrait of French composer Darius Milhaud at Mills College, 1966. 2 rolls of negatives and proofs and 3 8 x 10 prints. Part 2. Black Panthers.

items.title: National Committee to Defend the Rights of South Vietnamese Students records, 1972
items.description: This collection consists of correspondence, petitions, and newspaper clippings regarding the National Committee to Defend the Rights of South Vietnamese Students.

items.title: National United Committee to Free Angela Davis records, circa 1970-1972
items.description: The records of the National United Committee to Free Angela Davis consists overwhelmingly of support letters, most sent from East Germany and the Soviet Union, which the group used to demonstrate global opinion about her conspiracy trial in California.

items.title: Pacific Life Community records, 1972-1982, 2017
items.description: Pacific Life Community began as a small group committed to resisting the coming of Trident [nuclear submarines] to the Pacific Northwest. It was founded in 1975 by Robert (Bob) and Janet Aldridge and Jim and Shelley Douglass (along with about a dozen others).

items.title: Pacific Studies Center records, circa 1969-2017
items.description: Materials from the Pacific Studies Center on subject matter such as Silicon Valley companies, the electronics and communications industries, environmental issues and records from company president Lenny Siegel's participation in committees on these issues, labor issues, U.S. military and weaponry, government reports…

items.title: Physicians for Social Responsibility, Mid-Peninsula & Stanford Chapter, Prescription for Prevention proceedings
items.description: Proceedings from a symposium on nuclear war held at Stanford University in October 1983. Speakers included Gordon A. Craig, Admiral Noel A.M. Gaylor, Sidney D. Drell, Erik H. Erikson, Alexander Sakharov, Helen Caldicott, Victor W. Sidel, Melvin Konner, and Robert Karl Manoff.

items.title: Robert C. Aldridge papers, circa 1970s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of collected writings, research materials, correspondence, printed material, photographs and printed ephemera relating to the life and career of Robert C. [Creston] Aldridge (1926-2022) with a particular focus on his activities as an anti-nuclear and peace activist and an advisor/consultant/sponsor…

items.title: Robert P. J. Cooney, Jr. papers on the Institute for the Study of Nonviolence, 1965-1987
items.description: Robert P. J. Cooney, Jr. is an author, editor, and graphic designer. He joined the staff at the Institute for the Study of Nonviolence in Palo Alto in the mid-1970s. The Institute was founded by Joan Baez and Ira Sandperl in the mid-1960s in Carmel Valley, California.

items.title: Robert P.J. Cooney, Jr. Papers
items.description: Six archival boxes detailing Robert P.J. Cooney's involvement with the Institute for the Study of Nonviolence, as well as related activities. [Descriptive information provided by dealer // JAD2016/8/10].

items.title: Salvador Enrique Alvarez personal archive, 1950s-2015
items.description: Materials consist of Salvador E. Alvarez's papers related to his political activism and community involvement, including the United Farm Workers, the Hispanic Catholics of America, and the founding of the School of Social Work at San Jose State.
items.era_note: Shown here on a reading of the collection, rather than on the dates above.

items.title: Stanford Physicians for Social Responsibility records, circa 1981-2005
items.description: The Stanford chapter of Physicians for Social Responsibility (PSR) was established in 1981 as a regional extension of the national organization, which was founded in 1961. These records reflect the activities of the Stanford chapter of Physicians for Social Responsibility (PSR) from its inception in 1981.

items.title: Unity/La Unidad Archive Project collection, circa 1970-1990
items.description: Unity/La Unidad was a newspaper published from 1978 to 1990 by the League of Revolutionary Struggle (M-L). Published twice a month, it appeared in three languages: English, Spanish and Chinese. The collection consists of 170.19 gigabytes of born-digital materials captured from a hard drive provided by the donor.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. The individuals and families represented include: pioneers and settlers; professionals, including teachers, doctors, scientists, lawyers and judges; bankers and merchants.

items.title: Dreams of a city [videorecording] : creating East Palo Alto
The valley of Santa Clara; historic buildings : research papers, 1965-1975
items.description: Author. Notes, maps, photographs, and clippings used in the preparation of Butler's THE VALLEY OF SANTA CLARA: HISTORIC BUILDINGS. Organized by city or town.

sectors.name: Society and community — Medicine and public health

items.title: [Collection of records from Lucile Packard Chldren's Hospital and predecessors], 1959-2002
items.description: Consists of files from organizations listed in this record, including Board meeting minutes, committee meeting minutes (legal, finance, audit, credentials and policies/procedures), chronological files and construction files. One box consists of Board of Directors biographical files.

items.title: Esther Clark papers, 1947-1973
items.description: Collection includes Clark's work with childhood accident prevention, the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, personal subject files, reprints, and photographs.

items.title: Halsted Holman papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: The papers of Halsted Holman include publications; newspaper and magazine clippings pertaining to Holman's research interests; correspondence; typescript and handwritten manuscripts and outlines for talks; anonymous patient surveys; self-care materials for patients; project reports; email and website print-outs.

items.title: Henry S. Kaplan papers, circa 1960-1983
items.description: Radiologist, cancer research pioneer and educator. Henry S. Kaplan, 1918-1985, began his teaching career at the Stanford University School of Medicine in 1948. He served as professor and chair of the Dept. of Radiology (1948 to 1972) and was named D'Ambrogio Professor of Radiology in 1975.

items.title: Jay Haley papers, 1957-2007
items.description: Jay Haley (1923-2007) was born in an oil town in Wyoming. He was a pioneer in family therapy, and his work traces its birth and development during half a century. He was a founder and first editor of Family Process , the first journal in family therapy.

items.title: Joseph Hopkins papers, circa 1970-1990
items.description: Dr. Joseph R. Hopkins, MD, MMM, is Clinical Professor Emeritus at Stanford University's Department of Medicine, Division of Primary Care and Population Health.

items.title: Kenneth D. Brock journals, 1949-2018
items.description: Brock was hired in 1984 by the State of California, Department of Health Services, to work as a consultant with the Centers for Disease Control to establish a registry of AIDS cases in California. It was a quasi-legislative appointment by Senator David Roberti's office after he authored the first AIDS bill in 1983.

items.title: Mental Research Institute (MRI) records
items.description: The Mental Research Institute (MRI) was founded by Don Jackson in 1959 in Palo Alto, California. Originally a division on the Palo Alto Medical Research Foundation, in 1963 MRI became an independent, multi-disciplinary, non-profit corporation devoted to research and training.
items.era_note: Shown here on a reading of the collection, rather than on the dates above.

items.title: Roy B. Cohn papers, 1963-1982
items.description: Chiefly articles and correspondence related to work with Samuel Kountz in renal transplantation and the prevention and treatment of transplant rejection. Includes: The Immunological reaction in the vascular system of allogenic renal homotransplants: its early detection and treatment / Roy Cohn and Samuel Kountz.

items.title: Russel V. Lee family papers, circa 1895-2014, bulk 1940s-1970s.
items.description: Dr. Russel Van Arsdale Lee founded the Palo Alto Medical Clinic (PAMC), one of the first group practice clinics in the United States. He was a champion of rights for abortion, prepaid medical care and free drugs for addicts, and a leader in health education. His five sons all became doctors.

items.title: Russel V.A. Lee papers, 1935-1976
items.description: Chiefly correspondence together with supporting subject material, including pamphlets, minutes, and newsletters, related to work as Founder and Director of the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, 1924-61. Major subject groupings in health insurance, health care for the aging, community medical clinics and group medical practice.

items.title: S.O.S. Program Collection
items.description: Lecture recordings and transcripts from the S.O.S. Program, a pioneering divorce therapy group founded in Palo Alto, California in 1963 by Sally Spray (now Sally Moltzen).

items.title: Stanford Prevention Research Center, Five-City Project, videorecordings, 1980-1984
items.description: The Five City Project education campaign began in 1978 and ran for six years. Monterey and Salinas were chosen as education communities; Modesto, San Luis Obispo and Santa Maria were chosen as controls. The campaign was aimed at the entire population, including teenagers.

items.title: Thomas C. Merigan papers 1967-2016
items.description: Thomas C. Merigan is the George E. and Lucy Becker Professor of Medicine, Emeritus at the Stanford University. His practice at Stanford spanned 45 years and included many years as chair of the infectious disease division of the Department of Medicine.

items.title: William C. Dement papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: William C. Dement is Professor Emeritus in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford. He founded the Sleep Research Center at Stanford and co-founded the Sleep Research Society. He was also the founding President of the American Sleep Disorders Association (ASDA).

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Archive of Takeo Shikamura and Hatsu Shikamura
items.description: Collection of Takeo Shikamura’s papers and photo albums, Hatsu (Helen) Yamamoto's and her family’s papers, photos albums, journals.
items.era_note: Shown here on a reading of the collection, rather than on the dates above.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza photographs, 1900-1972
items.description: Includes photostatic pictures of Ernesto Galarza's mother, Henrietta Galarza, ca. 1900, sisters Nora and Henrietta and younger brother, ca. 1905, and pictures as an adult in 1959, 1965, and 1972.

items.title: Michael L. Belangie papers, 1945-1980
items.description: Born in Butte Montana, on June 29, 1907, Michael Louis Belangie was the eldest of three children. His father was of French-Canadian origin, and spent his working life as a miner. Personal and professional papers, some also pertaining to his wife, Mary.

items.title: Newcomer family papers, 1850-1972
items.description: A diary or record book of Sidney's life from birth to age 24, kept by his mother, together with other of her papers. Lecture notes that H. Sidney Newcomer kept reflecting pre-World War I mathematics and optics education at the University of Wisconsin. Patents, 1929-1972, awarded to H. Sidney Newcomer.

items.title: Richard W. and Elizabeth Lyman personal papers, 1940-2013
items.description: Elizabeth (Jing) Lyman (wife of Richard Lyman, seventh president of Stanford University) was active in community affairs, the Women's Resource Center, and other foundations. Richard W. Lyman, who served as Stanford's seventh president from 1970 to 1980.

sectors.name: Society and community — Philanthropy and foundations

items.title: Anne Firth Murray papers, 1970-2018
items.description: Anne Firth Murray, a New Zealander, was educated at the University of California and New York University in economics, political science, and public administration, with a focus on international health policy and women's reproductive health. Papers include Murray’s Global Fund for Women and Hewlett Foundation files.

items.title: David and Lucile Packard: A lifetime of Stanford philanthropy
items.description: Dave and Lucile Packard's philanthropic activities have had a major impact on Stanford University through grants provided through the the David and Lucile Packard Foundation.

items.title: System Development Foundation records, 1957-1993
items.description: The System Development Foundation (SDF) got its start in the 1950s as a not-for-profit corporation researching and developing computer software in the information sciences. Of most interest to researchers will be the research files and project reports.
items.era_note: Shown here on a reading of the collection, rather than on the dates above.

items.title: William Hewlett papers, 1907-2018 (bulk 1960-2001)
items.description: William Hewlett was the co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, one of the most successful technology start-up companies in the history of Silicon Valley. He and his business partner and longtime friend David Packard flipped a coin to determine the order of their names when starting their company.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: A3C Oral Histories
items.description: Bio note. Scope and Content Note (can be brief).

items.title: Emory M. Lee collection of Asian American papers, circa 1960-2008
items.description: Newspapers, newsletters, journals and periodicals pertaining to the Asian American experience. Includes postcards (both used and unused) depicting San Francisco's Chinatown. Emphasis is on the local San Francisco Bay Area, but also includes nationwide material.

items.title: Issei Oral History Project in Watsonville Collection
items.description: The Issei Oral History Project in Watsonville was created by historian Kazuko Nakane in preparation for the book Nothing Left in my Hands : The Issei of a Rural California Town, 1900-1942. Interviews were conducted by Nakane from 1978 to 1983 with fifteen Japanese-American residents in Watsonville, California.

items.title: Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area : ephemera from Eve Sutton, 1980-2004
items.description: Material was collected by Eve Sutton. Primarily material from Palo Alto and Stanford University, including Congregation Kol Emeth, Stanford Hillel, Resource magazine, and the Bureau of Jewish Education.

items.title: Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1981-2010
items.description: Material collected by Roger S. Kohn and Zachary M. Baker, both Stanford University Library curators, from local synagogues, individuals, organizations, and businesses. The collection documents non-traditional Jewish life in the Bay Area, especially newsletters and announcements from various organizations.

items.title: Ken and Caretha Coleman archive of Black histories in Silicon Valley, circa 2020s
items.description: Collection includes oral histories of Harry Bremond, Caretha Coleman, Al Cotton, Kathy Cotton, Peggy Forbes, Maynard Holliday, Pamela Isom, Max Pearl, Marc Ramsey. Additional material related to African Americans in Silicon Valley forthcoming.

items.title: Kenneth Kann papers and oral histories relating to the Petaluma (CA) Jewish chicken ranchers and egg farmers and the life of Joe Rapoport, circa 1970-1995
items.description: Kenneth Kann (1944-) was raised in the East European Jewish immigrant community of Chicago and attended the University of Wisconsin, Madison, during the 1960s. He completed a PhD in modern US history at the University of California, Berkeley in 1977.

items.title: Kistler family papers, circa 1940-2013
items.description: Olga Ritso-Kistler was born Olga Ritso in Ukraine in 1920, where her Estonian father was a medical student, during the Russian civil war. As Soviet power consolidated, the family's attempt to return with their two small children to Estonia via Moscow was complicated.

items.title: Paul Louie papers, circa 1820-2004
items.description: Paul Louie (1918-2009) was a Chinese American activist, historian, and minister in the Presbyterian Church, born and raised in Seattle, WA, who later moved to San Francisco. News clippings and complete newspapers, reports, photographs, books, slides, and other documents.

items.title: Donald Kennedy, President of Stanford University, papers

items.title: Gerhard Casper, President of Stanford University, papers
items.description: Gerhard Casper is President Emeritus of Stanford University and a Senior Fellow at both the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies (FSI Stanford) and the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR).

items.title: Jane Lathrop Stanford papers, 1860-1983
items.description: Jane Eliza Lathrop was born August 25, 1828, the daughter of Dyer Lathrop of Albany, New York. In 1850 she married Leland Stanford, returning with him to California in 1855 where they settled in Sacramento. Leland Stanford later became President of the Southern Pacific Railroad and Governor of California.

items.title: John L. Hennessy, President of Stanford University, records
items.description: Records from his term as President of Stanford University, along with the records of the Provost. Some of the records were generated by the previous administration of Gerhard Casper.

items.title: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson papers, 1941-1990
items.description: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Stanford in 1940 and returned after his wartime service in the Navy to earn his MBA in 1947. After seven years in the business world, he returned to Stanford in 1954 as assistant to university president J. E. Wallace Sterling.

items.title: Richard W. Lyman personal papers, 1778-2011
items.description: Lyman was born in Philadelphia in 1923 and raised in New Haven, Conn. His father, a chemist who lost his job during the recession that followed World War I, became an attorney. His mother taught French. His exposure to the world began with a summer visit to Belgium to visit his maternal grandmother.

items.title: Stanford University Press records, 1915-2013

items.title: Stanford University website collection
items.description: The materials consist of Stanford University websites captured by University Archives staff. Included are the websites of Stanford's seven schools, their departments, and many school-affiliated labs and research centers; independent research centers and institutes reporting to the Dean of Research.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: Powers and Duties —The Board of Trustees is custodian of the endowment and all properties of the University. The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University.

items.title: Stanford University, Faculty Senate, records, 1891-2026(inclusive)
items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. The Council holds one regularly scheduled meeting annually.

items.title: Stanford University, Government and Community Relations, records

items.description: The Office of Technology Licensing (OTL) stands as a cornerstone of Stanford University's operational framework, its inception dating back to 1970, aimed at overseeing and maximizing the university's intellectual property assets.

items.title: UCSF/Stanford Hospital Merger records

items.description: Jay Haley (1923-2007) was born in an oil town in Wyoming. He was a pioneer in family therapy, and his work traces its birth and development during half a century. He was a founder and first editor of Family Process , the first journal in family therapy.

items.description: Loren R. Mosher, clinician specializing in the treatment of schizophrenia without drugs, earned his undergraduate degree in biological sciences at Stanford University in 1956.

items.description: The Mental Research Institute (MRI) was founded by Don Jackson in 1959 in Palo Alto, California. Originally a division on the Palo Alto Medical Research Foundation, in 1963 MRI became an independent, multi-disciplinary, non-profit corporation devoted to research and training.
